News.title: Schools told to find time for children to read for pleasure
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Schools will be expected to set aside time in the day for pupils to read for pleasure, under Labour plans to overhaul the curriculum.

Primary schools will have to set aside time within the curriculum every day, and secondary schools will have the flexibility to make sure students have regular time to read throughout the week, the Department for Education (DfE) said.

Secondary schools will also be told to encourage pupils to read entire books, poems and other literature as part of plans due to be announced on Monday.

Children’s daily reading levels are too low amid the battle for attention with screens, the DfE said.

The government will also introduce a new statutory Year 8 reading check to help identify children who need extra help.

Education secretary Lucy Powell will set out the new curriculum next week, the first in more than a decade.

She said: “Across the world, we are seeing a ticking time bomb for our future generations, as reading and literacy levels are falling with too many children seeing reading as a chore or missing out altogether.

“We cannot afford to stand idly by and let this continue. Reading fluently is the gateway to lifelong learning, opening up every subject in school and creating opportunities throughout life.

“Reading is not just a skill that sets children up for success throughout their lives. It’s an experience to be enjoyed, and every child should have the opportunity to discover that.

“Through these reforms and the National Reading Movement, I’m determined to buck that trend, to make sure every child in this country can become confident, fluent readers, curious about the world, ready to keep learning throughout their lives.”

Author Michael Morpurgo said: “I am so thrilled that this initiative is happening, and would support it in any way that would help.

“I’ve been longing for storytime to be a regular part of every child’s life at school, and now it really might be.”

News.title: Investigators launch new appeal 45 years after toddler vanished on second birthday
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Investigators probing the disappearance of a toddler who vanished on her second birthday 45 years ago have urged anyone who has remained silent to finally come forward.

Katrice Lee disappeared on November 28 1981 while on a shopping trip with her family at a supermarket near the British Army base in Paderborn, Germany, where her father Richard Lee was serving.

Saturday marks her 47th birthday, but her family are still waiting for answers.

The Defence Serious Crime Command senior investigating officer said: “Katrice’s family deserve to know what happened to her.

“If you know something, but have convinced yourself it does not matter, it does.

“And if you have been waiting for the right moment to speak, that moment is now.

“Forty-five years should not mean the end of our search for answers.

open image in gallery Age progression photo first issued 30/04/13 by the Ministry of Defence, of Katrice Lee, as she may have look aged 38-years-old. ( PA )

“It should be the reason that someone finally finds the courage to come forward.”

In May 2024, Katrice’s father Mr Lee, a former warrant officer, tried to hand back his military medals at Downing Street in protest against what he labelled police failings in the investigation.

He said he was “not going away” until he received answers from the Ministry of Defence.

Mr Lee believes his daughter was abducted and has requested an independent or public inquiry into the handling of his daughter’s case.

Speaking in 2024, Mr Lee said: “I haven’t got answers yet.

“The MoD and the Royal Military Police know they’ve failed my daughter’s case since 1981.

“With what’s going on today, when everybody is aware of the blood contamination scandal, they’re aware of the Hillsborough disaster, it’s rather sad that all these institutions are more concerned about their reputation than just being open, honest and telling the truth.”

Natasha Walker, the older sister of Katrice Lee, previously said living without her sibling was “the hardest thing to do”.

Katrice was last seen wearing a blue duffle coat with a green fur hood, a green and blue pinafore dress, red wellies and a white blouse with a blue collar and cuffs.

Anyone with information can contact the Defence Serious Crime Command on 0800 616 818 or contact Crimestoppers anonymously via 0800 555 111.

News.title: Thousands of children to be offered flu jabs at pharmacies for the first time
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Thousands of children who missed their school flu vaccine can now receive a jab at a local pharmacy for the first time.

NHS England is urging parents to ensure their children are protected as cases rise nationwide.

More than 6,000 high street pharmacies across England are offering appointments, with bookings opening Monday via the NHS app or NHS Find a Pharmacy webpage, and appointments available from Tuesday.

Pharmacies are also offering nasal spray flu vaccines for children aged two and three.

Children can fall severely ill with flu and easily spread it to more vulnerable groups, including the elderly.

The rollout comes as hospital admissions for flu run at their highest level for this time of year since before the pandemic.

Flu admission rates in England reached 9.0 per 100,000 last week, up from 5.0 per 100,000 seven days earlier, according to the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

open image in gallery More than 3.5 million children from Reception to Year 11 have already had their flu vaccine ( Getty Images )

Admissions stood at 4.9 per 100,000 in the equivalent week in 2025.

NHS national medical director Professor Frankie Swords said: “The run-up to Christmas can be such a busy time for parents, so it’s great news that for the first time, it’s now really easy to book your child’s flu vaccine at your local high street pharmacy if they missed it in school.

“Winter viruses like flu are on the rise again, which puts real pressure on the NHS and could also ruin your family’s plans for Christmas.

“This offer is another way to protect children, families and communities, so if you need an appointment for your child, please book now.”

More than 3.5 million children from Reception to Year 11 have already had their flu vaccine.

Dr Suzanna McDonald, flu vaccination programme lead at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), said: “Vaccinating school children against flu not only helps protect them, but crucially helps protect younger siblings and other more vulnerable family members at greater risk, like grandparents.

“Ensuring all children from aged two receive a flu vaccine every winter is so important to help prevent the thousands of unnecessary hospitalisations we see among unvaccinated children.

“Please don’t dismiss the importance of a flu vaccine for your children. It will help keep them out of hospital and even save lives.

“Don’t put your child needlessly at risk, book that appointment with your GP surgery or at some community pharmacies offering the vaccine.”

open image in gallery Flu admission rates in England reached 9.0 per 100,000 last week, up from 5.0 per 100,000 seven days earlier, according to the UK Health Security Agency ( PA )

Outgoing health chief Sir Jim Mackey warned the NHS should prepare for a “horrible spike in flu”, as he said some hospitals have introduced mask wearing to stem the spread of respiratory illnesses.

Dr McDonald, said experts expect the flu jab to work well against the strain of virus currently in circulation even though it has mutated slightly.

Dr McDonald told BBC Radio 4’s Today programme on Friday: “Hospital admission rates have increased 80% in the latest data that we’ve published this week compared to last week, and that is a very sharp rise.

“What we’re seeing is that sharp rise is coming in a few weeks earlier than we saw this time last season, but last season was the earliest season that we’d seen for over 20 years.

“This is very early to be seeing such high demand in hospitals.”

Dr Matt Swallow, clinical lead at Asthma + Lung UK, said: “Flu can be particularly dangerous for young children, especially for the 1.2 million children living with asthma…

“It’s great news that pharmacies are offering another opportunity to ensure more children are protected.”

Henry Gregg, chief executive of the National Pharmacy Association, said: “Pharmacies have been working hard to vaccinate millions of patients in recent weeks but it is clear more can be done by the Government and other agencies to promote this service to those who are eligible.

“If you are a parent who has not yet got your child vaccinated, please come forward for vaccination at your local pharmacy, based conveniently on your doorstep.”

News.title: Black Friday 2026 live: Expert analysis on which deals to shop (and which to avoid)
News.content:
So far this year, the Telegraph Recommended team has only deemed 34 per cent of the deals we’ve checked worthwhile of inclusion in our coverage. For us to count something as a deal, it has to be more than 10 per cent off its average price over the last six months.

We’re doing our best to provide you with as many genuine discounts to shop as possible, but if you’ve got an eye on something we’ve not mentioned anywhere, you might want to do some checks yourself.

Here are our top tips for checking a Black Friday deal:

1. Don’t over-fixate on Black Friday itself

While interest in Black Friday deals will peak around the day itself, some of the best deals may have been available since the beginning of the week, or earlier. And lots of deals are still available for a week or so afterwards.

2. Use a price tracker

Sites like Price Runner, Keepa and CamelCamelCamel track the price history of a product over months – often years – which can help you see if the product has been lower than the sale price being advertised.

3. Expand your search to everyday essentials

Last year’s Cyber Weekend saw a 260 per cent spike in sales of “personal care” items including cosmetics, shampoos, fragrances and toothbrushes, according to Adobe. It’s a good time to stock up.

4. Research the product before you buy

In a recent survey of over 800 Telegraph readers, 70 per cent of you told us that quality and durability of products is your main priority during sales periods rather than finding the lowest-priced item in a category. Make sure you’re reading reviews and buying a good product.

5. Avoid overspending

Impulse-buying items that you don’t need means you’ll have less budget to spend on the best deals and most important purchases. Whether that means avoiding credit cards or shopping on your laptop instead of your smartphone, you know your own habits the best.

News.title: Alonso crisis deepens as chaotic Chelsea lose and fans taunt own player
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea.

The City Ground hosts the Premier League clash tonight, with two sides who are both falling short of expectations.

Forest head coach Oliver Glasner brought with him a sense of optimism after he left Crystal Palace, but the club are just outside the bottom three, sitting in 17th position with only nine points. As things stand, they are only clear of 18th-placed Sunderland because of superior goal difference.

Beneath them, Glasner’s former club Palace are bottom, two points away from them, and then Manchester United come in 19th, a single point behind. With Thomas Frank and Mauricio Pochettino now installed at Selhurst Park and Old Trafford, respectively, the pressure could soon be felt yet more keenly.

There have been flashes of encouragement, with a 3-1 win over Manchester City in early November, spearheaded by a brace from Liam Delap, who left Chelsea in the summer. However, last Saturday they lost 2-0 at Bournemouth to dent any nascent momentum, and the match was the sixth in 11 league games where the club have failed to score. Forest have scored nine times this season, with only Sunderland having a worse record in attack.

Chelsea’s Xabi Alonso has also endured a tough time of late. They were trounced 4-1 against Leeds United at home on Saturday, despite taking the lead in the first half.

That worrying collapse was the fourth loss in five league matches, and it followed a 1-0 defeat against Sunderland at the Stadium of Light before the recent international break.

There is speculation that Chelsea will move for a central defender in January, with 20 goals conceded in the Premier League so far.

Chelsea are currently in eighth place in the league with 16 points, five points behind Liverpool in fourth. Tonight, they could leapfrog Bournemouth, who are in fifth, two points ahead of them. Another loss, though, could see them in the bottom half once the weekend’s fixtures are completed.

News.title: Ireland beat Australia in front of 50,000 empty seats
News.content:
Farrell said he had not had time to fully digest what he made of the format, but he admitted the Friday double-header was a difficult sell, particularly at just five days’ notice, or the decision to stage every game at the same venue.

“Off the top of my head I don’t know whether the Friday night thing works, or the same venue [for every game],” he said. “Obviously they look like little things but they’re not to fans, when you don’t know when to book your flights or hotels.

“I loved the razzmatazz. Coming into the ground, it felt different. It felt like an event, a concert. It was just a shame we couldn’t get the people through the door.

“The 4.40pm kick off earlier… I felt for those boys,” Farrell added of the Fiji-Italy game earlier in the day, which was played out to even fewer fans. “But it’s not our job to make sense of it. Our job is to play rugby.”

Ireland did not do much of that initially, albeit it was always going to be difficult to top their statement win over South Africa last weekend.

They got off to a terrible start, coughing up four penalties in the first 10 minutes alone, two of them from their usually dominant scrum.

Australia responded with some truly awful kicking. First Carter Gordon turned down the chance to go for goal, opting instead to kick for the corner only to miss it by miles. Then they sliced another ball out on the full from centre field.

The Wallabies played much the better rugby in the first 20 minutes, though, with scrum-half Kalani Thomas particularly lively around the fringes on his first start.

After Carlo Tizzano broke clear from Brandon Paenga-Amosa’s offload, the Wallabies ought to have scored in the corner, only for Tom Wright to fumble.

Williams finally notched the first points of the evening, a close-range try after Ireland coughed up yet another penalty on their own five-metre line. But as Wallabies head coach Les Kiss admitted later, they should have scored more with nearly 80 per cent possession up to that point.

The try stung Ireland into action and they hit back immediately with Stuart McCloskey spinning out of a tackle and putting Henshaw over. Timoney added a second after Kurtley Beale came off the bench for his first international appearance for five years at the age of 37, and promptly missed a tackle on the short side. Prendergast added a penalty on the stroke of half-time as Ireland went into the break 17-7 up, having been 7-0 down.

News.title: Italy edge out Fiji in Nations Championship at sparse Twickenham
News.content:
Italy clung on against Fiji to put the first point on the board for the northern hemisphere in Nations Championship finals weekend, although their entertaining 23-21 victory was played out to a quarter-full Allianz Stadium.

Perhaps that was no surprise given the timing of the kick-off: 4.40pm on a Friday.

But with only 32,000 tickets sold for Friday’s double-header – Ireland vs Australia takes place later in the evening – the sparse nature of the crowd has raised questions about the new format.

It was a shame there were so few fans packed in for this game, because it was a fun match to watch, as Fiji’s games often are.

Gonzalo Quesada’s Italy had lost to the same opposition 16-21 in Rome last weekend, and they entered this game the only team from either hemisphere not to have won a single Nations Championship match. But their 17-7 half-time lead thanks to tries from Federico Mori and Giacomo Nicotera was no more than they deserved. Fiji only made one entry into Italy’s 22m in the first half, although it did yield a try from Sale’s 6ft5in Ponepati Loganimasi, who was allowed to race home from the halfway line.

Fiji scored their second try from their second entry into Italy’s 22m, and it was another beauty, Jiuta Wainiqolo sucking in two defenders before offloading to Peniasi Dakuwaqa, who stepped inside Stephen Varney to score.

Fiji’s third was the best of the lot, 13 phases of wonderful offloading rugby before a Dakuwaqa grubber kick released Wainiqolo., who in turn managed to offload to Sawala to score.

That nudged Fiji 21-20 in front. But a late Tommaso Allan penalty put Italy back ahead, as Fiji opted to kick for the corner with a minute remaining rather than go for the posts.

Italy held on, Andrea Bocelli blasting out over the public address at full-time in front of 60,000 empty seats. First blood to the northern hemisphere.

News.title: Vaccine gaps fuelling global measles resurgence, WHO warns
News.content:
Measles is one of the most contagious viruses known to humans and requires 95 per cent of the community to be vaccinated to prevent outbreaks. Children under-five, pregnant women and people with weakened immune systems are at greatest risk.

According to the WHO, it can cause pneumonia, brain infection, deafness and blindness, death and “immune amnesia”, where the virus can weaken the immune system for months or even years.

The measles vaccine, which used a weakened (live attenuated) virus in two doses, is safe and highly effective.

Dr O’Brien said: “Some of the more recent graduates have never seen a case of measles, but it is back”.

Diana Chang Blanc, unit head of the essential programme on immunisation at the WHO, said the spread of cases across income levels showed that even in places with strong health systems, small drops in coverage can leave pockets of unvaccinated people that can spread risks far beyond those areas.

In 2025, 59 countries had “large or disruptive outbreaks”, defined as more than 20 cases per million people over 12 months. Of them, 11 were previously declared measles-free. The US was not among them, as its outbreaks didn’t reach the threshold.

“It can take years to regain elimination status, whereas it takes only a 12-month period to lose elimination status,” said Dr O’Brien. “These are hard-fought gains that countries have made, and protecting them now is more important than ever”.

News.title: Australia embarrassed by remarkable Overton spell
News.content:
So often English cricketers have left the “Gabbatoir” looking dazed and confused after yet another horror show. This time, it was an insipid Australian side’s turn to be embarrassed and overawed by a remarkable showing from Jamie Overton. It was a batting display as ugly as anything Australian cricket has served up in the sandpaper civil war, which rumbles on.

As Australia were bowled for a meagre 108, Overton recorded figures of five for 12, the second-best in T20 by an Englishman and the best by any man in T20 fixtures between these old rivals. That was Australia’s lowest T20 total against England since the sides’ first meeting, ahead of the 2005 Ashes, when they were bundled out for 79 chasing 180. Back then, T20 was a bit of fun, now it is big business, and this was altogether more chastening.

A combination of rain, which delayed play three times and led to a DLS-reduced target, and Riley Meredith, who was gifted three wickets, meant that England’s batting lacked the freewheeling fun of their bowling performance.

But the chase was a formality, and England won by seven wickets. The Gabba was just a third full, with some hardy Barmy Army types in fine voice as England celebrated their win. With England leading the five-match series 2-1, it is hard to imagine too many Aussies racing to buy tickets for the final two games in Sydney and Canberra. England are flying out Rehan Ahmed and the uncapped Glamorgan batsman Asa Tribe as they manage a long list of absentees, which will include the South Africa-bound captain Harry Brook and keeper Jordan Cox by Canberra.

News.title: Colombia earthquake triggers surge in malaria cases
News.content:
Cases of malaria in rural Colombia have surged after a devastating earthquake left towns and villages in ruins, according to local charities.

Colombia has recorded over 74,360 cases of malaria this year, 40 per cent of which have been concentrated in Chocó – the epicentre of the earthquake which struck in August, killing at least 335 people and injuring 4,500 more.

The region has seen a 46 per cent surge in cases of the mosquito-borne disease compared to last year, up from 23,757 cases in 2025 to 34,759 cases so far in 2026.

Malaria can be very serious at any age, but it is the most dangerous for young children under five. If left untreated, it can become a medical emergency in as little as 24 hours and result in death.

While Africa accounts for around 94 per cent of global malaria cases, an estimated half a million infections occur in South America every year, mostly in the countries surrounding the Amazon basin – Colombia, Brazil, and Venezuela.

The earthquake hit at 7.4 on the Richter scale and was the strongest Colombia has seen in a decade, destroying roads and buildings. It hit during the rainy season, and water has collected in and around destroyed buildings, allowing mosquitoes, which breed in stagnant water, to survive and multiply, according to Save the Children.

Following the earthquake, thousands of people in Chocó have moved into overcrowded and unsanitary shelters after their homes were destroyed, increasing the spread of infectious diseases including malaria – which is carried between people via infected mosquitoes.

“The earthquake has worsened the conditions that favour the transmission of malaria,” Maria Mercedes Liévano, Save the Children’s Country Director in Colombia, told The Telegraph.

“Because we’re now seeing collapsed and damaged homes, families that are sleeping in overcrowded conditions out in the open, and are dealing with a health network that is overwhelmed,” Ms Liévano added.

News.title: Milk of human kindness: Brazil exports its donor breastfeeding programme worldwide
News.content:
When baby Luis Miguel was born in Guarapuava, Brazil, in February, he was unresponsive.

He had inhaled meconium, a newborn’s first stool, during delivery. It then entered his lungs and blocked his airways. Doctors at Hospital de Caridade São Vicente de Paulo resuscitated and intubated the baby boy, saving his life. He spent the next three weeks in the hospital’s neonatal unit.

His mother, 25-year-old sales assistant Luany Thainara Machado, could not produce enough breast milk and so hers was supplemented with that of a woman she had never met.

“While it might not make much sense for a mother to do this under normal circumstances it becomes very important when the need arises,” she said.

Nine months later, Luis Miguel is healthy and Machado is grateful that donor milk was able to support her son when he needed it most; so much so that today she donates 2.5 litres of her now plentiful supply every week. “Being able to help other mothers and other babies today, it feels really good,” she told The Telegraph, bouncing Luis Miguel on her knee as she spoke.

Sports.title: Furious Eckert not impressed with Southampton mocking as Middlesbrough boss confronts Azaz in fiery Spygate clash
Sports.content:
Next

TONDA ECKERT angrily cleared away a box of tissues left on the press conference table to goad Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg after Southampton’s 2-0 victory.

The stunned Saints manager brushed the tissues aside and spoke about needing to act with “class” when quizzed about them after Finn Azaz mocked away fans with a crying gesture following his 79th-minute sealer.



It later emerged that Hellberg confronted Azaz, telling him to “do better”, with the Middlesbrough boss also accusing the South Coast club of acting “small” with all the touches.

Ahead of kick-off, Southampton media chiefs had posted a pre-match video revisiting Saints’ play-off semi-final win over Boro and the Spygate fallout — before blasting Oasis song Stop Crying Your Heart Out afterwards.



Eckert was not aware of the tissues sitting on the press conference table and when they were pointed out he stared at them for around 15 seconds in silence before later throwing them on the floor.

Eckert said: “I hope that everyone who came here again today from the Middlesbrough staff knows that these things don’t come from me.

“I think that everything you do in defeat, and everything you do [with] class, I try to do that.

“I don’t know if I’m always able to do it, but I hope that there’s an appreciation that this doesn’t come from me.

“I didn’t like the video this morning. No, I didn’t like it.

“I think if we look back a couple of months, the reality is that both clubs have lost. One club lost off the pitch, the other on the pitch.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“It’s an episode that is good to close for both clubs and to move forward. For me, that episode from last year is closed.

“I’ve apologised to Kim, I’ve apologised openly, for me there’s no need to warm that up again. I think that everything you do in defeat, and everything you do [with] class, I try to do that.

“I’m not even sure if I know about all of the stories that come out from outside of the football pitch.

“I heard about some of them from the side, I haven’t even seen what has been put out, I just heard about it and I didn’t like it.”

Eckert also promised to speak to former Boro midfielder Azaz after his tear-wiping celebration sparked a late melee that saw ten players and two staff booked.



Eckert said: “I will have a conversation with him. I hope this one doesn’t become a big topic.

“It’s been one of the best games that the Championship has to offer this year, because it was two very good teams facing each other.

“I hope that these games are lived and remembered by the football, and not so much by what happens around.”



Speaking after the game, Hellberg said: “Hellberg said: “I saw there were some posts now at the end where they tried to mock me or whoever they were trying to mock. So I feel a bit small about that.

“There’s a very good football side. There’s so many good players. Their staff is good, so there’s no need for that.

“With Finn Azaz, I told him that I think you have to do better. You cannot do like that. I think that was a key thing to tell him.

“I know it’s a lot of emotions and sometimes emotion can get the better of you. But that’s what I told him too — that you have to do better on that occasion.”

Asked about the tissues removed by Eckert and the pre-match Spygate video, Hellberg added: “I think they had a chance to be a little bit bigger persons and then you have to judge if they were or not.



“I’m not afraid of showing feelings. I think in general if the world could show more emotions and stand up for what is right, I think that’s brave people.

“I’m not the one to hold grudges. I will tell people that I think they’re doing wrong and then I will try to be a good human being.

“They’ve always tried to fire everything up and I think it’s tough trying to keep the class in those moments.

“We were the better team for 60 minutes and we should have scored in those moments, so it’s sad we didn’t get anything today.”

The bad blood dates back to May, when intern analyst Will Salt was caught watching Boro’s training session ahead of the Championship play-off final against Hull.



EFL chiefs expelled Saints from the showpiece and docked them four points this campaign — although Eckert escaped with a fine and suspended ban.

Saints’ graphic designer clearly showed off a sense of humour, plastering “ALL EYES ON US” across the programme cover alongside four pairs of peering eyes.

Even the sponsors’ positioning could not have been scripted better — with covert-sounding bookie Midnite sitting right next to GPS-tracking giants Garmin.



Hampshire Police issued a 48-hour dispersal order across Southampton city centre and deployed extra patrols outside St Mary’s to keep rival fans apart.

The rain streamed down, yet it failed to dampen an electric atmosphere cranked up further by a pre-match light and pyrotechnic show.

Home fans wasted no time goading their visitors, singing “We’re Southampton, we’ll spy when we want” while several waved binoculars towards the away end.

Boro supporters hit back with chants of “You know what you are, you cheating b******s, you know what you are.”

Saints fans responded with sarcastic cheers before launching into “You’re going to cry in a minute” and “We saw you cry on the telly”.



They then twisted the knife with a deafening chorus of “Oh, Oli McBurnie” — reminding Boro of their 1-0 Wembley defeat to Hull via McBurnie’s 95th-minute winner.

On the pitch, Lewis Dobbin headed an early James Ward-Prowse corner over before Daniel Peretz denied Will Lankshear one-on-one.

Azaz rattled the bar from 20 yards against his old club, while Boro keeper Radek Vitek tipped Cyle Larin’s fierce header over.

After the break, Keven Schlotterbeck made a wonderful last-ditch tackle to deny Lankshear as he raced through on goal.

Saints struck in the 59th minute when Kuryu Matsuki’s cross found James Bree, who teed up Ryan Manning to fire home from 12 yards.



Azaz then pounced on Aidan Morris’s 79th-minute error to slot in the second before sprinting straight towards the away end with his crying gesture.

Chaos erupted on the touchline as players clashed in angry skirmishes, capping a night of pure needle at St Mary’s.

And Eckert revealed he has still invited Hellberg for a post-match drink, adding: “He was more than invited — it will be up to him.”

Sports.title: Fofana endures Chelsea DISASTER after shock interview as he’s hooked and fans chant ‘f*** off’ after penalty gaffe
Sports.content:

WESLEY FOFANA was booed and jeered by his own fans as he endured a night to forget just days after embarrassing himself in an interview.

Xabi Alonso has now called on Chelsea supporters to “support” the defender after he gave away a penalty and was dragged off in a disastrous 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest.



The French defender has had a nightmare start to the season at Stamford Bridge and was blasted after a recent unauthorised interview in which he made light of a penalty miss at Anfield.

Fofana has since apologised for the comments but fans were clearly not ready to forgive him at the City Ground.



Travelling Chelsea fans made their feelings immediately known as the 25-year-old was booed and jeered every time he touched the ball.

He was also the target of multiple expletive-laden chants, with some fans singing: “F*** off Fofana, you’re not welcome here.”

Others preferred the version: “F*** off Fofana, you will always be s***.”

It immediately went from bad to worse for Fofana, Xabi Alonso and those in the away end when Forest forward Igor Jesus shinned in a volley in the fifth minute to give the hosts an early lead.

Things got even more ugly after half-time, with the Frenchman allowing a routine long ball to bounce over his head and into the path of former team-mate Liam Delap.

Fofana raced back to try and stop the striker but his clumsy challenge saw Delap bundled over, handing the hosts a spot kick and a chance to double their advantage.

Morgan Gibbs-White made no mistake and Fofana was hooked off by Alonso almost immediately.

As he made his way off, replaced by Levi Colwill, chants of “w***er, w***er, w***er” could be heard from the away end.

Alonso confirmed he did not speak to Fofana in the dressing room after the game, but did make it clear that the player needs support.

He said: “We need to support everyone because we need everyone. We need the fans, we need all the players, we need to stick together because if not things will get more complicated.

“We have to stick together. Everyone that is in the changing room, everyone in the team is needed.



“We need to help and we need to go through this together. We don’t leave apart anyone.”

Asked if it would now be difficult to start Fofana again after the fan reaction, Alonso added: “I’m thinking right after the game and for the next games, we will see.”

Chelsea have now lost three straight Premier League games, having been undone by Sunderland and Leeds before heading to Forest.



Alonso, who has now lost as many Premier League games as predecessor Liam Rosenior in one fewer game, said: “We are working, trying to find solutions, trying to do our best, but things are not going the way we want.

“I don’t understand any other way football than to try to work, to try again. Even when things are not going right because if we want to get something, it will have to come from us.

“No one will come from outside to give us the solution and the work that we need, the quality that we need, the mentality that we need. It needs to come within the team.”

Fofana rubbed fans the wrong way earlier this week after claiming he laughed off his costly penalty miss against Liverpool in their Carabao Cup defeat last month.

He said: “If I miss it’s not serious, it’s definitely annoying, but if someone attacks me, it’s not the first time, I don’t care.



“I know there’s another match in three days. If you win, you forget about your penalty. It’s how football works. I missed. I had a beautiful shot, did you see it? I was shooting very high. The roof of Anfield.

“I remember a supporter very high up caught the ball. Yeah, I missed, now I laugh about it because it’s part of football. That’s how it is.”

Frustrations over his penalty comments only exacerbated tensions surrounding his poor run of form this season – and that of the club itself.



The Blues flew out of the blocks under Alonso but have since stalled in their quest to compete at the top of the Premier League table.

After going 2-0 down super sub Emmanuel Emegha offered the Blues a small ray of light with a neat finish. But Gibbs-White added a second to restore his side’s cushion.

And though Emegha headed home again to give his team a chance at a late rescue, it wasn’t to be as the hosts left 3-2 winners.

Jamie Redknapp felt bad for the star, and claimed Alonso made a mistake even starting him after his turbulent recent weeks on and off the pitch.

The Sky Sports pundit said: “We are seeing this unfortunately from Wesley time after time.



“I’m sure he feels absolutely rotten, and football is a cruel place when you’re making mistakes like that.

“But when I saw the teams, it didn’t feel like the game for him, he had a bad week with the podcast. I think the manager has got that one wrong.

“By playing Fofana you end up creating that. It was inevitable, he is lacking so much confidence. He is having a really difficult run of it at the moment.”

Sports.title: Frank Lampard reveals he was ‘within an inch’ of joining Leeds before £11m Chelsea move changed football history
Sports.content:

FRANK LAMPARD admits he was ‘an inch’ away from signing for Leeds United 25 years ago.

The Coventry boss expects a hostile reception from home fans when he takes his side to Elland Road on Saturday.



But it could have been so different as there was a time when he might have become a Leeds legend when David O’Leary had taken them into the Champions League.

Lampard was hot property at West Ham — and a wanted man around the turn of the century. He had already seen pal Rio Ferdinand leave Upton Park in 2000 and join Leeds for £18million.



And midfielder Lamps was set to follow a few months later — until Chelsea offered him the chance to stay in London.

Instead he moved to Stamford Bridge in an £11m deal when Claudio Ranieri was in charge — and went on to etch his name into the Blues’ history.



But on his second anniversary as Coventry boss, Lampard knows there will be anything but a warm welcome for him in West Yorkshire.

In recent years, that has come from the ‘Spygate’ controversy in 2019 when Leeds boss Marcelo Bielsa admitted snooping on the Derby training ground when Lampard was Rams manager.

The incident even sparked a fans’ chant of ‘Stop Crying Frank Lampard’ after his accusations that the practice was ‘unethical’.

But now Lampard sees signs of Leeds boss Daniel Farke taking the Whites back to that level — especially after they beat Chelsea 4-1 away last weekend.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Asked why he did not sign for Leeds, the Sky Blues boss said: “Because it was Chelsea! I was within an inch of signing for Leeds at that point.

“There were different factors involved, and no disrespect to Leeds as they were a really good team then, they were quite exciting.

“But I was a London boy and it felt right when I sat with Claudio.

“I felt that I made the right decision in the end. But back then, there was a real feeling, momentum and personality that Leeds had. And the team they have now is creating its own personality and story.

“They are in a really good position, watching them play. It’s an impressive model. They’ve been up, down, back up and they’ve been able to build.



“It’s a good standard for us to look at. It doesn’t always work right away when you come up, but they’re a strong unit.”

Despite Lampard’s respect for Farke’s squad, he knows what to expect from Leeds supporters.

Asked if there is no love lost between manager and fans, Lampard said: “That’s safe to say! Chelsea and Leeds have a very strong rivalry — that’s always there for me as a Chelsea man.



“And at Derby, it was quite public. It’s all history for me. It’s the fans’ prerogative to be passionate and it’s mine to be passionate in my own way.

“They have a strong fanbase. But it’s a difficult stadium to go to because of that and especially now as the way they are playing is great.”

But although Lampard took Coventry to the Premier League last season — the semi-final play-off game at Elland Road remains one of the highlights of his managerial career.

Derby were 1-0 down from the first leg — and went behind in the second — but stormed back to reach Wembley with a stunning 4-2 win.

Mason Mount and Harry Wilson were among the goalscorers and Lampard was captured afterwards singing ‘Stop Crying’ with his celebrating players.



The Sky Blues boss agrees it was a standout moment, adding: “It didn’t win us promotion, we were always aware we had Aston Villa in the final.

“But Leeds were way ahead of us throughout that season. Bielsa had done great work and beaten us quite comfortably in both league games.

“Everybody expected us to lose in the second leg. I wasn’t sure we’d win.

Raya missed the 1-1 draw with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday night, but his absence from a huge Prem test would almost be uncharted territory.

Since making his Arsenal debut in September 2023, Raya has missed just THREE top-flight matches.

MIKEL ARTETA says Arsenal are ready to splash the cash – if they can find a player that will “make a difference for the team”.

The Gunners are in the market for a new forward during the January transfer window after failing to sign one in the summer.



Arsenal were keen on Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior, but were unable to pull off a deal for either player.

The Premier League champions are now interested in Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi and RB Leipzig winger Antonio Nusa.



Arteta said: “We’ve always been very active in the transfer window, especially when we have certain issues.

“Have we managed to get a deal over the line? Sometimes not, so we will see if there is an opportunity there and something that we believe is going to make a difference for the team.”

The Arsenal boss will have the chance to push his case for a new attacker over the coming weeks. Gunners co-chair Josh Kroenke is due to be in London as the club have a string of big games.

They take on Manchester City this Sunday, before travelling to Tottenham the following week and Real Madrid three days later.

Arteta said: “We don’t wait to talk about these things only when it is face to face. That is why we have great phones now.

FINN AZAZ sealed Southampton’s sweet Spygate revenge — and ran up to his former Middlesbrough fans to run their faces in it.

The Saints ace — signed from Boro last summer — cashed in on some awful defending to fire home with 10 minutes left after Ryan Manning had put them into a 59th-minute lead.



Having received dog’s abuse from the travelling fans all evening, he raced over to celebrate in front of them.

It sparked a mass melee between both sets of players.



Azaz said after the game: “They sang about my family, home and away last season so I was just waiting for my moment to get one back.”

Asked if he had any regrets, he added: “None whatsoever.”

This was the first meeting since last season’s play-off spying scandal saw Saints booted out of the Wembley final, Manning drilled home James Bree’s pass to spark stadium bedlam.

The bad blood dates back to May when Southampton’s intern analyst Will Salt was caught watching Boro’s training session ahead of their Championship semi-final play-off final with Boro.

EFL chiefs expelled Saints from the showpiece and docked them four points for this campaign — although boss Tonda Eckert escaped with a fine and suspended ban.

Saints’ graphic designer clearly used last night’s occasion to show off a sense of humour.

Plastered across the matchday programme cover were the words “ALL EYES ON US” alongside four pairs of eyes peering like secret agents.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Even the sponsors’ positioning on the front could not have been scripted better — with covert-sounding Midnite sitting right next to GPS-tracking giants Garmin.

Eckert passed up the chance to apologise to Boro fans in his programme notes — instead reflecting on the new three-year contract he signed with the club.

Hampshire Police were taking no chances with this fixture, issuing a 48-hour dispersal order across Southampton city centre from midday yesterday through to tomorrow lunchtime.

Extra patrols were also deployed outside St Mary’s to keep rival supporters apart.

The rain was streaming down, yet it did little to dampen an electric atmosphere cranked up further by a pre-match light and pyrotechnic show.



Home fans wasted no time goading their visitors, singing “We’re Southampton, we spy when we want” while several waved binoculars towards the away end.

Boro supporters hit back with chants of “You know what you are, you cheating b***ards, you know what you are.”

Saints fans responded with sarcastic cheers before launching into “You’re going to cry in a minute” and “We saw you cry on the telly.”

They then twisted the knife further with a deafening chorus of “Oh Oli McBurnie” — a brutal reminder of Boro’s Wembley agony.

Having taken Saints’ place under the arch, Boro lost 1-0 to Hull City via McBurnie’s 95th-minute winner.



Eckert had urged his players to embrace the hostile atmosphere — and both sides served up a breathless, end-to-end opening 45 minutes.

Saints should have been in front early on when a James Ward-Prowse corner was headed over unmarked by Lewis Dobbin.

Boro were denied when Will Lankshear timed his run to perfection after Dobbin lost possession, only for his one-on-one shot to be kept out by Daniel Peretz.



Azaz charged forward against his former club and thumped a 20-yarder that rattled back off the bar.

Keven Schlotterbeck then surged forward from deep but dragged his effort from the edge of the box wide.

Lankshear will have been disappointed after scuffing a shot straight at Peretz following a superb pass into the box from Sebastian Berhalter.

Boro keeper Radek Vitek then produced a wonderful fingertip stop to deflect a fierce Cyle Larin header over the bar.

After the break, Aidan Morris fired over after the ball fell into his path at the edge of the box.



Schlotterbeck made a wonderful last-ditch tackle to deny Lankshear as he raced through and was about to pull the trigger.

And Saints moved into the lead in the 59th minute — a goal that ultimately proved enough to settle a feisty contest.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Kuryu Matsuki crossed from the left and the ball fell to Bree, who played it into the path of Manning to fire home from 12 yards.

Boro pushed desperately for a leveller in the closing stages, yet Saints stood firm to claim all three points on a night that lived up to every bit of its billing.

Sports.title: Nottingham Forest 3 Chelsea 2: Alonso clinging on to his job as baffling XI and Fofana horror show blow up in his face
Sports.content:
Next

CHELSEA have become the Premier League’s pushovers.

Bullied by Sunderland and Leeds, Xabi Alonso’s sorry side were beaten black and blue at Nottingham Forest – and a lot of the problems were of their manager’s own making.



Alonso picked a baffling team, stuck with an unpopular and out of form Wesley Fofana and watched his odd masterplan blow up in his face.

Chelsea are afraid of the big boys at the moment, having been steamrolled by Brian Brobbey and Dominic Calvert-Lewin in recent weeks.



So Oliver Glasner started Igor Jesus and Liam Delap together, and they caused havoc. Jesus bagged an early belter and Delap won a penalty from which Morgan Gibbs-White scored his first of two.

Emmanuel Emegha offered another silver lining for Chelsea, but while he may feel a bit chipper after scoring twice, there is nothing but doom and gloom around him.



In a bid to end their defensive dross of recent weeks, Alonso shuffled his back four around – but instead of dropping the defender who embarrassed himself in a YouTube interview this week, it was Levi Colwill watching from the bench.

Fofana, who laughed off one of his many poor performances in that interview, bizarrely started in the heart of the defence alongside midfielder Moises Caicedo and was booed by his own fans throughout.

It says a lot about their situation that those in the away end headed north expecting the worst. Their fears were confirmed almost from the off.

Even inside the first minute the Blues gave up possession in their own half and allowed their old teammate Delap to fire on Emiliano Martinez’s goal.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Four minutes later, his partner struck.

Alonso had warned his players on Friday there was no excuse not to get the basics right after the debacle against Leeds.

It would be fair to assume that marking the opponent’s striker in the box would fall into the category of basics, but they still failed at that and Jesus punished them with a beauty.

Daniel Munoz found space down the right and lifted a cross towards the Brazilian, who was being loosely attended to by Josh Acheampong.



Given the space, Jesus went for the theatrical, volleying from almost behind himself into the far corner – that it came off his shin only added to Chelsea’s embarrassment.

Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis, attending just his second game of the season, crossed himself in the stands. Whether he was praying to Christ or his striker, it worked.

The hosts were hardly full of endeavour after their goal, but they were also not up against much.

Chelsea have been prone to collapsing after setbacks, Alonso calling them fragile less than a week ago. While they did not immediately fall to pieces, there was little in terms of a response, the Blues hardly leaving their half.



No one in white looked interested in turning the tide. Morgan Rogers made a run or two, Cole Palmer played a couple of passes but beyond that there was nowhere near enough energy, intensity or even interest.

Having dropped him despite scoring against Leeds, Alonso sent on Emmanuel Emegha to try and fix things at the break.

Within minutes, Fofana had thrown them further into chaos – defending in the manner of a recovery lobotomy patient.

After misreading a long ball and allowing ex-Chelsea man Delap to race in behind, the Frenchman clattered into the back of his old teammate and handed the hosts a penalty.



At least he will be able to laugh about it sooner rather than later – this was not a performance Chelsea fans will forget in a hurry.

Gibbs-White stepped up and sent Martinez the wrong way, but it was Delap’s name The City Ground was singing in the moments after their second.

While Alonso was busy correcting his mistake of starting Fofana by sending on Colwill, his other substitute offered some hope at last.

After Rogers and Pedro Neto combined through the middle, the Portuguese winger’s shot was blocked but fell to the alert Emegha, who settled and finished low across Matz Sels for his second goal in as many appearances.



If some of the Dutch striker’s teammates had his energy and alertness, the Blues would be in a far better place.

Having one back added some fire to Chelsea for a spell.

But they could still not gain anything even resembling control and needed Martinez to parry from Murillo’s strike, coming after a free-kick won thanks to a desperate Jordan Henderson challenge.

Chelsea were back to losing their heads. Alonso was booked, Neto erupted after getting a booking of his own for a rough challenge out wide.



From that free-kick, more soft defending, Pep Chavarria given two chances to clear and not getting it further than the edge of the box, gave Forest their third and ended any hope of a comeback.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The ball fell to Xaver Schlager, whose fine clipped ball was prodded past Martinez by Gibbs-White, who had just nudged ahead of Acheampong. Chelsea headed back to London deeper in despair, leaving Forest back on the up.

Maybe Alonso could learn from Oliver Glasner who, just as he did before their win over Manchester City here, turned his fire on his players this week. Standards, it turns out, seem to matter.

Sports.title: Toxic Chelsea's woes continue as Nottingham Forest add to Xabi Alonso's misery
Sports.content:
Toxic Chelsea's woes continue as Nottingham Forest add to Xabi Alonso's misery

NOTTINGHAM FOREST 3-2 CHELSEA: Xabi Alonso's side suffered a third successive defeat in the Premier League on a night that saw their fans brutally turn on one member of his squad

View 2 Images Morgan Gibbs-White was at the double against Chelsea (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

Morgan Gibbs-White bagged a brace to give Nottingham Forest their third win of the season and prolong Chelsea's miserable run.

‌



‌



Forest star Gibbs-White scored twice in the second half and rendered two goals by Blues forward Emmanuel Emegha as mere consultation efforts. It was Igor Jesus' spectacular strike that fired Oliver Glasner's men ahead at the City Ground, and they were good value for their 3-2 victory.

‌



Chelsea, on the other hand, were rudderless in both defence and attack, as they failed to bounce back from their shocking 4-1 loss at home to Leeds last time out. The defeat piles more pressure on Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, whose side have won just one of their last games in all competitions - and that was against 19th-placed Manchester United.

‌



Friday's match also saw Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana jeered by his own supporters, who took umbrage to comments made in an unauthorised two-hour interview with a French YouTuber. Alonso said pre-match that Fofana had apologised to the club.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

But the travelling fans didn't make much of his apparent apology. "F*** off, Fofana. You're not wanted here," was sang in the away end shortly after kick-off.

‌



His every touch was booed and there was even more ire among the Chelsea faithful when Jesus produced an acrobatic strike to put Forest 1-0 up inside five minutes. Alonso's decision to play Fofana and Moises Caicedo as a centre-back pairing was already backfiring, with ex-Chelsea striker Liam Delap dominating them.

Delap created Forest's second goal in the 51st minute, punishing Fofana after he misjudged the flight of the ball high in his own half. The Forest man went steaming into the box and was clumsily fouled by the 25-year-old, who received a yellow card to add insult to injury.

‌



Should Chelsea sack Xabi Alonso? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Igor Jesus' acrobatic finish gave Nottingham Forest an early lead (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

‌



Gibbs-White cooly tucked home the penalty before Emegha, a half-time substitute, pulled one back for Chelsea. Fofana's misery was then complete when he was withdrawn by Alonso in place of Levi Colwill.

The Blues pushed for an equaliser after the hour mark and had an appeals for a penalty waved away when Morgan Rogers' cross hit Forest's Jair Cunha on the arm. But the fourth goal of the night went the way of the home team, as Xaver Schlager's superb pass cut through the Chelsea defence and found Gibbs-White, who slotted past Emi Martinez to give Forest breathing room.

Article continues below

It was needed when, from nowhere, Emegha made it 3-2 and gave the visitors hope. But Forest held on to grind out the victory, moving them up to 14th in the table.

Sports.title: Chelsea fans turn on Wesley Fofana with brutal chant after interview controversy
Sports.content:
Chelsea fans turn on Wesley Fofana with brutal chant after interview controversy

Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana was booed by his own fans against Nottingham Forest after an unauthorised interview had caused a stir

View 3 Images Wesley Fofana's comments have not gone down well with Chelsea supporters (Image: Andrew Kearns - CameraSport via Getty Images)

Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana was roundly booed by his own fans during the match against Nottingham Forest. The Frenchman was heavily criticised for giving an unauthorised interview that aired following the 4-1 defeat to Leeds United, triggering fierce backlash.

‌



‌



Fofana, who has struggled to find his best form at Stamford Bridge, landed himself in serious trouble earlier in the week when an interview he had given to YouTuber Zack Nani was published. The French-language conversation ran for approximately two and a half hours.

‌



It touched on subjects including the defender's thoughts on retirement and his Carabao Cup penalty miss against Liverpool earlier in the season. Fofana stepped up and failed to convert his spot-kick on 28 October, with Chelsea ultimately losing the shootout 6-5.

‌



He had not sought the club's approval before giving the interview, and Fofana subsequently apologised, yet supporters were incensed after translations appeared to suggest he had laughed off the Liverpool defeat and showed little concern about his future in the game. The timing of the release, coming so soon after the Leeds loss, only made matters worse.

Xabi Alonso in disagreement with Jamie Carragher after comments on two Chelsea stars READ MORE :

While some supporters have been willing to move on, many remain deeply unhappy. As Chelsea fell 1-0 behind early on against Forest, chants of "F*** off Fofana, you're not welcome here" echoed from the away end, accompanied by a chorus of boos.

View 3 Images Wesley Fofana was booed (Image: Gareth Copley/Getty Images)

‌



Make sure you never miss the latest Chelsea news and opinion by making Football London one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Fofana was deployed in central defence at the City Ground next to Moises Caicedo in a somewhat unconventional Chelsea formation. Danny Welbeck led the line with Emmanuel Emegha relegated to the bench.

Following a nervy opening period, the away supporters voiced their displeasure with chants directed at Fofana, while jeering him each time he received possession.

‌



Fofana was quoted as saying during the interview: "The Liverpool match was tough to take, but I moved on quickly because that's just part of football.

"I took responsibility for the penalty - I missed it - and, well, I knew I wasn't a good penalty taker to begin with, you know [laughs]? So, I just thought, 'Okay, I'll own it.' But I ended up conceding a penalty during the match - it was a handball - but that's just part of the game.

‌



View 3 Images Alonso shed light on the apology (Image: Getty)

"You've got to go for it. And the way I look at it, if I fail, well, I've been through things. I've lived through a lot. If I fail, it's not that it's not a big deal - sure, it sucks, obviously - but as for me, if I'm the one being attacked, it's no big deal."

‌



Fofana gave away a penalty early in the second half against Forest. Boss Xabi Alonso had confirmed that Fofana had issued an apology.

He said: "We have addressed that with him [Fofana]. And, for sure, it was unfortunate. He has apologised. He knows it was not right in the moment, it was not right, the content.

Article continues below

"We are here to take things seriously and he has said it is not going to be repeated and we know that it is something we don't want, these kinds of things. And they are not going to be repeated, for sure."

Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya reportedly missed training ahead of Sunday's Premier League clash with Manchester City

David Raya reportedly missed Arsenal's training session ahead of their Premier League showdown with Manchester City.

The Spanish goalkeeper was forced off during the Gunners' 2-2 stalemate with Newcastle United last weekend with an injury to his right shoulder and was replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta shows true colours with response to Man City charges question
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta shows true colours with response to Man City charges question

Manchester City could receive a record points deduction which would rule them out of the Premier League title race, but Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta doesn't want his team benefiting from any hands-outs

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta is only focussed on Arsenal's affairs (Image: Hayters TV)

Mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are determined to win the title on the pitch - and not rely on Manchester City being clobbered with a points deduction.

‌



‌



Arsenal face their arch rivals at the Emirates on Sunday with City still waiting for the outcome of their appeal against the Premier League charges and punishment. There is an expectation that City will get hit with a record points deduction which could see them relegated and several bookmakers have made them favourites for the drop as a result.

‌



When asked whether Arsenal want to win the title on the pitch, Arteta said: "That's the only thing that we should put the energy and the focus on. There's nothing else."

‌



Arteta also says he does not want the case to overshadow Sunday's showdown. "I hope that it doesn't because, as well, it's a process that is still open, it's not resolved and we don't know what is going to happen," he said.

Make sure you don't miss the best Arsenal coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"So, no, I think when we have two teams at the level that both teams are at right now with the quality players that are on that pitch, it's a massive game and a big game to enjoy, I think."

‌



City made a sensational start to the season which saw them win the first seven games in the Premier League. But they are now stuck in a rut with just one win from their last seven in all competitions.

That stark drop off in form has followed City being found guilty of the 115 Premier League charges and facing the prospect of a points deduction and record fine. City will be guaranteed another red-hot reception when they visit the Emirates on Sunday and yet Arteta says he is not sure whether the two things are linked.

‌



Will Arsenal beat Manchester City? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

View 2 Images Manchester City's season could be ravaged by a points deduction (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

‌



Arteta added: "I don't know, that's a question for them. What I can see is when I watch them play, there's a lot of the games that they have to win, because this is football, to win games, and that's the way that they play, and what everyone else is doing.

"I don't think it’s in form or in performance. I think as well that they've been very, very unlucky with certain results."

Article continues below

Arteta is expected to have David Raya fit after the Spain keeper went off injured at Newcastle last weekend which also meant that he missed the draw with Borussia Dortmund. Arteta said he hopes Raya will be involved and added: "Every player has the same mindset; they want to be available, they want to be in the best possible condition, and there's no difference between them."

Sports.content:

Bruno Fernandes missed Manchester United's training session at Carrington on Friday morning as Mauricio Pochettino goes in search of his first win at his new club

Bruno Fernandes sat out Manchester United's Friday morning training session at Carrington as a precautionary measure after feeling slightly unwell - and now Mauricio Pochettino has confirmed he could miss Saturday afternoon's Premier League clash with Brentford.

The United skipper has been remarkably consistent since joining in January 2020, missing just six matches. He's virtually always fit and available, and was anticipated to still be in the starting line-up for the crucial Brentford fixture.

Como signed the Argentina international from Real Madrid in 2024 for just €6million (£5m) and the Spanish giants have a buy-back option. Real can sign Paz for €80m (£66m) in the summer of 2027, although the midfielder is understood not to favour a return to Madrid, where he wouldn't be guaranteed a starring role under Jose Mourinho.

If Real opted not to trigger their buy-back clause then Como would be free to sell as normal. Whether United would be able to attract such a talented young player in their current malaise - especially if they fail to qualify for the Champions League - remains to be seen.

‌



United do have some things in their favour, however. Paz shares the same agent as United boss Mauricio Pochettino and the club's history still carries some weight.

Paz has contributed six goals and eight assists in 16 appearances for Cesc Fabregas' side this season and is sure to have other suitors next year. His record of 25 goals and 25 assists in 91 games in total for Como, as well as his six goals in 16 games for Argentina, show his credentials.

‌



But Fernandes' boots would be big ones to fill at United, with the Portugal international having been their chief playmaker ever since his arrival from Sporting in 2020. He has previously been courted by Al-Hilal and Fenerbahce and was keen to emphasise his decision when they approached him when discussing his current situation this week.

"The club offered me a new contract, so I think that, from their side, shows that they want me to stay," Fernandes told Sky Sports. "There's no negotiations ongoing, but I've seen people saying that 'he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years'. If I wanted more money, I wouldn't be here.

"I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had the chance to leave and I always chose to be here."

Sports.title: No Rodgers, no problem! Steelers shock Broncos after dramatic week
Sports.content:
It had been a week clouded by Aaron Rodgers and his explosive claims regarding head coach Mike McCarthy, but the Pittsburgh Steelers swatted at the storm to claim a shock 27-5 win over the Super Bowl-contending Denver Broncos on Black Friday.

Broncos quarterback Bo Nix endured a miserable afternoon as he surrendered two interceptions and a lost fumble that resulted in two defensive touchdowns for the Steelers.

Denver trailed 24-5 after a dire first half in which they were limited to just 58 yards of offense, becoming just the third team since 1991 to post fewer than 60 yards while conceding two defensive touchdowns over the first two quarters of a game.

TJ Watt scored with an end zone fumble recovery, Jalen Ramsey returned a Nix interception to the house and D.K. Metcalf recorded a touchdown catch before appearing to celebrate by holding up eight fingers in an apparent support of Rodgers.

The Broncos looked anything but a contender as they slumped to 8-3, while the Steelers distanced themselves from a reflection of turmoil to improve to 7-4 in their push for the playoffs.

The Rodgers saga had lingered as an unwelcome backdrop heading into the game after the four-time MVP quarterback was released this week in the wake of his sensational appearance on the Pat McAfee Show.

Rodgers had claimed that head coach McCarthy fell asleep in team meetings, rebuffed suggestions to connect better with Pittsburgh's defensive players and accidentally shouted "one, two, three, Packers!" at the end of a team talk against the Philadelphia Eagles, the latter of which McCarthy would admit as an embarrassing moment.

Rodgers was subsequently cut amid what is set to mark the final season of his NFL career, though the storyline resurfaced during the game as broadcaster Al Michaels read a supposed text from the 42-year-old in which he is said to have claimed the Steelers had "barred" him from the team facility after he was benched for Mason Rudolph.

Rudolph started in place of Rodgers for the first time since the incident as he went nine of 15 passing for 142 yards and a touchdown, while Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren combined for 117 yards on the ground.

Reflecting on their win after such an eventful week, Rudolph said: "We just sort of rallied around Coach McCarthy, and I think in a weird way, the adversity brought us brought us closer together.

"It was a lot. Sort of unprecedented - certainly like nothing I've ever been through, and probably the same for all of my team-mates.

"I'm just so proud of the way we turned the page from [Aaron Rodgers' release on] Wednesday, and the veteran leadership - the Cam Haywards, the Jalen Ramseys, the TJ Watts - they really led us forward."

It took until 9.23 remaining in the third quarter for the first first down of the second half to arrive when the struggling Nix connected with Jaylen Waddle for 22 yards.

Still, it would come up empty amid a sequence of five successive punts between the teams, until Denver turned the ball over when Zach Allen forced a fumble from Dowdle that was recovered by Riley Moss with 3.31 on the clock.

Such was the story of their night that Denver failed to capitalise as their resulting drive ended in Wil Lutz missing a 53-yard field goal at the beginning of the fourth quarter.

Rudolph followed up by launching a downfield strike to Roman Wilson for 37 yards to set up Chris Boswell's 33-yard field goal for a 27-5 lead with 11.16 to play.

Nix's turnover issues resumed when he was intercepted by Daylen Everette at Pittsburgh's seven-yard line to ultimately end the game.

Pittsburgh then forced a swift three-and-out to pave the way for Rudolph's 22-yard touchdown strike to Metcalf, who did outstandingly to haul in a back-pedalling catch while facing man coverage from star corner Pat Surtain II.

Denver turned to their own defense as a potential route back into the game when Alex Singleton stuffed Warren in the end zone for a safety, before Lutz and Boswell exchanged a pair of 44 and 47-yard field goals.

Sports.title: Price out in Players Championship Finals first round in night of upsets
Sports.content:
Three of darts' biggest names were subject to shock upsets in the Players Championship Finals as Grand Slam champion Gerwyn Price, World No 2 Gian Van Veen, and No 1 seed Wessel Nijman were all knocked out in the first round at Minehead.

Price was beaten by 6-4 Sebastian Bialecki - the first time the Pole had beaten the Welshman in his career - while Jeffery de Graaf won two legs on the bounce to consign van Veen to defeat by the same scoreline.

Nijman was upset by 20-year-old Henry Coates despite posting an average of 110 - the second-highest average in Players Championship Finals history.

Image: Luke Humphries recorded a routine win against Darryl Pilgrim

World No 4 Luke Humphries, meanwhile, battled through his recurring back injury to secure a routine 6-3 victory against Darryl Pilgrim, while Michael van Gerwen withstood Connor Scutt to secure safe passage with a 6-3 first-round win of his own.

Beau Greaves also progressed to the second round with a scrappy 6-3 victory against former Lakeside champion Christian Kist despite a mediocre average of 89.64, and will face Rob Owen in the next round.

Van Veen, Nijman and Price joined James Wade, Gary Anderson, and Rob Cross as six of the top 25 players in the world were eliminated at the first opportunity in the last major before the World Darts Championship, which is live on Sky Sports from December 11th.

Wade was beaten 6-4 by Justin Hood and 2014 winner Anderson slipped to a 6-4 loss against Karel Sedlacek, while Cross fell to a thrilling 6-5 loss to Mickey Mansell.

Top players crumble on night of shock Minehead results

Image: Gian van Veen lost in the first round of the match to Jeffrey de Graaf

Van Veen - who finished runner-up to Price at the Grand Slam - struggled from the outset and throughout his match, managing only one maximum and checking out a lowly 15% of his finishes.

The Dutchman had three darts at double 16 to keep himself in the tournament, but failed to level the scores at 5-5 before de Graaf ruthlessly produced a 112 checkout to produce the first upset of the round.

Price, fresh off his first major win in four years after three successive final defeats, was heavily favoured against 22-year-old Bialecki, and looked to have rediscovered his tournament-winning form at the perfect moment when he produced a stunning 120 checkout to peg the deficit back to 5-4.

Image: Michael van Gerwen is into the next round

But Bialecki kept his cool and threw for the match, claiming his first career win against Price at the seventh attempt. The Pole will face off against de Graaf in round two.

The status quo was somewhat restored when Humphries and van Gerwen produced characteristically routine wins against lower-ranked opponents, with Humphries silencing doubters by averaging 93.32 in a week dominated by coverage of his injury.

Image: Stephen Bunting won a last-leg thriller against Max Hopp

But the show was stolen by Coates. The Derby native overcame his opponent's stellar average by notching an incredible 85.71% checkout success rate to claim victory in only his fourth-ever televised game.

Elsewhere, Stephen Bunting edged into the next round after beating German Max Hopp in a last-leg decider, while Kevin Doets averaged 107.34 in his win over Ritchie Edhouse and Chris Dobey came from behind to beat Mike De Decker 6-4.

Sports.title: Lyon dropped by Australia for Test series vs New Zealand
Sports.content:
Nathan Lyon has been dropped by Australia for their upcoming Test series against New Zealand.

The 39-year-old off-spinner, who has been a mainstay for the Baggy Greens for 13 years, will be replaced by Western Australia's Corey Rocchiccioli.

Lyon has not spoken publicly since Usman Khawaja's explosive Sandpapergate claims were published in his autobiography.

Image: Lyon has taken 577 Test wickets from 145 matches for Australia

Australia selection chair George Bailey confirmed that his omission was not related to the ongoing saga, and was based on performances.

"Nathan has not quite had the impact we would like with the ball in recent matches," said Bailey.

"We also know he has an extraordinary record and his experience, knowledge and skill can still be valuable to the program we have moving forward."

Other notable omissions include Marnus Labuschagne, Cooper Connolly and Beau Webster, with middle-order batter Jack Clayton being drafted into the squad and is in line to make his debut during the series.

In recent years, Lyon has seen his role with the Test side diminished, with a right hamstring injury, sustained during day five of the third Ashes Test in 2025, ruling him out of Test selection for eight months.

Lyon, who ranks second as Australia's all-time leading wicket-taker behind Shane Warne with 577 wickets from 145 Tests, had previously been dropped for the second Ashes Test at The Gabba and spoke openly about the omission, saying he was "filthy" and "gutted" about being dropped.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Martin Samuel explains what impact Usman Khawaja's claims that the entire Australia team were aware of the ball-tampering scheme in South Africa in 2018 could have on next summer's Ashes series in England

Lyon had also been omitted from Australia's second Test against South Africa in October.

Prior to last year's Test at The Gabba, the off-spinner had remarkably not been left out of a Test squad since he made his debut in 2011.

Uncapped off-spinner Rocchiccioli will likely go head-to-head with Scott Boland for a spot in the side to play New Zealand on the fiery Perth pitch in the first Test which starts on December 9.

"Corey has been a strong performer in domestic cricket for the past few seasons and has traits that are well suited to Australian conditions," Bailey said.

Under-scrutiny skipper Pat Cummins will captain the side, while Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Steve Smith, who have all found themselves at the centre of Australia's recent Sandpapergate saga, were also named in the team.

Smith had missed Australia's final Test against South Africa in Cape Town with a neck injury.

Australia will add one final player after the sixth round of Sheffield Shield matches.
