Sports.title: What went wrong for Alonso's Chelsea at Forest?
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso called for his Chelsea side to get back to the fundamentals before kick-off - and then watched on as they were outworked and outclassed on their way to a miserable 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest.

"Everyone in the club and team, we need to stick together and go through this moment. We have to deal with it and we are responsible," Alonso told Sky Sports after the game, which marked their third successive defeat in the Premier League.

"It is a difficult moment for everyone at the club. For the team and the fans. Disappointed to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions.

"We can't stop. We are low in confidence. At this level you need to hold results and not concede so much. That is why we are losing."

Alonso now has as many losses in 15 games across all competitions as he did in 34 for Real Madrid (6). Since March, no side has more defeats in the top-flight than the Blues (14). And their problems are mounting by the day.

Here, Sky Sports analyses the decisions that contributed to the worrying defeat at the City Ground.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Premier League clash between Nottingham Forest and Chelsea

Chelsea failed at the fundamentals

Despite the calls from Alonso to strip the game back to basics and get the fundamentals right, Chelsea felt short from minute one.

At the half-time interval, facing a 1-0 deficit and with zero shots on target, Chelsea had ran 3.8km less than Oliver Glasner's side.

The Forest boss was then quick to point out that they had outrun their opponents by 6km after the game. Yes, Chelsea had more possession, but they were also well behind in high-speed runs.

"I've seen one team jogging after the ball and one team sprinting after the ball and in this day and age, you cannot do that," said Jamie Redknapp.

"Distance covered is not always the barometer, but one thing is for sure, high-speed runs will tell you everything."

Fofana in the firing line - should he have started?

Starting Wesley Fofana in the same week the player had to apologise for his controversial interview, where he said he can "laugh about" the penalty miss that contributed to their Carabao Cup exit to Liverpool and contemplated retirement during injury spells at the club, was a bold move from Alonso. It did not pay off.

The tone was set early on. Fofana's first touches were heavily booed by the travelling Chelsea fans who had made the 130-mile journey in the cold and rain to watch their side slip to yet another dismal defeat.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Morgan Gibbs-White scored twice against Chelsea

The centre-back could only watch on as Igor Jesus volleyed in his stunning opener but was at the centre of attention, for all the wrong reasons, for the second.

After misjudging the ball while battling with former teammate Liam Delap, who caused problems all evening, Fofana rushed to atone for his error and fouled the striker in the penalty area.

Morgan Gibbs-White doubled the lead from the spot and ultimately the comeback, led by substitute Emmanuel Emegha, fell short.

He was cautioned for the challenge and eventually taken off for Levi Colwill, who was dropped by Alonso instead of Fofana, and the fans booed him once again.

"It didn't feel like a game for him tonight. He had a bad week with the podcast," said Jamie Redknapp after the game.

"By playing Fofana tonight, you created that. It was inevitable. He is lacking so much confidence; he needs some time.

"He is having a real difficult run of it at the moment."

Caicedo at centre back - why?

After making the decision to drop Colwill, options at the centre of defence were limited with Maxence Lacroix and Reece James both sidelined.

Playing Josh Acheampong at centre-back and giving a rare start to Malo Gusto, an unused substitute on the night, seemed the more obvious choice but Alonso opted to play Moises Caicedo, arguably the best midfielder in the league, in the back four instead.

He was then tasked with dealing with a strike partnership of Delap and Igor Jesus. A difficult task for even the tallest of centre-backs, let alone a makeshift one standing at 5-foot-10.

He gave space to the Brazil striker for the opener and his presence in midfield was missed. He still led the way with 114 passes on the night, but Chelsea needed him in the middle of the park to deal with the likes of James McAtee and Xaver Schlager.

"They have bought players but if they do not sign a centre back, they cannot compete," said Redknapp after the game. He is right.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Emmanuel Emegha gave Chelsea late hope

Emegha's impact was too little, too late

Alonso admitted that Emegha's performance after scoring twice off the bench was the lone positive for his side to take from their trip to the East Midlands. "For sure, he is having a good impact," he said. "He has done well. That is a positive."

He scored his first goal in the 4-1 defeat to Leeds United last time out but lost his place in the starting line-up on Friday.

Danny Welbeck, 36, was given the nod ahead of him and his performance mirrored the struggles Chelsea had as a unit.

Alonso called on the experience of Jordan Henderson and Welbeck to help weather their current struggles but it only whipped up the storm.

Welbeck was a bystander in the first half and had just seven touches before being replaced at the break, Emegha then scored with his first two to help spark hopes of a comeback.

His header for the second, holding off Jair Cunha, was one of the rare moments Chelsea matched the physicality of their opponents. He has to start moving forward without Joao Pedro available.

Alonso said the only way he knows how to address these issues is to attack them on the training ground. He has just five days to do that before they are put to the test against Crystal Palace, live on Sky Sports, who will be desperate for a win.

Sports.title: Forest beat Chelsea to heap pressure on Alonso as Fofana is booed
Sports.content:
Morgan Gibbs-White scored two in Nottingham Forest’s 3-2 win over Chelsea at the City Ground as the crisis deepened for Xabi Alonso.

Igor Jesus volleyed Forest in front inside five minutes of what was a dismal first half for Chelsea and they never recovered parity. Wesley Fofana - booed by his own supporters throughout - conceded a penalty early in the second half that Gibbs-White converted.

Emmanuel Emegha did come off the bench to pull one back soon afterwards but another goal from the Forest captain better reflected the superiority of Oliver Glasner's side even if Emegha's second in the 89th minute made for a surprisingly nervy finale.

Forest began the evening beside the Trent with only goal difference keeping them out of the relegation zone, but victory lifts them clear of the bottom six. The spotlight now falls on Chelsea, who missed the chance to climb back into the top five.

It is four Premier League defeats in their last five games under Alonso who appears to be scrambling for solutions given the evidence of this team selection. It is not only Fofana under scrutiny at Chelsea. A club in disarray? Alonso needs to get a grip on it and fast.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Igor Jesus volleyed home a stunning opener

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Morgan Gibbs-White slotted home a penalty

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gibbs-White scored his second

How Forest were too good for Chelsea

Liam Delap had been the two-goal hero in the 3-1 win over Manchester City last time out at home and would have been desperate to score against another of his former clubs but it was Igor Jesus' stunning strike that silenced the Chelsea supporters early on.

"It is the first opportunity for them to play together, they have different strengths," Glasner had told Sky Sports beforehand. Igor Jesus' strengths include volleys beyond Emiliano Martinez, it turns out. It was his first goal at the City Ground since April.

Alonso had responded to the alarming defeat to Leeds by dropping Levi Colwill and playing Moises Caicedo in defence. The Chelsea boss changed to a back four as well in a bid to find some form after losing three of their previous four Premier League games.

"Today we need strong characters, big personalities," said Alonso beforehand. "Players that know what it takes to compete in the Premier League." That explained the decision to bring in Danny Welbeck up front, with Jordan Henderson holding midfield together.

But Welbeck was a passenger in the first half, having only seven touches of the ball - half as many as anyone else - while Henderson found himself overrun. Forest were at the back line time and again. Chelsea were fortunate to be only one down at the break.

Fofana had not endeared himself to supporters by giving an unauthorised interview in which he not only talked of being close to quitting football but appeared to joke about missing a penalty in the Carabao Cup defeat to Liverpool. This performance was worse.

He was culpable for Forest's second goal, bested by Delap before hastily fouling him inside the penalty box in a rash attempt to recover. Gibbs-White slotted home from the spot and Fofana was substituted to the sound obscene chants from the Chelsea fans.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Emmanuel Emegha got Chelsea back in it

Alonso's side did pull one back through the young substitute Emegha, when Pedro Neto's shot was deflected kindly into his path. But Xaver Schlager's sumptuous ball clipped in behind the Chelsea defence allowed Gibbs-White to hook home his second.

Emegha nodded in another late on to make the decision to omit him after scoring the first goal against Leeds look even more of an error, but it was not enough to earn an undeserved point. Forest held on and are on the up again. Chelsea have problems.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Emegha gave Chelsea late hope

The key moments from The City Ground

5 - GOAL! Igor Jesus volleyed Forest into an early lead

51 - GOAL! Gibbs-White doubled the lead from the spot

54 - GOAL! Substitute Emegha pulled one goal back

73 - GOAL! Gibbs-White latched onto Schlager's pass

89 - GOAL! Emegha scored his second of the night

Glasner: We are progressing

Nottingham Forest boss Oliver Glasner speaking in the press conference:

"It looks like we are progressing and this is what we all want to see. But also last time [against Man City] was the first swallow [that does not make a summer] and now it's the second swallow and I think everybody could feel it tonight.

"So stay humble, take this feeling of the win and the confidence and the belief but stay humble and prepare well for the three-game week before we face Brighton here.

"We are all feeling again that we are heading in the right direction. Still a lot to do, but every win helps in building confidence and trust. But still 12 points after 12 games is not enough."

Alonso: Things are not clicking

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso speaking in the press conference:

"We are working, trying to find solutions, trying to do our best, but things are not going the way we want. And I don't understand any other way but to work, to try again.

"Because if we want to get something, it will have to come from us. No one will come from outside to give us a solution. And the quality that we need, the mentality that we need, it needs to come from within the team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso reflects on his side's defeat

"Overall, we can do better. I think that we are going through a difficult moment of confidence, things are not clicking, things are not going the way we want.

"We know that in football, this can change quickly, or this can continue. So it's down to us to work and to find solutions to have a better feeling on the pitch and to get better results, because that's what we need."

Asked if he was frustrated with the Chelsea fans booing Wesley Fofana:

"We need to support everyone because we need everyone. We need the fans, we need all the players, we need to stick together, because if not, it will get more complicated."

Sports.title: Southampton sink Middlesbrough in ill-tempered first meeting since 'Spygate'
Sports.content:
Southampton's unbeaten start to the season at St Mary's continued as they beat leaders Middlesbrough 2-0.

Six-and-a-half months on from 'Spygate' - which dominated the headlines during last season's play-offs - Saints emerged victorious, as they did in the semi-final second leg, in an ill-tempered affair that saw 10 yellow cards brandished to players and two to coaching staff.

Had it not been for the four-point penalty imposed on them as a result, Friday night's win would have sent them to the top of the Sky Bet Championship.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Southampton's Finn Azaz caused a stir with his celebrations after scoring his side's second goal

But goals from Ryan Manning and Finn Azaz - who goaded his former club's fans as he celebrated - put them within touching distance of the summit.

Boro's third defeat of the season opens the door to Stoke and Wolves to leapfrog them into top spot if they win on Saturday.

In the build-up, Tonda Eckert and Kim Hellberg insisted they had buried the hatchet - but neither fanbase had forgotten it. Both sets of players were booed when they came out to warm up, while chants referencing the saga echoed around St Mary's. The atmosphere was electric.

Meaningful chances came at a premium in the first half, but they were high quality when they did come.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Manning opened the scoring for Southampton

The home fans fell silent for a split-second when Will Lankshear ghosted away from his man and moved one-on-one with Saints goalkeeper Daniel Peretz, who denied the Championship's top scorer.

And at the other end, Radek Vitek had to be at his best, first to tip Azaz's fierce strike onto the crossbar, then to push a Cyle Larin header over.

The first goal came just before the hour. Kuryu Matsuki's cross flew over everyone in the box, but James Bree was there to collect and fizz in a low ball that Manning ran onto and side-footed high into the net.

Image: Finn Azaz scored Southampton's second against his former club - then goaded the travelling fans

Twenty minutes later, Azaz capitalised on a defensive mistake to calmly slot home the second, before running straight towards the visiting supporters and making a sarcastic crying gesture, sparking a heated reaction.

This is not a rivalry that is going anywhere any time soon.

Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert in his press conference

Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert admitted he "didn't like" a social media video posted by the club ahead of the first meeting with Middlesbrough since 'Spygate' last season.

The video included footage of Oli McBurnie's Championship play-off final winner for Hull against Boro at Wembley in May.

It was also played on the big screens at St Mary's in the lead-up to kick-off.

"I didn't like the video this morning. No, I didn't like it," Eckert said in his post-match press conference.

"I haven't even seen the video, I've just heard the information about what was in there and I didn't like it.

"I think, if we look back a couple of months, the reality is that both clubs have lost. One club has lost off the pitch, the other has lost off the pitch. I think it's an episode that is good to close for both clubs and to move forward.

"I've apologised to Kim, I've apologised openly. For me, there is no need to warm that up again."

It was pointed out to Eckert that a box of tissues had been placed on the table behind which managers sit, seemingly mocking Hellberg after his emotional reaction to the defeat in the play-off semi-final at St Mary's in May.

After a few seconds of looking at the box, he said: "You can take this one [box of tissues] off." He then placed them under the table.

"I just love to talk about football and I hope everyone who came here, especially the Middlesbrough staff and players know that," he said.

"I hope they know these things don't come from me."

Hellberg said: "They are always trying to fire everything up. I saw there were some posts at the end where they tried to mock me - or whoever they were trying to mock - so I feel a little bit small about that.

"Otherwise, there's a very good football side, so many good players, the staff are good. There's no need for that, but it is what it is."

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Scratchy Ireland still prove too strong for Australia at Twickenham
Sports.content:
Nick Timoney was among the try scorers at Twickenham as Ireland banked a sixth Nations Championship victory from seven Tests

Ireland rounded off their Nations Championship campaign with a sixth victory from seven Tests, defeating Australia 38-14 at Allianz Stadium Twickenham.

Such a record can only be matched by England and France, should either or both defeat New Zealand and South Africa this weekend, respectively - Ireland finished behind England on points difference and France due to bonus points in the northern hemisphere standings.

On Friday, centre Robbie Henshaw, back-row Nick Timoney, wing Rob Baloucoune and replacement No 8 James McNabney (two) scored tries, with Sam Prendergast adding all five conversions and a penalty.

Ireland 38-14 Australia - Score summary Ireland - Tries: Henshaw (26), Timoney (37), Baloucoune (43), McNabney (73,80+1). Cons: Prendergast (26,39,44,74,80+1). Pens: Prendergast (40+3). Australia - Tries: Williams (22), Thomas (56). Cons: Gordon (23, 57).

Andy Farrell's Ireland were far from their best on the night, but the Wallabies could only score two tries through lock Jeremy Williams and scrum-half Kalani Thomas, wasting a further nine 22 entries up against an extremely tough Irish defence.

The victory also saw Ireland claim the Raeburn Shield from Australia - rugby's lineal world title which dates back to the first Test match ever played in 1871. Australia had won it by beating Wales, who claimed it from New Zealand in Cardiff a fortnight ago.

Twitter Due to your consent preferences, you’re not able to view this Privacy Options

Ireland began the contest well off the standard they produced in victory over world No 1-ranked South Africa last week, with their attack struggling to click and errors widespread.

Australia, despite a wealth of early possession and territory, produced a number of mistakes themselves, though, with fly-half Carter Gordon guilty of missing touch with a penalty from hand in the most glaring example.

In the end, it took until the 22nd minute for the Wallabies to strike for the opener: Williams scoring from close range after Tadhg Beirne had actually stolen an Australia five-metre lineout, but Ronan Kelleher had spilled to surrender possession back.

Despite making the much stronger start in the contest, it took Australia until the 22nd minute to score via Jeremy Williams

Within four minutes, Ireland were level, as they struck for a try off their very first 22 entry: a clever lineout move to the tail setting scrum-half Jamison Gibson-Park breaking back down the blindside, before Kelleher was stopped just short.

Centre Stuart McCloskey did the damage from there, as he took on the ball and fed midfield partner Henshaw, who slid over untouched.

Ireland's Robbie Henshaw scored their opener four minutes after Australia had taken the lead

Three minutes from the end of the half, Ireland displayed their clinical nature again as Timoney scored following a well-constructed rolling maul to move Farrell's side in front.

Back-row Timoney crossed for a clinical Ireland to take a lead into half-time

Ireland almost had a third try before the break in the final play, only for centre Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii to stick out a hand in a deliberate knock-on. The Wallaby avoided a yellow card, but Prendergast stretched the lead to 10 points off the tee.

Into the second half, Ireland started far brighter, with Jacob Stockdale almost scoring down the left less than two minutes in, and Baloucoune then scoring a minute later after collecting a Prendergast cross-field kick James Ramm could only deflect into his path.

Rob Baloucoune, a week after scoring two in victory over South Africa, scored Ireland's third on the night

Prendergast converted for a 24-7 lead, and what ensued was virtually 10 minutes of sustained Australia attack in the Irish 22 for no points.

The Wallabies did finally cross for their second try through Thomas in the 55th minute, with the score surviving a TMO check into the grounding.

Gordon narrowed Ireland's lead to 10 points with the conversion, but they failed to build from there.

Scrum-half Kalani Thomas slid over for Australia's second try, but again it came after a number of 22 entries yielded no points

Instead, Ireland's pack tore forward for a scrum penalty against the head in the lead-up to their fourth try - impressive back-row McNabney showing his power off the bench to wrestle over by the posts.

In the final attack of the half, Ireland then blew out the scoreline beyond what had truly transpired in the contest, in truth, with the exciting McNabney finishing again.

Exciting back-row James McNabney scored twice in the closing stages on just his second Test cap

Farrell: Not a brilliant performance but we're building... on the quiet

Ireland head coach Andy Farrell told ITV Sport:

"Everyone could see it was a bit error-ridden with all sorts of things going on.

"But I suppose the way that we stayed composed and did it in our own way was a credit to how we kept on going.

"That was epitomised in the first half where we had no territory and no possession whatsoever, and we go in with the lead, which was very pleasing.

"It wasn't a brilliant performance, but at the same time I'm very pleased with the composure to make sure we keep on going.

"We would have taken that [going four from four] at the start, wouldn't we? Sport, when you're playing good sides in international rugby, doesn't always go your way.

"It didn't last week, but we still found a way. We did that today. We'll take that and we'll move on to the Six Nations.

"We're very pleased with the competition that we're building, and we've got a lot of good players back home who are dying to get back into the room.

"We're building nicely, on the quiet."

Andy Farrell's Ireland ended their 2026 with 10 victories from 12 Tests

O'Driscoll: Are Ireland Rugby World Cup contenders? Not yet

Giving his verdict on Ireland's year, Brian O'Driscoll told ITV Sport:

"It was a disappointing Argentina, so you can't really gauge a huge amount. It was a good victory against them. Fiji, the expectation there is to win.

"The big one was South Africa, and they stood up to the plate there. They delivered a performance they should be proud of.

"This is a very well-settled team, except in one or two positions, and mainly your pivotal position at No 10.

"To give him [Prendergast] the confidence to guide the team around in a big game like that will go a long way towards restoring belief in all the players that have played 70, 80 Tests.

"But mostly for him as he's kind of forging his path as a relative newcomer to the Test Arena.

"I think, on the whole, very pleasing. If you had given us 10 victories in 12 games this calendar year, we'd have bitten your hand off, considering how they lost to France in the opening game of the Six Nations.

"The only other loss being to New Zealand in Eden Park.

"Are we World Cup contenders yet? I wouldn't say yes, no, I wouldn't. I think there's other teams a little bit ahead of us, but a year is a long way to go, and hopefully we can narrow that gap."

Australia head coach Les Kiss cut a disappointed figure at full-time

Prendergast: We were scrappy at times

Ireland fly-half Sam Prendergast told ITV:

"I think we stuck with it pretty well. There were some scrappy parts we'd like to be a bit better at.

"I thought we were quite clinical in their 22 but scrappy at times. I think he [Andy Farrell] will have a similar gist; there's definitely some good parts. There's loads we can be better at and want to be better at today.

"Coming into the autumn, we knew we had a couple of big games to start. We went four from four and that's what we were targeting. There was no lack of motivation.

"I'm really enjoying [playing for Ireland]. We're building towards the Rugby World Cup. Loads of highs and lows at the moment so, I won't get too high."

Kiss: Ireland were clinical, that was the difference

Australia head coach Les Kiss told ITV Sport:

"The first half we got some traction but we're disappointed with our end zone. Ireland were very clinical and took their chances when they came up.

"Credit to them, we needed to persist a bit longer. They were up for it. That was the difference; they took the key chances when they had to.

"Fair play to them, they put the scoreboard pressure on us. There's still a lot of good things there and a lot of things to look forward to, we've just got to build more consistency throughout our game."

What's next?

Ireland are next in action during the 2027 Six Nations in February, when they start with a huge Test against England in Dublin at the Aviva Stadium on Friday February 5 (8.10pm kick-off).

Ireland's Nations Championship fixtures and results Australia 31-33 Ireland July 4 Japan 20-36 Ireland July 11 New Zealand 40-21 Ireland July 18 Ireland 42-12 Argentina November 6 Ireland 43-15 Fiji November 14 Ireland 20-17 South Africa November 21 Ireland 38-14 Australia November 27

Australia now enter their offseason and are not in action again until April 25 2027 when they face New Zealand at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane. Australia are hosting the Rugby World Cup in 2027 between October 1-November 13.

Sports.title: Aaron Rodgers fires back at Tom Brady after NFL legend called out ex-Steelers star for his explosive interview
Sports.content:
Aaron Rodgers fires back at Tom Brady after NFL legend called out ex-Steelers star for his explosive interview

Aaron Rodgers has issued a fiery response to Tom Brady after the NFL legend called out the ex-Steelers quarterback for torching the 'sanctity' of the team's locker room.

On Thanksgiving, Brady weighed in on the ongoing saga surrounding Rodgers and the Steelers after the quarterback was cut by the franchise in dramatic fashion.

The decision to release Rodgers came after the quarterback conducted an explosive interview on The Pat McAfee Show, taking aim at the franchise and, in particular, coach Mike McCarthy following the team's decision to drop him for their Friday game.

In reference to the saga, Brady said on FOX's Thanksgiving Day broadcast 'that the sanctity of an NFL locker room is a very sacred place and we shouldn't ever lose track of that as players'.

The seven-time Super Bowl winner added that it's 'a privilege to be in that locker room' and questioned Rodgers for airing 'private things' out in the public eye.

Just one day later, Rodgers has now fired back. During Prime Video's broadcast of the Broncos-Steelers matchup, Al Michaels revealed a text he received from Rodgers.

Aaron Rodgers has fired back at Tom Brady after the latter publicly criticized his actions

Brady took aim at Rodgers during the Eagles-Cowboys Thanksgiving Day game

Al Michaels reads a message from Aaron Rodgers while on the call of Steelers-Broncos for Prime Video. pic.twitter.com/R9HMP37Zam — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 27, 2026

Michaels claimed that Rodgers said: 'A lot of talk about the sanctity of the locker room. The code of sanctity exists to protect the integrity of the locker room, not to provide immunity from accountability for its leadership.'

Reading from his phone, Michaels continued: 'They [Steelers] took this public. [I] never heard from the head coach, then they leaked at 11pm.

'They also barred me from the facility. That's why I went to McAfee'.

Rodgers' comments instantly went viral on social media, with fans left in disbelief that the two legendary quarterbacks were locking horns in the public eye.

Taking to X, one fan wrote: 'What a stunner, by the way, that Rodgers would find a way to respond to Brady today - by texting Al Michaels.

'The actions speak more than the words. Maybe I'm wrong, he's been an amazing player, first ballot Hall of Famer, but he's done in the NFL.'

Meanwhile, another fan said: 'Aaron Rodgers fires back at Tom Brady, is basically what this was. I’d trust Tom, who had his own issues with his coach over Aaron Rodgers because Brady was one of the best leaders in NFL history.'

Another wrote: 'So Aaron Rodgers is gonna pick a fight with Tom Brady now??'.

Rodgers was released by the Steelers after he eviscerated 'unwell' McCarthy in an interview

During his analysis on Thanksgiving, Brady was quick to recognize Rodgers' resume on the field, but made it clear that individual greatness does not excuse his actions.

He continued: 'Certainly a Hall of Fame career. He's a tremendous player and it has nothing to do with his play style.

'I was fortunate to be around a lot of great teammates over the years and what made a great teammate to me was [that] you cared about your teammates and coaches.

'And that supersedes any individual aspect of your game that you want to promote.'

Meanwhile, in his interview with Pat McAfee on Wednesday, Rodgers eviscerated 'unwell' coach Mike McCarthy and claimed he would fall asleep in team meetings.

Rodgers said: 'I want to take you back through my last week, so you can understand this is not an abnormal week. These are some of the issues that I've been dealing with that ultimately led to where we're at now.

'Last Wednesday, we were in a quarterback meeting. Mike came in late, sat down, and within 10 minutes began snoring. Woke himself up, was rattling his papers. We all looked around. Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again, and less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened.

'Thursday, he misses an offensive meeting. Friday, he doesn't come to the walkthrough. We only have a walkthrough really on Friday. Doesn't come to the first walkthrough. Doesn't come to the protection walkthrough on Thursday.

Rodgers accused the 62-year-old Steelers coach of sleeping and 'snoring' in team meetings

'Saturday, he misses the morning meeting, and we don't have a team meeting Saturday night for whatever reason in Philly, and then it comes to Sunday when obviously we struggled and the product wasn't great.'

Rodgers claims an enraged McCarthy, when confronted with the sleeping claims by his quarterback, said to him: 'I'm not f***ing sleeping, I've never slept at the f***ing facility. Who the f*** is saying that? F*** you.'

In possibly the most shocking allegation, however, Rodgers claimed McCarthy confused the Steelers with his and Rodgers' former team, the Green Bay Packers, during his halftime speech in Philadelphia.

He added: 'I think the nail in the coffin for so many of us was at halftime. Towards the end of it, the offense is on one side, defense on the other side, and there's some rambling or something, and without even a heads up, he says, 'All right, 1-2-3, Packers.'

'That's what he broke it down on in the locker room. It was one of those things where nobody was even like saying Steelers because it was so you know in the moment, and it was like weird rambling that was audible enough that everybody across the entire locker room heard it, and I think we all looked around, going, 'What the f***? What is going on? Where is this person? Where is his head at this point?'

Sports.title: There's a convenient ignorance in the new Tyson Fury documentary. This is what they've chosen to hide, and what it reveals about Netflix's cynical relationship with reality, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
There are some affecting and moving moments in Tyson Fury, the documentary about a part of the fighter’s career which, conveniently, does not include any defeats, does not mention the fact that he served a backdated two-year drugs ban after he first won the world heavyweight title in 2015 and skims quickly over his predilection for homophobia and misogyny.

Fury’s wife, Paris, emerges from the 103-minute film as the hero of the piece, a strong, funny, clever, caring, emotionally intelligent woman who held her family together as her husband struggled with mental health issues and she tried to cope with the trauma of giving birth to a stillborn child.

Her relationship with Fury is everything that is good about the film, which was released on Netflix on Friday morning.

It is a fascinating study of the fighter, too. Or at least of the parts we are allowed to see. We are not allowed to see wrongdoing or cruelty or ridicule or bullying but we are allowed to see vulnerability.

We are allowed to see a fighting man who has a recurring dream about seeing a slow-motion plane crash and realising too late that the plane is heading straight for him and that there is nothing he can do to escape the fireball.

Any analysis of Tyson Fury – or what was left of it after some feverish last-minute editing removed all references to a diagnosis of schizophrenia that had been eagerly trailed in the build-up to its release – has to begin and end with the fact that it is more of an exercise in public relations and promotion for his fight against Anthony Joshua next month than an examination of a career in full. It is a long, long way from the unvarnished truth and that makes it average.

The Tyson Fury documentary is a fascinating study of the fighter. Or at least of the parts we are allowed to see

Fury’s wife, Paris, emerges from the 103-minute film as the hero of the piece, a strong, funny, clever, caring, emotionally intelligent woman who held her family together

Its most chilling episode is the aftermath of Fury's victory over Wladimir Klitschko in Dusseldorf in November 2015 when Fury falls into an agony of self-loathing.

He sits on a stage promoting a rematch that never happened, taking off his shirt and parading his bloated body to the cameras, saying that he hates everything about boxing and wondering aloud whether Klitschko will do him a favour by ‘knocking me into next week’.

‘I do not care about anything or anybody,’ he says in that clip.

And on the stage beside him and in the audience in front of him, people laugh heartily and people smile nervously and by then Fury knows he may face drugs charges because he has tested positive for the anabolic steroid nandrolone.

But the film does not tell us that. It does not explore what effect that might have had on Fury’s mental state. It does not explore quite how much of an advantage using the drug gave him over opponents.

The film's ethos raises more questions about just how far companies like Netflix are prepared to go to manipulate the image of sportsmen and women whose stories they are telling and selling. Partly because of the late panic about the mention of a schizophrenia diagnosis and its subsequent excision from the film, the line between where truth begins and ends feels thoroughly blurred by the time the credits roll.

Let’s be honest about this: the film was partly sold to the public on the back of that claim that Fury had been diagnosed with schizophrenia – as well as bipolar disorder, anxiety, depression, ADHD and OCD – some months after the 2015 world title victory over Klitschko in Germany.

That was how it was trailed. That was what garnered many of the headlines. It was not until Daily Mail Sport’s Jeff Powell MBE broke the story that the British Boxing Board of Control might not let the fight go ahead if it believed Fury was suffering from the illness or any lingering psychosis that the mention of schizophrenia was edited out of the scenes.

Fury will finally step into a ring with Anthony Joshua next month. And the primary purpose of the documentary is to advertise the fight

'Only one thing is certain,' Board general secretary Robert Smith had said on Thursday afternoon. 'That Tyson will not be allowed to enter the ring unless our doctors are satisfied there is no risk to his health.

'We are reviewing all the information about his mental condition and will come to a decision about authorising the fight in the next few days.'

Netflix, whose broadcast of the Joshua-Fury fight represents a leap forward in their move into boxing and live sport in general, sensed a clear and present danger to their investment, a danger that they had brought upon themselves.

It was not long before there was a statement. There had been a mistake. Fury had never been diagnosed with schizophrenia after all and everything was fine now. Nothing to see here.

And so, on Friday morning, once Tyson Fury had been aired without any mention of schizophrenia at all, the BBBofC released a statement, too. ‘Tyson Fury has been cleared to box on December 11,’ it said. Sighs of relief all round. Whatever you do, don’t mention the schizophrenia.

It may have been a blip in the promotion, which will ramp up as the fight gets closer, but the episode shone a light on Netflix and its coverage of sport as it seeks to move further and further into the arena. At the heart of its coverage, there is a contradiction that is also a flaw.

Much of its selling point is to show the viewer things they have not seen before, to take them behind the scenes of a sport and allow them to get to know the combatants more closely than ever. It is part of what has made Drive to Survive, their F1 behind-the-scenes documentary, so stunningly successful.

But Drive to Survive only shows you what F1 wants you to see. It’s an official version. It’s varnished.

The Netflix cameras chase Adrian Newey and Christian Horner through the paddock in filming for an episode of Drive to Survive

The inconvenient stuff, the anabolic steroids, the stuff that might harm the product? That is nowhere. That does not even get a mention in the Fury documentary

And the Tyson Fury documentary carries exactly the same vibe. The inconvenient stuff, the anabolic steroids, the stuff that might harm the product? That is nowhere. That does not even get a mention.

‘People in the boxing world just wanted to use me,’ Fury says in the documentary as he looks back at the time of his gravest battle with mental illness.

Until late on Thursday night, schizophrenia was being used to plug one of his fights. Boxing has always been a dark trade so cynicism is greeted with a shrug.

Some things have changed since Fury fought Klitschko in 2015, some faces are different and there is a new broadcaster, or streamer, in town. But some things remain the same.

Sports.title: How Andoni Iraola made Liverpool's fans - and players - fall in love with him: 'There's a connection building. He gets the club'
Sports.content:
How Andoni Iraola made Liverpool's fans - and players - fall in love with him: 'There's a connection building. He gets the club'

The first sign that Andoni Iraola was different came this summer in Chicago during Liverpool's pre-season tour.

Sitting in a conference room up in the clouds overlooking the Windy City skyline and out to Lake Michigan, Iraola relaxed into a chair and held court for the best part of an hour. It was his first interview with the assembled Merseyside media corps but felt more laidback and personable than most of those chats tend to.

Most managers have little time for outsiders but Iraola, sipping a black coffee, was happy to stay put and talk about modern football, life in the Basque country and cycling. Only some of that conversation made the cut for the write-up but it all painted a clear picture of the new Liverpool boss.

Four months later, the Anfield faithful are slowly falling in love with Iraola.

It’ll take plenty more time and trophies to reach the adoration they had for Jurgen Klopp but, if Iraola can get halfway to that level, he will have done well.

So ahead of his first Merseyside derby, how has Iraola settled in at Liverpool – and why are the fans taking to him in return?

The Anfield faithful are slowly falling in love with their Spanish manager Andoni Iraola

Iraola takes training in Chicago on Liverpool's pre-season tour. The manager was relaxed during that time despite the pressures of a move to a huge club

It’s the little things that have helped Iraola forge a bond with the Kop.

He has been spotted on the parks of Merseyside taking in Sunday league football. He took his young daughter to a Women’s Super League game and attends her netball matches. And he has taken time to learn about the history of the club and the city, with incognito visits to tourist hotspots.

Iraola and his wife came to Liverpool on a city-break long before he became manager and loved the feel of it; it was a reminder of his hometown Usurbil, near San Sebastian in northern Spain.

He also enjoys cycling, a lifelong hobby, and his helmet helps him go unrecognised on rides around the city.

At the AXA Training Centre, there is a feeling of unity. Virgil van Dijk is a regular at academy matches, Dominik Szoboszlai dropped in on an age-group side last week and first-team players are tutoring youngsters and tracking the teams' scorelines.

None of the above might feel noteworthy in isolation but, to Liverpool fans, these little signs of a joined-up club mean the world. This is a unique fanbase which is often misunderstood: they want people who ‘get’ the club and the city. By immersing himself in them, Iraola is achieving those small wins.

‘There’s definitely a connection building between us and Iraola,’ says Dan Clubbe of fan channel Redmen TV. ‘First and foremost, matters on the pitch are starting to get exciting and the belief is growing as a result.

‘But beyond that, he’s very likeable and although it’s a cliche, he seems to “get it”. Small as they may seem, things like the WSL game, getting out to grassroots footy, integrating youngsters... that all resonates with us as fans.

‘It even goes beyond that. He seems to genuinely love it (here) and wants to understand better the opportunity he’s got, the place that he’s in. It’s still early days but it feels like he realises the significance and responsibility of his position.’

This time last year, the wheels were starting to fall off for Arne Slot. Liverpool felt like a fractured club

Tensions were rumbling around Mohamed Salah, who kicked off publicly and said the club had thrown him ‘under the bus’

This time last year, the wheels were starting to fall off for Arne Slot. Just six months after a Premier League trophy parade through the streets of the city, Liverpool lost 4-1 at home to PSV Eindhoven to record their ninth loss in 12 games, also including a 3-0 defeat by Nottingham Forest at Anfield.

Tensions were rumbling around Mohamed Salah, who in early December kicked off publicly and said the club had thrown him ‘under the bus’. He was dropped from a matchday squad and his relationship with Slot never really recovered. He is now at Turkish side Trabzonspor.

The best way to describe the feeling around the club last season was fractured. Sources point to how Slot kept the same outlook when things were going badly as he did when they were going well.

The place needed a fresh outlook. Iraola was the leading candidate to succeed Slot, though the hierarchy also assessed Pierre Sage, who has since been hired and fired by Crystal Palace, and Sebastian Hoeness of Stuttgart.

The Basque has brought back a feelgood factor to Anfield. Everything feels brighter, smiles are worn more often and even the online naysayers have had to find new things to complain about.

Captain Van Dijk has helped Iraola settle and took the squad to the museum at Anfield a fortnight ago to teach the new signings and academy graduates about the club. Iraola did not join them as he was too busy in the analysis room.

One of Iraola’s assistants, former Bournemouth defender Tommy Elphick, is a big Liverpool fan and that has helped, too. Elphick, alongside fellow assistant Shaun Cooper, has been influential in sorting out a set-piece record that was the worst in the league last season.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk has helped Iraola settle into the club

Iraola with assistants Tommy Elphick (left) and Shaun Cooper, who have helped sort out the team's set-piece problems

Elphick and Cooper were with Iraola at Bournemouth and helped him settle into English football after his move from Spanish side Rayo Vallecano.

All of this is helping fans have a better connection with the players, and one small tweak has been to starting holding a team huddle right by the travelling supporters in away games. No team has more away points in the Premier League than Liverpool and Alexander Isak has scored in six straight away trips in all competitions.

It helps that the football is more exciting, too. Isak has scored 10 for the season already and looks a completely different player to the unfit striker that was bereft of confidence last term and managed only four goals.

Florian Wirtz has also been revived and this week publicly thanked Iraola – and his Germany boss Klopp – for helping him rediscover the levels which saw him earn a £116million move to Anfield.

The list goes on: Alexis Mac Allister looked like a man whose best days were behind him but now is back playing like the midfielder who won the World Cup in 2022, while Jeremy Jacquet looks a Rolls-Royce defender in the making. Milos Kerkez is slowly trending upwards.

And then there is Iraola’s faith in youth. Rio Ngumoha, 18, and Trey Nyoni, 19, have been trusted to perform by the new boss. Lewis Koumas and James McConnell have been getting the nod in squads ahead of senior pros Federico Chiesa and Wataru Endo.

Iraola, who is superstitious and tapes his fingers before games for this reason, knows the significance of this week: having thrashed Manchester United and won away in Europe against a decent Club Bruges side, a Merseyside derby win would complete a trio of fantastic results.

Florian Wirtz this week thanked Iraola for helping him rediscover his best level

Iraola has shown faith in youngsters including winger Rio Ngumoha - and he has been repaid handsomely

‘It’s a little bit like here – you know a lot of people on the other side,’ he said on Friday, comparing the clash with Everton to the derby between his boyhood club Athletic Club, of Bilbao, and Real Sociedad, of San Sebastian.

‘I have a lot of friends who are Real Sociedad and they have a lot of friends who are from Athletic.

‘There is always banter throughout the season and everyone wants to finish above them and win the games against them. It’s quite a natural rivalry. The relationship between them is normally quite good but everyone wants to win that game.'

Iraola went on to add that he is very happy in Liverpool, which he described as an ‘easy’ way of life. It will certainly feel that way if he completes the perfect double of beating Manchester United and Everton in the same week.

Sports.title: Inside Stoke City's turnaround under Mark Robins: How they cleansed 'toxic' dressing room, the medical guru who stopped their injury crisis, a transfer expert armed with Brighton's secrets - and why they won't fall away like last season
Sports.content:
Stoke City have been here before. They know how it feels to be among the pace-setters, striding towards the place where they once belonged. They know, too, how easy it is to fall away. At this stage last season, their first full campaign under Mark Robins, they sat second in the Championship. Would it be their year, a return to the top flight after seven years away, seven years in which they had finished in the bottom half of the Championship every season? It would not. They won three of their last 20 matches, none of their last six, and ended up 17th. Victory for Stoke – who finished in the top half of the Premier League for three seasons in a row in the 2010s, remember – over Millwall on Wednesday night, their fifth on the bounce, sees them second again. Beat West Ham this weekend, who haven't won in six, and it's time to dream. Will this be their year? Before a ball was kicked, Opta’s supercomputer had Stoke as the most likely team to be relegated. Robins, however, said things ‘felt different’. Speaking to those around the club this week, there’s a genuine belief they are. Not that anyone would have thought it three months ago, when a 4-1 thumping at Wolves – a third straight defeat to start the season – left them bottom. Club bosses wondered whether a change might be needed. The mood in the stands was starting to shift. There had been little appetite to sack Robins in the summer, but now the questions of whether they made the right call crossed a few minds. Despite a dismal end to last season, and a poor start to this, Stoke stuck with boss Mark Robins - a decision that is paying off Jack McGlynn leads the celebrations during Stoke's 2-1 victory over Millwall in midweek. They sit second in the Championship

Your browser does not support iframes.

After spending £30million on players over the summer, selling them the vision of what the club was building under Robins, it was felt sacking him before the window had even closed would be a dreadful look. Stoke stuck by Robins, beat Norwich on deadline day in a gutsy backs-to-the-wall performance, and haven’t looked back since. One thing that did change after the Wolves defeat, even if it wasn't the manager, was the formation. Sorba Thomas, the club’s leading scorer last season, was sold to Hull for £8million. Not only did it allow Robins to cash in on a player who made it clear he wanted to leave, but also to switch to a wing-back system that now gets the best out of the squad. Robins and sporting director, Jon Walters, the former Stoke striker who felt the brunt of fan frustration following their collapse last term, have gone about building a club and culture that can finally succeed. The past few seasons have been spent shipping out plenty of rubbish and bringing in players with the right character and mentality. Insiders talk about how ‘toxic’ the dressing room was just a couple of years ago, and how the standards set were ‘ridiculously low’. A staggering injury crisis helped wreck their promotion hopes last season, so this summer the club revamped the entire medical department. Damian Roden, the head of sports science during their Premier League days, returned as head of medical and performance. The club’s Premier League heroes of yesteryear, the likes of Ryan Shawcross and Robert Huth, have hailed Roden as one of the key factors in them finishing ninth three times on the spin under Mark Hughes. Roden’s periodisation model, which adjusts training volume and intensity to keep players at their freshest for match day, underpins Stoke’s weekly schedule. He’s been joined in the medical bay by Matt Ratcliffe and Mark Sertori, who spent more than a decade at Manchester City and was recently head performance for Roma. So far, Stoke have only had a couple of muscle injuries. John Coates, co-owner of Stoke (left), and sporting director Jon Walters have found a formula that is working as the club chase a return to the Premier League George Hirst scores the second of two goals against Millwall. The son of Sheffield Wednesday legend David has been working with Robins, a former striker, on his finishing The change in the Football League’s financial restrictions from the old-school Profit & Sustainability Rules, which capped losses over a rolling three-year period, to the new Squad Cost Ratio that allows clubs to spend a percentage of their revenue, has been a gamechanger for the Potters. Suddenly, the shackles are off. Stoke have owners in the Coates family who put in as much money as they can. They recently opened a new £12m first-team building at their Clayton Wood training ground, which boasts a gym, swimming pool, hydrotherapy and cryotherapy suites and a tactics room for video analysis. Now, they can spend on the squad too without worrying about being hamstrung by losses from previous years. They hope to bring in more players in January. The squad value has soared from around £30m a few years ago to more than £100m now. Stoke are also finally starting to reap the rewards of their bespoke data-led recruitment model, following in the footsteps of Brighton and Brentford. Like those two clubs, Stoke’s owner John Coates – son of Peter, who founded bet365 – has vast experience in the gambling industry. Their head of recruitment Ian Torrance helped set up Southampton’s ‘Black Box’ scouting database and used data from Tony Bloom’s Jamestown Analytics during his time at Italian side Como. Nearly all their signings this summer have hit the ground running. Ethan Galbraith, brought in from Swansea in a deal worth up to £10m, already looks like one of the best midfielders in the Championship. Jack McGlynn, one of two players signed from the MLS alongside Luca Bombino, has been another revelation in midfield and already has five league goals. Justin Devenny brings Premier League experience from Crystal Palace. Defender Luke Graham, snaffled from Dundee for £2m, has been a rock at the back and has earned his first Scotland call-up. Former captain and centre back Shawcross, one of Robins’ first-team coaches, has worked extensively with Graham, analysing video clips. Ethan Galbraith, brought in from Swansea in a deal worth up to £10m, already looks like one of the best midfielders in the Championship McGlynn, signed from the MLS, has been another revelation in midfield Robins, a former Manchester United front man, has been doing one-to-one work with striker George Hirst, who joined for an initial £6m from Ipswich. That’s paying off, too. Hirst scored the winner against Birmingham last weekend and both goals against Millwall in midweek. Stoke paid compensation to hire Arsenal Under 21s coach Max Porter, who helped bring through Myles Lewis-Skelly, Ethan Nwaneri and Max Dowman with the Gunners. He is in charge of how Stoke move the ball in possession – and appears to be doing a fine job. The big question, especially after last season’s tail-off, is whether they can sustain this form. Stoke are, on the face of it, overperforming their underlying numbers. Opta’s expected table, which calculates where a side should be based on their expected goals (xG), has Stoke 16th. The feeling inside the club, however, is that in games where Stoke took an early lead and looked to defend it, it was always likely their opponents would rack up shots and xG. If you look at Stoke’s rolling xG average, too, Robins’ side are starting to consistently create more than their opponents. Even if they were getting lucky earlier in the season, they aren’t anymore. Their first-half performance against fellow promotion chasers Birmingham was hailed by those inside the club as the best Stoke have played in years.

Your browser does not support iframes.

No goalkeeper has kept as many clean sheets as Viktor Johansson, one of the most reliable stoppers in the division Insiders feel the squad now has the depth to deal with any injuries that do come their way. Midfielder Djibril Soumare came off against Birmingham and is expected to be out for a while but they have plenty of cover. Galbraith missed two games and Stoke won them both. Fans, for the first time in years, are going into matches expecting to win. They have one of the meanest defences in the Championship. No goalkeeper has kept as many clean sheets as Viktor Johansson, one of the most reliable stoppers in the division. Stoke’s realistic aim is to finish in the play-offs. They have 35 points so far and know the average to finish in the top eight is around 69. It would need near-relegation form not to achieve that from their last 29 games. Stoke have been here before. This time it feels different.

Sports.title: How Southampton showed a lack of 'class' in bitter win over Middlesbrough after Spygate scandal: Star taunts fans with celebration and Kim Hellberg mocked to leave Tonda Eckert angry at his own club
Sports.content:
Southampton embarrassed themselves in their first meeting with Middlesbrough since the Spygate scandal as tempers flared at St Mary’s.

The club conducted themselves disgracefully in a bitter reunion six months on from their ejection from last season’s Championship play-off final.

Ryan Manning tucked James Bree’s cutback past Radek Vitek on 59 minutes to open the scoring for Saints before attacker Finn Azaz brought the contest to boiling point.

The former Boro forward scored Southampton’s second goal late on and then ran the length of the pitch to goad the away supporters by pretending to cry.

It sparked a fracas as Azaz and Will Lankshear - who wasn’t even at Boro last season when tensions were at their highest between the clubs - squared up, while travelling fans tried to get over the barricade.

Speaking after the match, Azaz said: 'They sang about me home and away last season, so I was just waiting for my moment to get one back. I have no regrets whatsoever.'

In a bitter reunion, Ryan Manning tucked James Bree’s neat cutback past Radek Vitek on 58 minutes before Azaz added a second as Southampton remained unbeaten at home in 10 months. Saints, though, were needlessly provocative throughout.

The scenes calmed post-match but Southampton’s off-field operation humiliated the club - taking their celebration too far.

Southampton's Finn Azaz mocked Middlesbrough's fans by pretending to cry after scoring

His celebration - in their first meeting since last season's 'Spygate' - sparked a brawl, with Azaz being booked

Hellberg cried in his press conference at Southampton last season when Boro lost in the play-offs semi-final before being reinstated. Saints reminded him of that incident by playing Oasis' Stop Crying Your Heart Out over the speakers. Throughout the match, the Saints fans sang: 'We saw you cry on the tele.'

Shamelessly, they added a box of tissues to the podium in the press conference room, which mortified Eckert, who removed them before Hellberg gave his post-match remarks.

‘I hope everyone who came here from the Middlesbrough staff knows that these things don't come from me,' Eckert said after removing the box of tissues, having stared at them for 20 seconds.

‘Everything you do in defeat and if you win you do in class and I try to do that. I hope that there's an appreciation that this doesn't come from me.’

Hellberg added: 'In general, those who show more emotions and stand up for what is right are brave people. Hiding behind people and being afraid of emotions, that's the problem we have in the world a little bit.

'We have to hide from everything, how people are feeling, mental health and everything. It’s important we stand up for that – I'm not afraid of showing feelings.'

Saints beat Middlesbrough in last season’s play-off semi-final but were booted out by the EFL four days before the final after Daily Mail Sport revealed Southampton had sent their very own Johnny English to spy on Boro’s training sessions.

Both managers called for an armistice before the match but that memo clearly hadn't reached the Southampton marketing team, who posted an inflammatory video on social media.

Hellberg cried in his press conference at Southampton last season and a box of tissues were shamelessly added to the podium in the press conference room after today's match

The uncouth 79-second film mocked Boro, with the narrator declaring, ‘they got another go, their story continued’ over footage of Oli McBurnie’s winning goal for Hull City in the play-off final was also projected onto the big screen just eight minutes before kick-off.

'I didn't like the video this morning,’ Eckert said. If we look back a couple of months, the reality is both clubs have lost.

‘One club has lost off the pitch, and the other club has lost on the pitch. It’s an episode that is good to close for both clubs to move forward.

‘It’s time to move on at one point. For me, that episode from last year is closed. I've apologised. I've apologised to Kim (Hellberg). I've invited him for a drink. I just hope that we can do everything we do with class.'

Considering Southampton started this season on minus four points for the breaches, their supporters’ staggering endorsement of the cheating was as indiscreet as the espionage itself.

‘We’ll spy when we want,’ sang the Southampton fans – a reminder of when their spy kid tried to conceal himself behind a tree near Middlesbrough’s training ground to film their training session. The EFL discovered three further spying missions on investigation.

Southampton fully embraced their cheats tag as they claimed three points, responding to chants of ‘you cheating b*******, you know what you are’ with sarcastic applause.

Victory moves Saints within four points of Middlesbrough, who remain top of the table going into the weekend but could slip down as far as fifth. Sadly, that was overshadowed by their crass conduct.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso tells angry Chelsea fans to back Wesley Fofana after they told him to 'f*** off' during desperate defeat by Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso tells angry Chelsea fans to back Wesley Fofana after they told him to 'f*** off' during desperate defeat by Nottingham Forest

Xabi Alonso called on Chelsea’s fans to support Wesley Fofana after their away end spent their latest defeat chanting for their own player to get out of their club.

Fofana started against Nottingham Forest after apologising for the unauthorised interview he had conducted with a French YouTube channel. The content of that chat included him laughing off how he missed the penalty which condemned Chelsea to their Carabao Cup exit at Liverpool.

From the first minute at the City Ground, he was booed on the ball and subjected to abusive singing from Chelsea’s supporters, who chanted: ‘F*** off Fofana, you’re not wanted here.’

Fofana went on to give away a penalty by fouling his former team-mate Liam Delap and was then replaced by Levi Colwill, who had been dropped from the line-up instead of the Frenchman.

From the first minute at the City Ground, Fofana was booed on the ball and subjected to abusive singing from Chelsea’s fans, who chanted: ‘F*** off Fofana, you’re not wanted here'

Alonso confirmed he had not yet spoken with Fofana after full-time and added at his post-match press conference on the fans: ‘We need to support everyone because we need everyone. We need the fans, we need the players, we need to stick together because if not, things will get more complicated. We need to help. We need to go through this together.’

Alonso also would not confirm if he will leave Fofana out of Chelsea’s next game at home to Crystal Palace on Wednesday despite what turned into an ugly night here for his team.

‘We are going through a difficult moment of confidence, things are not clicking, not going the way we want,’ Alonso added. ‘We know in football, this can change quickly or can continue. It's down to us to work to find those solutions to have a better feeling on the pitch and to get better results because that's what we need.

Forest manager Oliver Glasner added: ‘We were struggling at the beginning to score the goals, especially here at the City Ground. We could see the progress but we couldn't get the results in many other games and now it's of course to keep working. Just 12 games played with 12 points so it's still not satisfying for us. Many games to go and for us it's to stay humble and keep working.’

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso is CONFUSING his Chelsea stars: Blues boss must take his share of the blame as chaos threatens to engulf the club again after deserved defeat by Nottingham Forest, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Xabi Alonso is CONFUSING his Chelsea stars: Blues boss must take his share of the blame as chaos threatens to engulf the club again after deserved defeat by Nottingham Forest, writes IAN LADYMAN

It is not yet December and already chaos threatens to engulf Chelsea once more.

A bright start to the season under Xabi Alonso was, it transpires, merely a hazy, late summer mirage. Winter, it seems, will bring only a new version of a classic modern Chelsea discontent.

A coach who has started to do strange things – Alonso selected midfielder Moises Caicedo at centre-half here for the first time in his seven-year club career – a fanbase turning on everyone from the owners to the players and a team slowly getting disorientated on a dismally familiar carousel of selection changes.

It is Chelsea rebooted but just with the same stories written by and for different people. How dismal it must feel for those with this great club in their hearts.

Here on a misty and rainy night at the City Ground, nobody suffered more in Chelsea colours than central defender Wesley Fofana.

Harangued throughout by his own travelling fans for a foolish and unauthorised midweek YouTube interview in which he seemed to make light of missing a penalty in the Carabao Cup defeat at Liverpool, the Frenchman was hauled off soon after conceding a penalty that allowed Morgan Gibbs-White to stretch Nottingham Forest’s lead to two goals early in the second half.

Wesley Fofana was hauled off soon after conceding a penalty that allowed Morgan Gibbs-White to stretch Nottingham Forest’s lead to two goals early in the second half

Fofana was harangued throughout by his own travelling fans for an unauthorised interview in which he seemed to make light of missing a penalty in the Carabao Cup defeat at Liverpool

‘You are not wanted here,’ sang the Chelsea fans and after this they may get their wish. For his own sake, it may be a while before we see the young defender again.

At that stage of the night, Chelsea actually still had hope. Half-time substitute Emmanuel Emegha had just pulled a goal back with his team’s first shot on target of the whole night. He was to get another right at the death, too.

But having started the game with a fabulous fifth minute volley from the Brazilian Igor Jesus – it came off his shin but that doesn’t matter – Forest had the look of a team with their opponents’ measure all evening and that was how it played out. And when Gibbs-White scored his second of the game to make it 3-1 with less than 20 minutes left, Chelsea’s night was pretty much over.

Alonso must certainly take his share of the blame here. Caicedo is his best midfielder but was played out of position with England’s Levi Colwill left on the bench.

Put simply, it backfired. Chelsea’s defending did not improve on recent efforts and in midfield, where they were outplayed by Forest’s Xaver Schlager and James McAtee, they missed the Ecuadorian desperately.

More widely Alonso’s Premier League record – six wins from 12 games – is now worse than that of Liam Rosenior when he was sacked back in April. Their six defeats are one more than Manchester United. And this at a time when Chelsea are playing but once a week. No European competition and out of the Carabao Cup, the Spaniard has plenty of time with his players on the training field. What is he doing with it? Confusing everybody, it would seem, for what Chelsea presented here was a jumble. How they lost by only a goal was a miracle in itself. They deserved nothing.

Forest had come in to the game with issues of their own. Their coach Oliver Glasner had accused his international squad of not making enough effort with their English. Early on their football spoke for them as McAtee spread the play with a wonderful fifth minute pass, Daniel Munoz crossed and Jesus rose to volley his second league goal of the season high past Emiliano Martinez quite wonderfully.

Caicedo is Alonso's best midfielder but the Ecuadorian was played out of position by the Chelsea manager with England’s Levi Colwill left on the bench

Alonso’s Premier League record – six wins from 12 games – is now worse than that of Liam Rosenior when he was sacked back in April

What followed for the rest of the first half did not match that quality. Over time, Alonso’s team did find a way into the game territorially but a free-kick routine that ended with Morgan Rogers ballooning ten yards over the bar perhaps summed their efforts up as indeed did the fact they ended the opening period having managed only three touches inside the Forest box.

Replacing the ineffectual Danny Welbeck with Emegha at the interval brought Chelsea some shape at least. Welbeck had been peripheral. Forest were the team to kick on, though, and when Fofana slipped catastrophically to allow Liam Delap through in the 50th minute, he then brought him down. Gibbs-White slotted in the penalty and Chelsea were in big trouble.

With the away end threatening revolt, Alonso’s team somehow fashioned a lifeline goal from nowhere within four minutes. Pedro Neto’s speculative shot struck Forest defender Jair Cunha on the thigh and when the ball dropped to Emegha, he controlled it instinctively and found the corner.

With Fofana soon withdrawn to doubtless protect his own sanity, Chelsea’s fans now had nothing else to do but support their team. The visitors’ sense of desperation certainly made it a better game but what followed only served to damn Chelsea even more.

Far from the goal imbuing them with the impetus and belief to rescue the game, Alonso’s players somehow allowed Forest to take the initiative once more. There was a fatuous and unsuccessful penalty appeal for handball against Cunha – he had his arms clamped to his side when Rogers’ cross struck him – but precious little else.

And when the generally excellent Austrian Schlager threaded the needle to find Gibbs-White through a crowd with 17 minutes left, the England forward lifted the ball over the advancing Martinez to present a two-goal margin once again.

Chelsea subsequently offered almost nothing only to score – this time with an Emegha header – with two minutes left. Had they added an equaliser it would have been wholly unjust. They didn’t.

Sports.title: Nathan Lyon is revealed to be Australia star who suggested ball-tampering in first Test after Sandpapergate, as scandal takes new twist
Sports.content:
Nathan Lyon is revealed to be Australia star who suggested ball-tampering in first Test after Sandpapergate, as scandal takes new twist

Australia’s ball-tampering scandal has taken yet another twist after off-spinner Nathan Lyon was named as the player who suggested using mints on the ball in their first post-Sandpapergate Test match, against Pakistan in Dubai in October 2018.

Less than seven months after the Australians were caught using sandpaper to achieve reverse swing on their now infamous tour of South Africa, Lyon allegedly asked team-mates in the UAE: ‘Who’s got the mints? Who’s doing the ball today?’

According to SEN broadcaster Gerard Whateley, he was put in his place by Travis Head, who told him: ‘You’re f****** kidding me. We’re not doing that shit again.’

Tim Paine, who had taken over the captaincy from the banned Steve Smith, ensured the mints or lollies – the Australian word for sweets – never reached the field of play, while Justin Langer, who had replaced Darren Lehmann as head coach, later screamed at the entire team for even considering the ploy.

Usman Khawaja, who played in that game, confirmed this week – without naming Lyon – that the incident had taken place, telling The Grade Cricketer podcast he remembered Langer’s ‘blow-up’.

He added: ‘I remember it was very targeted at one player, then the whole team. What I remember from it was like: “If any of you guys ever even think about this again, you will not play for Australia again.”’

Nathan Lyon (second from right) has been identified as the Australia star who suggested ball-tampering again in the first Test after the Sandpapergate scandal erupted - pictured during that match against Pakistan in Dubai

But Khawaja confirmed that the player in question had also played at Cape Town, where the sandpaper controversy first blew up, which narrowed the field to six players, two of whom were Khawaja himself and Paine.

A subsequent investigation by Australian media outlet Code Sports, who spoke to ‘multiple sources’, emboldened them to name Lyon as the guilty party. A Cricket Australia spokesperson said that the independent forum announced last week by David Boon and Todd Greenberg, CA’s chair and chief executive, was ‘the appropriate place for any information to be provided’.

The latest bombshell came on the day CA laid out the forum’s terms of reference, which will include the Test team’s ‘ball-management practices’ during the 2017-18 Ashes, when England’s players suspected the Australians were breaking the laws en route to a 4–0 win.

In the aftermath of the Cape Town Test, Daily Mail Sport revealed that David Warner had told the England players during post-series drinks that he had tampered with the ball.

But the forum’s scope will not extend beyond the South Africa series, which means the mints incident in Dubai will not be investigated.

The forum, which will be overseen by Fiona McLeod, a prominent barrister, will remain open for six weeks. And while its broad findings will be made public, individual testimony will remain confidential. No player or backroom staff member is obliged to take part, and there will be no retrospective punishments.

Boon said: ‘We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority.’

Meanwhile, Lyon has been left out of Australia’s squad for the four-Test series against New Zealand, starting at Perth on December 9, with the spin-bowling role going to the uncapped Western Australian Corey Rocchiccioli.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta: Arsenal's next step is to break 'unprecedented' Man City record he helped set
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has challenged his Arsenal players to become record-breakers.

Manchester City wrote their names into the history books when they won the 2017/18 title with 100 points when Arteta was on Pep Guardiola’s coaching staff. The Gunners won their first title in 22 years last season and are desperate to begin a period of sustained success by winning the Premier League back-to-back.

Arteta spelt out his dreams and ambitions also of winning the title this season in real style with another record points haul and they have got off to a storming start with nine wins from their first 11 games. And the Gunners boss believes his team have got more levels to come - and he firmly believes history is within their grasp.

Arteta said: “We haven't hit the level yet that City did and I was there when we did 100 points. And that's the level that is unprecedented and every record I was beating with that.

‌



“And that's what we have to aim for because that's what I expect that all the clubs and all the squads with the capacity they have in this league are going to take us this season or the next few seasons.

Black Friday special! Click here to sign up to Mirror+ for just £1 a month!

“You want to be the best version that you can and that's something that's been done only once in the league and that's what we want to do.

‌



“It's going to be extremely difficult but we want to be as close as that because that's what is going to increase the probability of winning the championship again.”

Former Arsenal boss Arsene Wenger, acknowledged as the best manager in the club’s history, famously set his players a target of going a whole season unbeaten. They failed at their first attempt in 2002/03 but then enjoyed the Invincibles campaign when they were crowned champions in 2003/04 without losing a Premier League game.

Targets generally inspire players and ironically the 2017/18 season fell into the years in which City have been found guilty of breaking Premier League rules.

But there can be no doubt that City’s rivalry with Arsenal over the past five years has inspired both teams and pushed them to new levels. It has also brought out a new title rivalry between Arsenal and City which has mirrored the likes of City and Liverpool, Manchester United and Chelsea down the years among others.

‌



Arteta said: “You admire the opposition, the level that they have and how they do things. You certainly learn from that, and that inspires you to go to a different level.

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta coached the Manchester City team which broke the 100 point barrier (Image: GETTY )

“That's the level that City have brought to this league, which is unprecedented. What they've done is unprecedented in this league.

“The scenario does change. You feel it in the atmosphere, you feel it in the stadium. It has a different meaning sometimes.

‌



“Like when we play a derby, there is something in the atmosphere and the passion people feel about the game. The energy is a bit different. That is something you sense, because football is about that.

“Yes, that's what we want: to win every game. But obviously we talk about the highest opposition that this league has seen and how we've been competing with them. But for sure, it's only what we want to do is to win the game.

“When we play the home games against big teams, that becomes crucial in the title challenge. We know how important those home games are to make the difference, but obviously the second part, we're in November, and we know how long we have to play, but that's for every single team.

“We cannot control what the opponents are going to do; we just need to give ourselves the best version, and I'm sure the atmosphere is going to be incredible on Sunday, and we need to enjoy and embrace those kinds of games and go for it.”

‌



View 3 Images Mikel Arteta helped deliver Arsenal's first league title since 2004 - but now wants more (Image: Getty)

Arteta is also expected to have face-to-face talks with Arsenal owner Josh Kroenke in the next few weeks ahead of the January window with the Gunners looking to strengthen.

But Arteta insists any move in January is already being plotted as they look to bolster their squad for a challenge at home and abroad.

Arteta added: “We don’t wait to talk about these things only when it is face to face. That is why we have great phones now. We can have constant communication between us.

‌



“But it is always great when he is around. There is a different feeling. You can spend some time together and it’s great to understand how he is doing as well. He will be around.”
