Ghana News.title: Newmont Ahafo South Mine named Mining Company of the Year at 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards
Ghana News.content:
Newmont Ghana Gold Ltd – Ahafo South Mine has been named Mining Company of the Year at the 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards held in Accra on Friday, November 27.

The mine also emerged winner in several other categories, including Best Green Mine, Best Performer in Environmental Management, Best Performer in Innovation and Best Performer in Exploration (Brownfield).

The awards recognised outstanding achievements by mining companies, individuals, service providers, students and other stakeholders in Ghana’s mining industry.

In the Best Green Mine category, Newmont Ahafo South Mine emerged winner, with AngloGold Ashanti Obuasi Mine and Gold Fields Ghana Ltd – Tarkwa Mine placing first and second runners-up, respectively.

AngloGold Ashanti Iduapriem Ltd won the Corporate Social Investment Project of the Year award, ahead of Gold Fields Ghana Ltd – Tarkwa Mine and Newmont Ahafo South Mine.

Newmont Ahafo North Mine was adjudged Best Mining Company in Diversity and Inclusion, with Gold Fields Ghana Ltd – Tarkwa Mine and AngloGold Ashanti Iduapriem placing first and second runners-up, respectively.

Newmont Ahafo South Mine also won Best Performer in Environmental Management. AngloGold Ashanti Obuasi Mine was named first runner-up, while Asanko Gold Mine Ltd, Newmont Ahafo North Mine and Zijin Golden Ridge Ltd jointly took the second runner-up position.

In the Best Female Miner of the Year (Technical) category, Ing. Mrs Linda Ofori Adjei Acheampong emerged winner, followed by Sandra Anokye Koranteng and Rebecca Manteaw Bekoe as first and second runners-up, respectively.

For the non-technical category, Habeebi Jillian Opoku Ansah was named first runner-up, while Stephanie Danso placed second runner-up. No winner was indicated in the awards list.

Newmont Ahafo South Mine continued its strong showing by winning Best Performer in Innovation. Golden Star Wassa Ltd and Perseus Mining (Ghana) Ltd jointly placed first runners-up, while AngloGold Ashanti Iduapriem was named second runner-up.

Sulemanu Koney received the Lifetime Achievement Award.

Underground Mining Alliance won Best Performer in Contract Mining, with Yellow Power International placing first runner-up.

Interplast Ltd was adjudged Best Performer in Local Manufacturing of Mine Inputs, followed by Carmeuse Lime Products Ghana Ltd and B5 Plus Limited as first and second runners-up, respectively.

Sandvik Mining and Construction Ghana Ltd won Best Performer in Mine Supplies and Support Services. Carmeuse Lime Products Ghana Ltd and Epiroc Equipment Ghana Ltd placed first and second runners-up, respectively.

Samuel Boakye Pobee was named Mining Personality of the Year, with Alex Kofi Annin and Alex Kofi Oduro taking the first and second runner-up positions, respectively.

Asante Gold Bibiani Ltd emerged winner in the Best Performer in Occupational Health and Safety category, ahead of Golden Star Wassa Ltd and Adamus Resources Ltd.

Desimone Limited won Best Performer in Engineering, Procurement, Construction and Management (EPCM), with DRA Ghana Ltd and Wayoe Engineering and Construction Ltd placing first and second runners-up, respectively.

Nana Boakye Danquah Yiadom was adjudged Best Mining Reporter, followed by Timothy Ngnenbe and Caleb Wuninti Ziblim as first and second runners-up, respectively.

In the Best Student in Inter-Mines Essay Contest category, Nhyiraba Anowa Afful Maame emerged winner, with Elliot Corey Ameyaw Hayfron and Nana Ekua Brown Josephine placing first and second runners-up, respectively.

Nicholas Addae Okyere was named Best Level 200 Student (Male), while Grace Asantewaa won the Best Level 200 Student (Female) award.

Sylvester Yenzanya received the award for Best Postgraduate Student in Research.

Perseus Mining (Ghana) Ltd won Best Performer in Local Content, with Asanko Gold Mine Ltd and Gold Fields Ghana Ltd – Tarkwa Mine placing first and second runners-up, respectively.

The Financial Deal of the Year award went to Zijin Golden Ridge Ltd, Absa Bank and Ecobank Ghana Ltd. Stanbic Bank and Engineers and Planners Ltd were named first runners-up.

Newmont Ahafo South Mine won Best Performer in Exploration (Brownfield), with Asanko Gold Mine Ltd and Golden Star Wassa Ltd placing first and second runners-up, respectively.

Asanko Gold Ghana Ltd was adjudged Best Performer in Exploration (Greenfield), followed by Cape Coast Resources Ltd and Danampco Company Ltd as first and second runners-up, respectively.

Ghana News.title: Lands Ministry, Newmont set up working group to strengthen mining partnership
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Hon. Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah has inaugurated a six-month Joint Ghana–Newmont Working Group to address concerns relating to the fiscal, regulatory and operational environment affecting the mining company's investments in the country.

Inaugurating the group on Friday, November 27, 2026, the Minister said the initiative was aimed at creating a structured platform for dialogue, resolving areas of concern and strengthening the partnership between the Ministry and Newmont.

He acknowledged the company's contribution to Ghana's mining industry through investment, employment, local procurement, technology transfer and revenue generation, but stressed that the Ministry remained committed to reforms that would secure greater national benefits from the country's mineral resources.

The Minister explained that the Working Group would examine Newmont's concerns, review the relevant laws and policies, assess the cumulative impact of recent fiscal and regulatory measures and recommend practical ways to improve compliance and operational efficiency. Its priority areas include the revised royalty framework and investment competitiveness, contract mining and local participation, gold sales and pricing arrangements, foreign exchange issues, and the development of a more predictable mining investment environment.

Newmont's co-chair welcomed the initiative, describing it as an important opportunity to strengthen understanding and work through issues affecting the company's operations and future investments in Ghana. He disclosed that the company had already committed US$4 million for 2027 to advance new projects and extensions, with further major investment decisions expected towards the end of that year.

The group is expected to submit a priority issues assessment, workstream recommendations and a final report with a clear implementation roadmap identifying agreed actions, responsible institutions and timelines.

The Committee includes representatives from the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources, Minerals Commission, Ministry of Finance, Attorney-General's Department, Ghana Revenue Authority and Environmental Protection Authority, alongside Newmont representatives.

Ghana News.title: Government targets 2027 completion of Azumah Nelson Sports Complex
Ghana News.content:
Construction work on the Azumah Nelson Sports Complex has resumed, with the government setting 2027 as the target for completing the long-delayed facility.

The National Youth Authority (NYA), which is overseeing the project, says efforts are underway to accelerate construction, with the football pitch expected to be ready for use by the end of this year.

Other major components, including the spectator stands, tartan tracks and pavements, are also being worked on as part of the broader development of the complex.

To support the renewed construction drive, the Authority has committed GH¢5 million from its 2026 capital expenditure to the project and made provision for an additional GH¢10 million in its 2027 allocation.

The Chief Executive Officer of the NYA, Osman Ayariga, said the project had encountered delays because the government inherited an existing contract with outstanding payments to the contractor.

Those financial obligations, he explained, had contributed to the suspension of work on the facility.

Mr Ayariga said the outstanding challenges had since been addressed sufficiently for the contractor to return to the site and resume construction.

He gave an assurance that the Authority would sustain the momentum to ensure the complex was completed within the government's 2027 target.

The resumption of work is expected to advance efforts to provide the area with a modern sporting facility, with the football pitch and other planned infrastructure forming key components of the development.

When completed, the complex is expected to provide facilities for sporting activities, including football and athletics.

Ghana News.title: Ken Ashigbey calls for mining industry excellence to become national standard
Ghana News.content:
Ing. Dr. Kenneth Ashigbey, Chief Executive Officer of the Chamber

The Convenor of the Media Coalition Against Illegal Mining (MCAM), Ing. Kenneth Ashigbey, has called for excellence, professionalism, discipline and commitment to safety in Ghana's mining industry to become standards embraced across the country's economy.

He said the mining industry's pursuit of excellence should extend beyond winning awards and recognising outstanding performance to influencing workplace practices, business growth, community development and national productivity.

Speaking at the 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards in Accra on Friday, November 27, Ing. Ashigbey said making excellence an everyday standard could significantly transform the mining industry and the country as a whole.

He urged industry players to envision a mining sector where workers returned safely to their families after every shift, businesses supplying mines expanded into competitive manufacturing, and mining communities became centres of economic opportunity.

“Excellency, truly, must become our everyday standard. If excellency tonight became our everyday standard across our entire industry, and indeed our country, imagine every mine worker return home safely to their family after every shift,” he said.

Ing. Ashigbey said the adoption of high standards across the mining value chain could also empower local businesses to grow beyond supplying mining companies and develop products capable of competing in markets across Africa and beyond.

He stressed the importance of creating an enabling environment for businesses to expand, innovate and contribute more meaningfully to the country's industrialisation agenda.

According to him, mining communities must also benefit from the economic activities generated by the sector, with young people in such communities having access to opportunities that enable them to build prosperous futures.

“Imagine every business is growing from supplying our mines to manufacturing products that competes successfully across Africa and beyond, imagine mining communities become centres for opportunity where young people can look forward to a prosperous future because mining has taken place in their communities,” he added.

The MCAM Convenor further called for the values that underpin excellence in mining to be replicated across other sectors of the economy.

He said discipline, innovation, professionalism and a strong safety culture were essential not only to mining operations but also to improving performance and productivity across Ghana's industries.

Ing. Ashigbey noted that the true significance of excellence lay in its ability to inspire continuous improvement, raise institutional standards and establish a culture in which quality performance became a norm rather than an occasional achievement.

“Imagine the discipline, innovation, professionalism, and commitment to safety that we strive for in mining becoming the standard across every sector of our national economy. That is the real promise of excellence,” he said.

He added that excellence should not be measured solely by achievements recorded in a particular year, but by the lasting impact it had on individuals, institutions and the wider society.

“It is not simply about being the best in a particular year, it is about raising standards, inspiring others and creating a culture in which continuous improvement become nature,” Ing. Ashigbey said.

The 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards brought together stakeholders in the mining sector to recognise outstanding achievements, promote responsible mining practices and celebrate excellence across the industry.

Ghana News.title: Ken Ashigbey urges mining industry to translate economic contributions into lasting development
Ghana News.content:
The Convenor of the Media Coalition Against Illegal Mining (MCAM), Ing. Kenneth Ashigbey, has called on Ghana's mining industry to ensure its substantial economic contributions translate into sustainable opportunities, improved livelihoods and lasting development for mining communities.

He said while the sector had demonstrated its capacity to generate significant revenue, support businesses and contribute to national development, its impact must ultimately be measured by the improvements it brings to the lives of workers, families and communities.

Speaking at the 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards in Accra on Friday, November 27, Ing. Ashigbey said the industry had made considerable progress through investment, technical expertise, innovation and responsible business practices.

He cited the sector's contribution to government revenue, local expenditure and social investment as evidence of its importance to Ghana's economy.

“As an industry, we have demonstrated what is possible, when we combine investment, technical expertise and innovation and responsible business practices,” he said.

According to him, the mining sector contributed GH¢23.1 billion in taxes in 2025, representing 28 per cent of Ghana's direct domestic tax revenue.

He also highlighted the industry's expenditure within the local economy, saying producing members of the Ghana Chamber of Mines spent approximately GH¢7.1 billion domestically, while investing GH¢88.6 million in social interventions in their host communities.

Ing. Ashigbey said the figures underscored the mining industry's contribution to national economic activity, government revenue mobilisation and community development.

However, he stressed that the significance of those contributions should not be assessed solely in monetary terms, but also by the extent to which they create opportunities and improve the welfare of people affected by mining operations.

“ These are definitely significant contributions, but beyond the figures, our workers, families, businesses and communities whose lives are touched by mining, our collective responsibility is to ensure that these contributions translate into sustainable opportunities and lasting development,” he said.

He said the industry had a responsibility to ensure that the wealth generated from mineral resources supported long-term development, particularly in communities where mining activities take place.

According to him, the benefits of mining should be reflected in improved living conditions, stronger local businesses, employment opportunities and investments that would continue to serve communities long after mining operations had ended.

Ing. Ashigbey further emphasised the importance of responsible business practices in ensuring that the sector's economic gains were accompanied by meaningful social benefits.

He said the Ghana Mining Industry Awards played an important role in promoting such standards by recognising companies and individuals whose performance demonstrated excellence, innovation and responsible operations.

“That is why the Ghana Mining Industry Awards truly matter,” he said.

He noted that the awards were not merely a platform for celebrating achievements within the industry, but also an opportunity to encourage higher standards, inspire innovation and reinforce the sector's commitment to responsible mining and sustainable development.

The 12th Ghana Mining Industry Awards brought together stakeholders in the mining sector to celebrate outstanding performance, innovation, safety, environmental stewardship and contributions to Ghana's mining industry.

Ghana News.title: Toxic dumping ground: Greenpeace finds UK retailers’ faulty returns at Agbogbloshie e-waste site
Ghana News.content:
An investigation by Greenpeace Africa and Unearthed has revealed that dozens of electrical appliances returned to major UK high-street brands, including Tesco, Argos and Asda, have ended up at the Agbogbloshie e-waste dump in Accra, a site notorious for toxic pollution.

Greenpeace is an independent global environmental organisation founded in 1971, known for investigating and exposing environmental abuse by governments and corporations through peaceful direct action and scientific research. The organisation operates in over 55 countries and refuses funding from governments, corporations or political parties to maintain its independence.

Many of the items found at Agbogbloshie, including toasters, slow-cookers and kettles, were still in their boxes and labelled as faulty returns by the stores. The heaps of appliances suggest they were shipped in bulk.

The findings were published on the eve of Black Friday, a period when industry research suggests one in five discounted items purchased are likely to be returned.

Exporting broken electrical goods to Africa is illegal in almost every circumstance, and UK law requires used items to be tested before being sold overseas.

However, the investigation found that returned goods are being sold off in bulk and shipped untested to Ghana. Faulty items returned to major retailers are likely sold through liquidation channels to "jobbers"—individuals and small businesses who buy goods by the pallet-load to extract value, including listing items on eBay or exporting them. Argos runs its own liquidation site, which recently auctioned six pallets of "small kitchen appliances RETURNS", described as "raw customer returns that have NOT been checked or tested for faults (mainly faulty)."

In Ghana, local shopkeepers told investigators that between 10 and 30 per cent of the goods they import are faulty, and many end up being dumped. The Agbogbloshie site, once ranked alongside Chernobyl as one of the most polluted places on earth, releases carcinogens through the burning of plastic.

Commenting on the findings, Greenpeace UK’s chief scientist, Dr Doug Parr, condemned the practice.

“Customers will be appalled to learn that, instead of being repaired or recycled, these faulty returns ended up in a notorious megadump leaching toxic run-offs that poison entire communities. This isn’t the circular economy, but long-range fly-tipping, and it’s shameful,” he said.

“There are laws meant to stop e-waste being dumped on low-income countries, yet this is happening anyway. Functioning and faulty items are bundled together into ‘unlucky dip’ pallets and shipped overseas, no questions asked. This is waste export in disguise, shifting the environmental and social costs of our throwaway economy onto countries like Ghana.”

Dr Parr called on retail giants to take responsibility for their returns and urged the environmental watchdog to launch a full investigation.

Following the findings, Tesco stated it had suspended its third-party e-waste management provider “with immediate effect” while it carries out a full audit.

Argos said it “takes these findings seriously and is reviewing the information provided,” while Asda, via the British Retail Consortium, described the reports as “deeply concerning.” However, none of the retailers directly responded to questions over whether faulty electrical returns were sold off through liquidation channels instead of being processed as e-waste.

Ghana News.title: 5.4m Ghanaians still practise open defecation
Ghana News.content:
An estimated 5.4 million Ghanaians still practise open defecation, while the country spends approximately $290 million annually to address poor sanitation, the Ministry of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs has disclosed.

The Deputy Minister of Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Rita Naa Odoley Sowah, who made this known at the 2026 National Commemoration of World Toilet Day in Bongo in the Upper East Region on November 19, 2026, described the situation as a national emergency requiring urgent and collective action.

“Nationally, 5.4 million Ghanaians still practise open defecation, inasmuch as we can see that it has drastically reduced,” she said.

The commemoration, held in partnership with WaterAid Ghana on the theme: “From Open Defecation to Open Opportunity through the Gender Lens”, brought together traditional authorities, government officials and development partners to renew commitments towards improving sanitation.

The deputy minister said the estimated $290 million spent annually on poor sanitation could otherwise be invested in critical infrastructure such as schools, health facilities and roads.

“That is money that could build classrooms, clinics and roads. So let me say plainly, this is not a small problem. It is a national emergency, and it has a woman's face,” she stressed.

She said the consequences of open defecation went beyond public health concerns, particularly affecting the safety, dignity and educational opportunities of women and girls.

“Before sunrise, a girl wakes up in her home without a toilet. She must wait for darkness or walk into the bush, afraid of snakes, strangers and being seen,” she said.

She explained that such experiences exposed girls to danger and sometimes prevented them from attending school, stressing that access to safe sanitation was essential to gender equality and human dignity.

Bongo's sanitation challenge

The deputy minister commended the Bongo Traditional Council and the District Assembly for taking steps to address the sanitation situation through the signing of a District Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) Compact and the development of a 10-year WASH Master Plan.

She said the government was committed to supporting sanitation interventions through the allocation of resources to Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs), with a proportion earmarked for sanitation.

“Bongo has chosen to act. Bongo signed a district WASH Compact.

The Assembly produced a 10-year comprehensive WASH Master Plan,” she said.

The Paramount Chief of the Bongo Traditional Area, Naba Baba Salifu Atamale Lemyaarum, said about 80 per cent of the district's population practised open defecation, according to the 2021 Population and Housing Census.

He said the situation was corroborated by the 2024 World Service Level Assessment conducted by WaterAid Ghana, which indicated that the district's open defecation rate was more than four times the national average of approximately 18 per cent.

“The irony, therefore, is that while the country is making progress in the fight against open defecation, Bongo appears to be moving in the opposite direction. This is a situation that my people and I cannot afford to take lightly,” he said.

Naba Lemyaarum said the traditional council had responded to the challenge by introducing the Bongo Sanitation Challenge following the signing of the district's WASH Compact in September 2025.

Under the initiative, he said, 690 household toilets had been constructed, representing an estimated investment of GH¢2 million and providing sanitation access to approximately 3,700 people.

“These figures represent much more than toilets constructed or money invested. They represent an investment in the local economy of Bongo, job creation for local artisans and expanded market opportunities for suppliers of building materials,” he stated.

He further disclosed that the traditional council had established a WASH Fund to support poor and vulnerable households in constructing household toilets and improving sanitation facilities in public places.

Naba Atamale said the traditional area, which had 42 communities under his supervision, was targeting the elimination of open defecation by 2030.

Equality and dignity

The WaterAid Ghana Country Director, Ewurabena Yany-Akufur, said sanitation was not merely an infrastructure issue but also a question of public health, equality and human dignity.

She said the absence of safe toilets disproportionately affected girls, pregnant women, older persons and persons with disabilities, adding that sanitation facilities must be safe, accessible, functional and properly maintained.

“A toilet is not a privilege. It is an essential service that everyone deserves,” she said.

She called for stronger local government delivery systems, effective regulation and sustained behavioural change to complement investments in sanitation infrastructure.

Call for collective action

The Upper East Regional Minister, Donatus Akamugri Atanga, called on all 15 municipal and district assemblies to prioritise sanitation, improve access to toilet facilities and intensify public education to promote healthy sanitation practices.

He said sustainable sanitation required collective commitment, behavioural change and local ownership, describing the inauguration of the Bongo WASH Fund Committee as a significant step towards mobilising resources for sanitation interventions.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
