World.title: Hardrock crowned champions!
World.content:
Hardrock FC are Castle Lager Premier Soccer League champions. The Kwekwe side beat FC Platinum 1-0 at Chahwanda Stadium to clinch the title in their debut season in the top flight, sparking wild celebrations in the mining town.

Prince Dube scored the only goal of the game in the first minute, finishing off a flowing team move laid on by Thubelihle Mavuso, to send Hardrock to 73 points, two clear of second-placed Scottland FC.

This story is for NewsDay subscribers.

World.title: Immigration seizes passports of seven Danish students at Zinasu conference
World.content:
THE Department of Immigration has confiscated passports belonging to seven Danish students who attended a Zimbabwe National Students Union (Zinasu) conference in Bulawayo this Saturday.

The development comes after the conference reportedly encountered disruptions, with police initially stopping the meeting over alleged failure to obtain clearance from the regulating authority in terms of the Maintenance of Peace and Order Act (MOPA).

According to the Zimbabwe Lawyers for Human Rights (ZLHR), Hillside Police had earlier indicated that the conference could not proceed because it did not have the required clearance.

This story is for NewsDay subscribers.

World.title: Makovora opens doors for amateur boxers to shine
World.content:
AFRICAN bantamweight champion Bongani Makovora is using his experience as a professional boxer and coach to create opportunities for aspiring fighters, with his new promotion, Talon Promotion, staging its inaugural event this evening.

The Open Boxing Tournament will be held at Vainona High School Hall, with amateur boxers set to showcase their talent in what marks the first event under the Talon Promotion banner.

The tournament gets underway at 18:00, with general admission pegged at US10 and VIP tickets going for US20.

This story is for NewsDay subscribers.

World.title: Highlanders row plunges PSL relegation battle into chaos
World.content:
THE Castle Lager Premier Soccer League has been thrown into complete chaos after the Premier Soccer League (PSL) was forced to postpone two decisive matches in the relegation battle following a standoff between Highlanders and their players over unpaid dues.

The postponement of the matches involving AGAMA FC and Highlanders at Wadzanai Stadium in Shamva, as well as Herentals and ZPC Kariba in Harare, has disrupted the final-day programme, leaving clubs scrambling to adjust their plans ahead of the rescheduled fixtures.

Highlanders reportedly failed to raise a team for their trip to Shamva after their players refused to fulfil the fixture amid a dispute over outstanding payments, with the situation further complicated by a notice of withdrawal of labour from the Footballers Union of Zimbabwe.

This story is for NewsDay subscribers.

World.title: Experts call for holistic response to girls’ HIV risk
World.content:
Local News

Vanessa Gonye · November 20, 2026

NEW HIV infections are significantly higher in adolescent girls compared to adolescent boys, raising concern over lack of empowerment of young girls and adolescent women.

Speaking to NewsDay, National Aids Council (NAC) chief executive officer Bernard Madzima said the issue also raised concern around teenage pregnancies and the inter-linkages.

“The data shows that the issues are socio-economic and among the most affected areas will be the traditional hotspots for HIV infections,” he said.

“So, the concern around teenage pregnancies also extends to new HIV infections and STIs [sexually transmitted infections] and economic issues, looking at even the young girls dropping out of school.”

He said these issues affected the empowerment of adolescent girls and to address them, the approach must be holistic and an issue of building resilience among young girls in all aspects.

“That is the approach which really would make sure that a young woman is empowered and that way we avoid teenage pregnancies and HIV infections,” Madzima said.

Also commenting on the issue, Community Working Group on Health (CWGH) executive director Itai Rusike said poverty drove young women to survival strategies, where early or transactional sex becomes a means of obtaining basic needs such as food and gifts.

He said early sexual debut, high rates of adolescent pregnancy and peak HIV acquisition overlap significantly in older adolescent girls and young women, indicating that the same unprotected or non-consensual sexual exposures driving teen pregnancies also expose minors and young women to HIV.

“Leaving school early significantly multiplies the risk of both early pregnancy and HIV acquisition and remaining in school acts as a protective barrier.

“Insufficient or delayed age-appropriate education leaves minors without the knowledge to navigate bodily autonomy, contraception or prevention.”

Rusike said restricted access to contraceptives and services translated to stigma, out-of-pocket transport costs and cultural misconceptions regarding parental consent for minors seeking reproductive health services hinder access.

He said deep-seated patriarchal norms dictated that men are solely responsible for sexual decision-making and that women should be passive participants in relationships.

“When a young woman is financially dependent on an older partner or engaged in transactional sex for survival or gifts, she holds very little social or economic leverage to insist on condom use without risking the relationship, financial support or facing physical violence.

“As CWGH, we take cognisance that empowering youths is not merely a social responsibility but a strategic investment for the future of our society, national development and economic prosperity.”

Rusike added that many Zimbabwean youths lacked access to information on general health, comprehensive sexuality education and reproductive health services, leading to higher rates of avoidable ill health, unintended pregnancies and STIs.

“The CWGH believes that it is crucial to address these health, social, economic and related challenges through targeted interventions that empower young people to take charge of their health, economic and social well-being,” he said.

Shamwari Ye Mwanasikana executive director Ekenia Chifamba said addressing teenage pregnancy required more than focusing on individual behaviour, adding that there must be deliberate efforts to prevent child marriage, address sexual and gender-based violence, strengthen child protection systems, promote comprehensive sexuality education and ensure that girls can access youth-friendly sexual and reproductive health services.

“Child marriage, sexual violence and coercion are significant contributory factors to teenage pregnancy and increased vulnerability to HIV among adolescent girls.

“These practices undermine girls’ bodily autonomy and their ability to make independent decisions about their sexual and reproductive health,” she said.

“In child marriages, particularly where there are significant age and power differences between partners, girls may have limited bargaining power to negotiate condom use, delay pregnancy or make decisions about when and whether to engage in sexual activity.

“Sexual violence and coercion further expose girls to unintended pregnancies, HIV and other sexually transmitted infections.”

Chifamba said Zimbabwe had made progress in integrating HIV testing, counselling, antiretroviral treatment and prevention of mother-to-child transmission services into antenatal healthcare.

“However, the availability of these services does not necessarily guarantee that adolescent girls can access them consistently, confidentially and without discrimination.”

According to Unicef, adolescent girls and young women remain highly vulnerable, with new HIV infections occurring at triple the rate of their male peers.

Adolescent pregnancy remains high at 22%.

In sub-Saharan Africa, adolescent girls and young women continue to carry a disproportionate burden of HIV.

According to the 2024 Global AIDS Update, 3 100 young women acquired HIV every week in 2023.

Behind these numbers are lives shaped by early marriage, poverty, violence and limited access to reliable health services.

World.title: PANELZ pushes US$5m to transform Zim arts
World.content:
Local News

Tendai Sauta · November 20, 2026

ZIMBABWE’S creative industries are seeking more than recognition in national development plans as they want a properly funded sector capable of creating jobs, generating income and competing on regional and international markets.

As preparations for the 2027 National Budget gather momentum, Tafadzwa Muzondo (TM), founder and executive chairperson of PANELZ, is urging the government to translate policy commitments to practical financial support, tax reforms and infrastructure investment.

In an interview with NewsDay Life & Style reporter Tendai Sauta (ND), Muzondo outlines the organisation’s proposals and what artists expect from Treasury.

ND: Why is PANELZ’s presentation to Parliament significant for the creative industries?

TM: Our recommendations were captured in the submissions considered by the Parliamentary Portfolio Committee on Sport, Recreation, Arts and Culture during the 2027 Pre-Budget Seminar in Bulawayo.

This is important because it gives the sector an opportunity to move beyond consultation towards concrete budget commitments.

We want the creative industries to be recognised as an economic sector contributing to employment, entrepreneurship and national development.

ND: What are the most urgent challenges facing Zimbabwean artists?

TM: The first is inadequate and unsustainable funding.

We need a structured Arts Development Fund that supports artistic production and enterprise development, rather than relying mainly on occasional grants.

Second, the cost of doing business is high.

Artists face licensing fees, levies, import duties and tax obligations that do not always reflect irregular creative-sector earnings.

Third, there is inadequate infrastructure.

Many community halls, theatres and performance spaces need rehabilitation and equipment.

ND: What tax reforms are you proposing for the 2027 budget?

TM: We want an expanded, clearly defined duty-relief schedule for creative equipment, including eligible spare parts and repair-related items.

We are proposing a 48-hour approval target for applications processed through the relevant authorities.

We also want a one-stop licensing system to simplify applications and payments. In addition, digital and presumptive taxation should be reviewed to accommodate small creative businesses whose income fluctuates from month to month.

ND: How should government finance the proposed Arts Development Fund?

TM: We are proposing that the fund draws revenue from existing economic activities rather than imposing additional taxes on citizens or artists.

Our suggested sources include a 2% share of tourism receipts or levies, 5% of radio licensing revenue, 5% of National Lottery proceeds and 10% of the proposed copyright levy.

We are also proposing an initial US$5 million injection for grants and loans, with the National Arts Council of Zimbabwe (NACZ) overseeing disbursement.

These are proposals that require Treasury assessment and appropriate legislative and administrative arrangements.

ND: How can artists outside Harare benefit from the proposed funding?

TM: We want a dedicated Creative and Cultural Industries financing window through institutions such as Empower Bank, the Women’s Bank and

SMEDCO.

Established artists should have access to loans to expand their businesses, while emerging artists should benefit from grants to develop their work.

Applications should also be accessible through provincial NACZ offices.

Rural communities, young people, women and persons with disabilities must not be excluded.

ND: What makes the 2027 budget transformative for artists?

TM: We want a funded Arts Development Fund, an expanded duty-relief schedule, simplified licensing, an operational Zimbabwe Film Commission and seed funding of US$500 000 for 10 provincial arts hubs.

We also want the proposed 30% local-content quota enforced and government institutions to pay creative service providers within 14 days.

Our guiding principle is that if the best can be achieved, good is not enough.

Recognition in policy documents must translate to opportunities, sustainable businesses and improved livelihoods.

ND: How will PANELZ assess whether the government delivers?

TM: We will monitor funding disbursement, the number of artists benefiting across provinces, licensing and duty-relief processing times, infrastructure rehabilitation and payment compliance.

We intend to publish progress updates and continue engaging Parliament where implementation falls short.

For us, the test of the 2027 budget will be whether it improves the working conditions and economic opportunities of Zimbabwean creatives.

World.content:
FINANCE minister Mthuli Ncube’s 2027 National Budget contains proposals that deserve scrutiny. Zimbabwe’s economic circumstances differ sharply from those of wealthier, more industrialised countries. In an economy where many enterprises operate on narrow margins and households face persistent financial pressure, fiscal measures must be tested against local realities.

World.title: Eswatini says ready to host SADC PF’s 59th plenary assembly
World.content:
THE Speaker of the House of Assembly of Eswatini Jabulani Mabuza has said his kingdom is ready to host the 59th plenary assembly of the SADC Parliamentary Forum (SADC PF), as regional parliamentary leaders gather at Ezulwini Palazzo from November 20 to 27.

Speaking at a media briefing on Thursday, Mabuza said the eight-day assembly would bring together presiding officers, Members of Parliament and parliamentary officials to consider regional issues, review committee reports and strengthen cooperation among member parliaments.

Delegates are expected from Angola, Botswana, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Seychelles (virtually), South Africa, United Republic of Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe, alongside the host Parliament of Eswatini. The plenary theme is “Harnessing Political Leadership

World.title: Mali: Mali Remains Strategic for Russia Despite Heavy Losses, Investigator Says
World.content:
Russia is unlikely to pull out of Mali despite losing more than 10 percent of its forces there, an investigator who tracks Russian military deployments told RFI. Lou Osbourn co-founded All Eyes On Wagner, a collective of journalists and cybersecurity analysts. She said the losses prove that Russian fighters are taking part in operations alongside Malian troops and that "Africa remains an area of interest for Moscow".

The United Kingdom's The Guardian newspaper - which had access to the leaked records through a media consortium that includes RFI - reported on Tuesday that 349 Russian fighters were killed in Mali between September 2023 and September 2026.

It based its tally on death certificates held by Russia's national statistics agency, Rosstat, but said that the real figure was probably higher because deaths can take time to be registered.



Two hacking groups obtained the records: Cyber Partisans, which is linked to the Belarusian opposition, and Ukraine's Silent Crow. Moscow does not publish its military losses in Africa.

Russian mercenaries from the Wagner group arrived in Mali in late 2021 to support the country's military rulers. In June 2025, Wagner handed over its operations there to the Africa Corps, a unit under Russia's defence ministry.

The Guardian linked most of the 349 deaths to fighting with armed groups. The records list 70 Russians who died on 27 July, 2024, when Tuareg separatists and fighters from JNIM, a group linked to al-Qaeda, ambushed Malian troops and Wagner fighters near Tinzaouaten, close to the border with Algeria.

Another 43 Russians died on 25 April, 2026, when JNIM and the Tuareg-led Azawad Liberation Front launched coordinated attacks across Mali. General Sadio Camara, Mali's defence minister, was killed in the offensive.

Russian forces withdrew from the northern city of Kidal by the following morning, and Malian troops and the Africa Corps retook it on 6 October.

Osbourn tells RFI why she trusts the leaked figures and what they reveal about Russia's role in Mali.

France rejects 'absurd' Russian claims of direct involvement in Ukraine war

RFI: The leaked records list 349 Russian fighters from Wagner and then the Africa Corps killed in Mali over three years. Is that a significant toll?

Lou Osbourn: Yes, it's quite high. It's more than 10 percent of their force. The deaths also line up with specific events - the battle of Tinzaouaten and the more recent fighting.

RFI: You're talking about the coordinated attacks of 25 April, when several places were hit at once and Mali's defence minister, General Sadio Camara, was killed?

LO: Yes, that's right. It shows they suffered heavy losses. The figures are particularly interesting because the Russian authorities revealed so little about the deaths of Wagner fighters and later Africa Corps fighters. We looked into this ourselves, especially around the time of Tinzaouaten.

RFI: That was in July 2024, when Tuareg separatists and jihadists from JNIM laid an ambush...

LO: Exactly. Even the fighters' families weren't told at the time. There was a blackout on the information. What's interesting about these figures is that they show Russia did record the deaths.

RFI: The leaked figures put the toll at 70. That's also how many the armed groups claimed to have killed at the time.

LO: Yes, absolutely. It was a traumatic experience for Wagner.

RFI: The group's biggest defeat in Africa?

LO: Absolutely, the group's biggest defeat. What's very interesting is that the official records amount to a kind of acknowledgement of the defeat. But that acknowledgement was never made public.

Why Russia remains dependent on medicines made by the West

RFI: These figures come from Rosstat, Russia's national statistics agency, which was hacked by two groups, Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow. Do you have any doubts about how reliable the figures are?

LO: We have few doubts, for two reasons. We know one of the hacking groups and it generally doesn't tamper with the documents it obtains. That gives us some confidence in the source.

The numbers also fit what's happening in the countries concerned. There's been a lot of talk about Mali, but the records list deaths in many African countries. In Niger, for example, there were very few - two, if I remember rightly. Russia's involvement there is very limited. Our estimate was around 200 people.

RFI: Two hundred fighters?

LO: Two hundred Africa Corps fighters. When you compare the number of deaths with what we know about how many fighters are deployed, the figures look realistic and consistent.

RFI: You've said 349 Russian deaths in Mali is a high figure. Does it also show how involved Russia is alongside Malian forces?

LO: Yes. It shows they take part in military operations and that their role goes beyond training.

RFI: Which is something we knew...

LO: We did, but this gives us another concrete piece of evidence. It shows they're operating alongside the Malian army.

RFI: The leak gives no figures for Malian soldiers killed in recent years. If nearly 350 Russian fighters were killed, how many Malian soldiers might have died? Thousands?

LO: I think the toll is probably two or even three times as high. We know there are usually only a handful of Russian fighters embedded in small Malian army units. Sometimes there's one Russian fighter for every five Malian soldiers. So the Malian army's losses are probably much higher than Russia's.

'Working in Russia is like being a deep-sea diver', BBC's man in Moscow tells RFI

Close 

RFI: The hack of Russia's statistics agency revealed that at least 500,000 Russian soldiers were killed on the front in Ukraine between February 2022 and August 2026, or 700,000 if those reported missing are included. Could those losses put Russia's presence in Africa in doubt?

LO: I don't think so. Russia sends far fewer people to Africa and its troop numbers there are fairly stable. In countries where it's establishing a presence, it has only around 100 people. The Africa Corps runs operations in both Africa and Ukraine and rotates its troops.

Africa also matters politically to Russia. It helps Moscow win allies and gives it a way to try to stretch Western military resources in Ukraine and elsewhere. So Africa remains an area of interest for Moscow, and I doubt the release of these figures will lead to a withdrawal.

RFI: After the 25 April attacks in Mali, which killed 43 Russian Africa Corps fighters, Russia seems to be getting even more involved. Despite the cost in lives, the deployment still seems strategically important to Moscow, especially in Mali.

LO: Mali remains strategic because Russia uses it as a base for some of its activities. It was from Mali that Russian forces went into Burkina Faso and Niger. Resources are also at stake, and Mali matters to Russia politically.

For a year now, we've heard every three months that Russia is going to pull out. It's still there, and I find it hard to see why it would leave now. I don't think it will.

This interview was adapted from the original audio in French by David Baché.

World.title: Southern Africa: Crowded Waters - Can Southern Africa Steer Mozambique Channel Security?
World.content:
analysis

Rising international interest and insurgent activity at sea should push regional states to reassess their maritime commitments and capabilities.

Visits to Mozambique and Madagascar in November by Lieutenant General John Brennan, Deputy Commander of United States (US) Africa Command (AFRICOM), underscore the Mozambique Channel's growing strategic weight.

Alongside the channel's significance as a global commercial shipping route, AFRICOM highlighted Islamic State Mozambique's (ISM) developing maritime capabilities and the security of Cabo Delgado's multibillion-dollar onshore and offshore liquefied natural gas (LNG) investments.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

The US and Madagascar then signed an Acquisition and Cross-Servicing Agreement facilitating logistical cooperation in maritime patrols, military exercises and humanitarian operations. The agreement comes amid US concerns about Madagascar's deepening military ties with Russia.

These developments coincide with disruptions to Middle Eastern energy exports caused by the US-Iran war, which reinforce the strategic significance of Southern Africa's offshore energy projects. Continued disruptions to global shipping also underline the importance of alternative routes around Southern Africa, including the Cape of Good Hope and the Mozambique Channel.

They also follow October's inaugural South Africa-European Union (EU) Peace, Security and Defence Dialogue, after which Cosmin Dobran, Director for Peace, Partnerships and Crisis Management at the European External Action Service, advocated greater Southern African Development Community (SADC) involvement in securing the channel.

US encouragement for Mozambique to join regional maritime information-sharing arrangements, together with proposals for expanded military exercises and bilateral training, signals a greater emphasis on operational cooperation. The US is not alone. This month, an Indian Coast Guard vessel visited Maputo to conduct joint training and deliver naval spare parts. In March, India's Navy conducted joint surveillance of Mozambique's exclusive economic zone.

The channel's maritime security was also a focus of the recent 13th France-South Africa Strategic Defence Dialogue. France's longstanding military and commercial interests in the channel are entangled with unresolved sovereignty disputes with Madagascar over the Îles Éparses and with Comoros over Mayotte, which complicate regional maritime surveillance and operational cooperation.

The maritime dimension of the Cabo Delgado insurgency has intensified this year. Armed Conflict Location & Event Data analysis identifies 34 potentially maritime-related events involving ISM by mid-November, compared with 29 in 2025, 30 in 2024 and 20 in 2023. These include vessel seizures, abductions of fishers and sailors, extortion of coastal communities and clashes with naval forces.

Several incidents demonstrate the insurgents' ability to operate in coastal waters and occasionally target larger vessels, such as the May 2025 attack on the Russian research vessel Atlantida off Cabo Delgado.

In April, ISM intercepted a Tanzanian fishing vessel off Cabo Delgado, seizing its cargo and demanding a ransom before allowing it to continue to Tanzania. In May, insurgents reportedly seized at least 12 boats off Mocímboa da Praia and Macomia.

This expanding maritime activity poses rising security risks to commercial vessels operating in or transiting northern Mozambican waters.

The growing concentration of offshore energy infrastructure warrants careful consideration. In November, Italian energy company Eni began drilling for its second floating LNG project, Coral North, and expects to reach a final investment decision on a third floating LNG facility by 2027.

TotalEnergies resumed onshore and offshore construction of its US$20 billion Mozambique LNG project in January, and Mozambique's government has approved the revised development plan for the US$26 billion ExxonMobil-led Rovuma LNG project.

Locating floating production facilities roughly 50 km offshore may afford some protection from the insurgency, but distance alone no longer guarantees the security it once seemed to offer. Persistent maritime criminality, including drug trafficking networks operating between Mozambique and the Makran coast of Iran and Pakistan, and the wider proliferation of cheap drones and uncrewed vessels add to the risks.

Threats to commercial operations, and even unsuccessful attacks, would have disproportionate consequences for investor confidence and continued operations. The March 2021 Palma attack prompted the TotalEnergies-led Mozambique LNG consortium to declare force majeure, which was lifted only in 2025.

Nor should maritime insecurity and criminality in the northern Mozambique Channel be viewed solely through the prism of the insurgency. Cabo Delgado was a hotspot for transnational illicit trade long before the conflict began in 2017. Maritime trafficking networks that benefit from poorly monitored coastlines and weak oversight would continue to pose serious challenges even if the insurgency were resolved.

Protecting commercial investments must also not come at the expense of coastal communities. Fishers in northern Mozambique have experienced violence by both insurgents and security forces. Securing offshore energy developments and international shipping does not necessarily address the wider maritime insecurity these communities face.

The US and other international partners are tackling maritime security challenges in the same area where South Africa established counter-piracy patrols under Operation Copper in 2011. In 2012, the operation was formalised as a framework for trilateral maritime security cooperation between South Africa, Mozambique and Tanzania.

Successive South African presidential authorisations for Operation Copper have linked the deployment to implementing SADC's Integrated Maritime Security Strategy (IMSS).

The increasingly complex threat environment, expanding commercial interests and the growing involvement of international security actors should prompt a public review of Operation Copper, and of whether it genuinely contributes to implementing the IMSS. No long-range maritime patrols have been conducted under Operation Copper for four consecutive financial years, owing to the unavailability of South African naval vessels.

Southern Africa increasingly faces the problem of coordinating several overlapping mechanisms, which makes such a review essential. These include SADC's IMSS and its Standing Maritime Committee, as well as the Djibouti Code of Conduct and its Jeddah Amendment. This month, the Code's signatory states adopted a regional maritime security strategy and agreed to move towards establishing a combined maritime task force.

Close 

Two SADC member states, Tanzania and South Africa, will be chair and deputy chair respectively. This gives both countries an opportunity to shape wider regional maritime security cooperation and promote greater alignment with SADC's maritime security priorities.

Regional states have also leveraged EU financial and technical support to establish the Regional Maritime Security Architecture. Madagascar hosts the Regional Maritime Information Fusion Centre, which works with Seychelles' Regional Coordination Operations Centre to facilitate information sharing and coordinated responses to maritime threats.

International interest in the Mozambique Channel has long presented opportunities for geopolitically minded countries. However, the current proliferation of security initiatives makes coordination essential.

At next year's SADC Standing Maritime Committee meeting, member states should assess how their maritime security commitments and activities can better complement existing Western Indian Ocean arrangements, and ensure that international assistance supports collectively identified regional priorities.

States that cannot implement their maritime security commitments risk having their priorities determined by those that can. As international recognition of the Mozambique Channel's strategic significance grows, Southern African countries must actively shape and deliver maritime security cooperation in their own backyard.

World.title: Eritrea: Eritrea Accuses Ethiopia of Using Maritime Diplomacy to 'Camouflage Its Irredentist Ambitions'
World.content:
Addis Abeba — Eritrea has accused Ethiopia of using maritime diplomacy and regional security forums to mask what it described as territorial ambitions in the Horn of Africa, escalating tensions amid renewed disagreements over Ethiopia's pursuit of Red Sea access.

In a statement issued Thursday, Eritrea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused the Prosperity Party government of seeking to "manufacture a veneer of international legitimacy" around its demand for "sovereign sea access," which Asmara characterized as territorial revisionism.

The statement follows Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's address to the House of Peoples' Representatives on Thursday, November 26, in which he rejected claims that Ethiopia intends to invade Eritrea, but reiterated that access to the Red Sea remains a strategic imperative to be pursued through dialogue.



"Now they say, 'Ethiopia is going to invade Eritrea, Ethiopia will wage an invasion for the Red Sea'--we will not wage an invasion. Invasion is not needed; we want it peacefully and through dialogue," Abiy told lawmakers, likening Ethiopia's maritime ambitions to the natural course of the Abay River.

Abiy claimed Ethiopia had made repeated efforts to pursue economic cooperation with Eritrea, including proposals to extend electricity infrastructure, build roads and jointly develop a port, but said the Eritrean government had rejected them.

"We have made high efforts with the Eritrean government to develop together," he said, citing a proposal to supply electricity at Ethiopian domestic prices and jointly undertake infrastructure projects.

He also said Ethiopia had undergone a "strategic awakening" after its political elite failed to properly recognize the country's Red Sea interests, arguing that neighboring countries should recognize the long-term strategic implications of the issue.

Abiy further warned that Ethiopia's size and population meant instability within the country would have far-reaching regional consequences, cautioning against scenarios involving millions of Ethiopians moving into neighboring states.

"Because we are a large population; our disturbance disturbs many," he said, arguing that Ethiopia's stability was central to wider regional peace.

He also pointed to shifting geopolitical dynamics, including the potential opening of Arctic shipping routes, arguing that these could alter the Red Sea's strategic importance in the coming years.

Eritrea, however, said Ethiopia's maritime diplomacy was increasingly being used to normalize the involvement of a landlocked country in Red Sea security arrangements. It cited a late-October maritime security and search-and-rescue workshop in Addis Abeba, supported by the European Union.

The workshop brought together naval representatives from Puntland and Somaliland alongside representatives from Djibouti. Asmara argued that including Somali regional administrations while bypassing the Federal Government of Somalia undermined the sovereignty of a recognized coastal state.

Eritrea also cited the Tana High-Level Forum on Security in Africa, held in Bahir Dar from October 23-25, where National Intelligence and Security Service Director General Redwan Hussein argued that Ethiopia should have a role in Red Sea security arrangements given the waterway's strategic importance and growing involvement of global powers.

Redwan maintained that Red Sea security was not a responsibility reserved exclusively for coastal states, a position Eritrea said reflected Addis Abeba's efforts to expand its role in regional maritime affairs.

The Eritrean statement further cited Field Marshal Birhanu Jula's November 13 remarks in Mekele, in which he reportedly asserted that Dogali, Gundet and Adulis belonged to Tigray and made claims concerning Somalia's port of Zeila. Asmara described the remarks as part of a broader territorial narrative advanced by Ethiopian political and military officials.

It warned that repeated territorial assertions by senior officials, alongside threats to secure maritime access through force, challenged regional sovereignty and internationally recognized borders. The statement invoked Article 2(4) of the UN Charter, which prohibits the threat or use of force against the territorial integrity or political independence of states.

Close 

Asmara also rejected Ethiopia's maritime rationale, arguing that landlocked countries are entitled to access the sea through negotiated commercial arrangements but have no unilateral right to ports, naval deployments or arrangements that compromise the sovereignty of coastal states.

Eritrea claimed it had previously offered Ethiopia access to the ports of Assab and Massawa, including proposals in 2000 and 2002 to facilitate humanitarian assistance, which it said Addis Abeba rejected. It also accused Ethiopia of squandering opportunities for cooperation following the 2018 peace declaration between the two countries.

The statement reiterated a position shared by Egypt, Somalia and Sudan that Red Sea security and governance should remain the responsibility of littoral states, citing the October 4 El Alamein Joint Declaration, which reaffirmed freedom of navigation while emphasizing coastal states' role in Red Sea governance.

World.title: LA Olympics partnership with oil company prompts climate activist outrage, as board member resigns in protest
World.content:
An American oil company has signed on to help bring the 2028 Olympics to Los Angeles, potentially reducing the financial risk for California taxpayers. But the partnership has prompted backlash from climate activists and local politicians, and now a Los Angeles County official has resigned from an Olympic advisory group in protest.

Los Angeles County Chief Sustainability Officer Rita Kampalath announced Tuesday she was resigning from an Olympic environmental advisory group over a sponsorship deal between the organizers of the 2028 Games and the oil company Phillips 66.

The Texas-based oil company reached an agreement earlier this month to become the official fuel partner of the Olympics, Paralympics and Team USA.

LAPD CHIEF WARNS LOS ANGELES NOT PREPARED TO SECURE 2028 OLYMPICS DUE TO STAFFING SHORTAGES

The company will help fuel thousands of vehicles and equipment needed to put on the Games. It will also help support an Olympic torch relay that will take the flame through all 50 states.

Now some liberal officials in California, including Kampalath, are pushing back.

"The Games should represent the future Los Angeles is working to build, not the fossil fuel dependence we are working so hard to leave behind," Kampalath wrote in a LinkedIn post announcing her decision.

Kampalath is not leaving her county government job. She is stepping away from a group tasked with advising an Olympic-related fund that supports environmental projects, including wildfire prevention and ocean protection. She also clarified that her decision was personal and did not represent the county's position.

Other Los Angeles City Council members have also spoken out against the partnership.

Councilmember Hugo Soto-Martínez called the deal "disgusting," while Councilmember Katy Yaroslavsky called on Olympic organizers to drop the sponsorship, according to LAist.

LA HOTEL LEADERS WARN MAYOR BASS' $30 WAGE MANDATE IS KILLING BUSINESS AHEAD OF WORLD CUP, OLYMPICS

But another member of the council warned that doing so could come at a cost to the people they represent.

"Turning down this sponsorship would put more financial risk on Los Angeles taxpayers," Councilmember Tim McOsker told LAist.

Environmental activists are now circulating a petition calling on Olympic organizers to end their relationship with the company.

However, organizers have given no indication that they intend to back out of the deal.

LA28, the organization responsible for putting on the Games, has said its environmental commitments remain unchanged. Those commitments include using renewable electricity at competition venues, encouraging spectators to use public transportation and avoiding the construction of new permanent Olympic facilities.

Meanwhile, the Phillips 66 partnership will extend beyond Los Angeles. The company will also provide fuel to the U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Training Center in Colorado Springs and sponsor the 2028 U.S. Olympic and Paralympic track and field trials.

More than 15,000 athletes from around the world are expected to participate in the Olympics and Paralympics in 2028, when Los Angeles will host the Summer Olympics for the first time since 1984.

Los Angeles is preparing to host its third Olympics, and putting on the Games won't be cheap.

The estimated cost of hosting the event has grown to more than $7 billion, according to a January report from the city's administrative officer.

Olympic organizers rely heavily on corporate sponsorships and ticket sales to pay for the Games. But the city of Los Angeles has agreed to cover potential financial shortfalls, meaning taxpayers could ultimately be responsible if organizers don't bring in enough money.

Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin described initial air monitoring results after Wednesday's controlled detonation of a hazardous chemical stockpile in Iowa as a "best-case scenario" as officials prepare to release the results of additional environmental testing.

Speaking in an interview on Fox News Friday, Zeldin said four air monitoring stations positioned downwind of the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant recorded no detectable airborne lead after the controlled detonation.

"We only have measurements of 0.0, sometimes referred to as zero detect, sometimes referred to as non detect," Zeldin said.

"It's not that we just had a small elevation of lead being detected in our air monitoring," Zeldin added. "We had 0.0 readings on our air monitoring, and that's certainly a best-case scenario."

US ARMY TO PROCEED WITH IOWA DETONATION OF DEGRADED BOMB MATERIALS: ‘A CONSENSUS DECISION’

While the air monitoring results have been encouraging, Zeldin emphasized that the agency is continuing its environmental assessment, comparing thousands of samples collected before and after the detonation.

"We are going to make sure we do all of our due diligence," he said.

The EPA administrator said the agency expects to begin releasing the first post-detonation sampling results as early as Friday night.

"Hopefully that confirms what we saw at the air monitor," he said.

The agency's ongoing assessment comes after Wednesday's controlled detonation of the bomb-making chemical in Middletown, Iowa.

DR MARC SIEGEL: IOWA'S CANCER RATE IS RISING; ONE ANSWER MAY BE FOUND IN THE WATER

Roughly 5 tons of degraded lead azide were destroyed after being deemed unsafe and unstable amid concerns that a plume of potentially toxic dust could drift toward Missouri in the wake of the blast.

The EPA has collected more than 3,000 air, water, soil and dust samples, including 1,639 before the detonation to establish a baseline and 1,618 afterward to assess potential environmental changes.

In a separate update Friday, the EPA reported that it had completed 88% of post-detonation sampling at homes where samples had also been collected before the blast and was working to complete the remaining assessments.

The agency said air monitoring concluded Thursday afternoon after 30 consecutive hours of no detectable airborne lead.

World.title: Taliban reportedly strips women of their names in Afghan province, now being called 'goat' or 'grandmother'
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

The Taliban have reportedly banned the use of women's names in official documents in a northern Afghan province, with some women being referred to by degrading animal names, according to a report by Spanish newspaper El País.

The latest assault on women's rights under Taliban rule reportedly extends to medical records and prescriptions in Afghanistan's Balkh province, raising fears that the restrictions could spread nationwide.

Healthcare workers and other public employees have been instructed to address women as "Bibi," meaning grandmother or old woman, according to reporting by Afghan news outlet Zan Times and The Guardian cited by El País.

MOSCOW, TALIBAN FORGE MILITARY ALLIANCE IN POWER GRAB AFTER US AFGHANISTAN EXIT: REPORTS

Afghan women's rights activist Lalah Osmany, who is based in Germany, told El País that testimony from women, doctors and civil rights activists indicates some women are also being referred to in degrading terms such as "goat" or "cow."

"This is a systematic process of dehumanization," Osmany told the newspaper.

An Afghan activist speaking under a pseudonym confirmed the reported order to El País, although she said it had so far been ignored.

Zubaida Akbar, who directs the Afghanistan program at women's rights organization Femena, warned that the Taliban could eventually impose the ban nationwide, citing previous instances in which local restrictions were expanded across the country.

IRAN FLOGS FEMALE SINGER 74 TIMES FOR PERFORMING WITHOUT HIJAB IN VIRAL YOUTUBE CONCERT

Femena has counted more than 144 decrees restricting Afghan women's rights, according to El País.

Girls have been barred from studying beyond age 12, while women have been shut out of most professions and subjected to restrictions on speaking in public, the newspaper reported.



Some Afghan women have resorted to running underground businesses and secret schools in defiance of Taliban restrictions, according to Associated Press reporting published Nov. 17.

IRAN TO EXECUTE FIRST FEMALE PROTESTER TIED TO ANTI-REGIME UNREST

One Kabul beauty salon owner, whose identity was concealed for her safety, reopened her business after authorities raided her previous salon and confiscated her equipment.

"But now, they won’t even allow that; for women in Afghanistan, working has become a crime," she told the AP.

An assistant teacher at a secret school in Kabul described living in constant fear of arrest.

"We are absolutely terrified of that possibility," she told the AP.

Mohammad Aslam, a spokesman for the Taliban's Ministry for the Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice, defended the broader restrictions in comments to the AP, saying women could conduct business and social affairs provided they adhered to Islamic Sharia law and existing laws.

Osmany also warned that the reported naming ban could endanger female patients by increasing the risk of medical errors if prescriptions and medical records are filed under identical names.

Afghan women already face severe barriers to medical care under Taliban rule, including restrictions on male doctors treating female patients and bans on women pursuing medical training, according to El País.

In 2017, Osmany launched a campaign to have Afghan women's names included on official documents, including their children's birth certificates.

ARMY VET LAWMAKER MARKS ABBEY GATE ANNIVERSARY WITH BLISTERING MESSAGE FOR BIDEN-HARRIS: 'ABJECT FAILURE'

Despite receiving death threats from extremists, her campaign helped secure a change in 2020 allowing mothers' names to be voluntarily included on such documents. That progress was short-lived.

The Taliban swept back into power in August 2021 as the U.S.-backed Afghan government collapsed amid then-President Joe Biden's chaotic military withdrawal, leaving the country once again under the control of Islamist extremists.

The withdrawal drew widespread condemnation after 13 American service members, mostly Marines, were killed in an ISIS-K terrorist attack during the evacuation from Kabul.

Biden faced further backlash from Gold Star families after checking his watch during the dignified transfer of fallen American troops at Dover Air Force Base in Delaware.

Five years later, Afghan women and girls have seen hard-won freedoms stripped away under Taliban rule. Now, activists warn, even their very identities are under threat.

"Calling a woman by her real name in Afghanistan is an act of resistance," Osmany told El País.

World.title: Luka Dončić is a scoring machine. The NBA has rarely seen anything like it.
World.content:
Most NBA teams wouldn’t choose to let a player considered perhaps the greatest ever walk away in free agency. Yet that’s exactly what the Lakers did last summer — because most NBA teams will never have a franchise pivot ready to go quite like Los Angeles did.

Ever since Dallas stunningly traded Luka Dončić to the Lakers midway through the 2025 season and the Lakers paired the Slovenian superstar in his mid-20s with LeBron James, the all-time great who is a generation older, the NBA waited to see when the Lakers would decide to put the team’s future on Dončić’s timeline. That moment officially arrived last summer, when the 41-year-old James left in free agency and the Lakers didn’t try to stop the move.

There was no longer any doubt about which star the Lakers orbited. The only question was how comfortably Dončić would shoulder the championship expectations.

Nearly a fifth of the way through the regular season, the results have been extraordinary enough to push Dončić into a pantheon of scorers alongside such hallowed names as Wilt Chamberlain and Michael Jordan — and thrust the Lakers into the discussion as a serious challenger to the Western Conference’s pre-ordained championship contenders, the San Antonio Spurs and the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Only Chamberlain (in 1961 and 1962), Rick Barry (1966), Jordan (1986), James Harden (2019) and Elgin Baylor (1960) have scored more points through their first 16 games of a season than Dončić’s 586 thus far.

While facing Dončić during the last six years of his 14-year career, longtime NBA guard Reggie Jackson grew accustomed to his opponent’s tendencies and style, including feeling out a defense during the opening minutes. This season, “it’s kind of like he already knows all the answers,” Jackson told NBC News. “He comes out in the first quarter and he just he has his foot on the gas, and then from there, whether depending on what type of shot is going in, he kind of seems to play it off that.”

Dončić is scoring more than a point per minute and a league-high 36.6 points per game by taking and making more 3-pointers (4.8 on 13.2 attempts per game) and free throws (8.8 on 10.2 per game) than anyone. His accuracy both beyond the 3-point line and inside it exceed his career averages. Dončić has called it enjoyable to score as much, but has said he’s more driven by winning.

Iztok Franko, a data-driven Slovenian basketball analyst and author, has watched every game Dončić has played since he was a teenage sensation at Spain’s Real Madrid, and has seen Dončić produce a burst of high-scoring games before. Yet the combination of a hamstring injury that sidelined Dončić for both rounds of the Lakers’ postseason last spring and the team’s offseason decision to mold itself in his image had left Dončić “very motivated and hungry for this season,” Franko believes.

“Especially because this is now his team, with all the makeover the Lakers did over the summer. Luka had the longest period without basketball in his career, and the man truly loves playing basketball, so I think he had a huge itch to play, to entertain us again,” Franko said. “He also missed the Slovenian National Team play in the summer for the first time since 2017 and fully focused on rehab and preparing for this season.”

“So, I think all of that, plus the motivation for a good start, which was very important to avoid the noise, the criticism of the new team that would come if they would struggle out of the gate, contributed to him starting the way he did.”

Rob Pelinka, the Lakers’ president of basketball operations, compared Dončić to an illusionist, he told the team’s broadcaster this month, because “every night he does something unexpected.”

“If you look at the math or analytics of what he’s doing, it’s like in the same breath as Wilt Chamberlain. Like, did I just say that?” Pelinka said. “Like a modern-era player putting up those kind of numbers?”

After Dončić had scored 42 points to beat Miami eight games into the season, Heat star and two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo called Dončić “one of the best scorers to play this game, if not the best.”

Did he meant currently playing, or ever?

“Of all time,” Antetokounmpo told reporters. “I feel like some people are scared to say that, but he’s got to be up there.”

That game was one of Doncic’s seven already with 40 points or more. No other player has scored 40-plus more than four times this season.

Any player scoring at a pace like that would face scrutiny over its sustainability, but with Dončić, such concerns are rooted in the reason why he is a Laker at all. When Dallas traded him in 2025 — after puzzlingly negotiating solely with the Lakers, without seeing what 28 other teams would offer — the Mavericks justified the decision partly by questioning Dončić’s commitment to conditioning.

Dončić responded last season with a much publicized and revamped offseason workout regimen, but on nights when his jumper was not falling, he could also depend on James, the NBA’s all-time leading scorer, and up-and-coming sidekick Austin Reaves to step up in his place.

Reaves is still a Laker, but with James gone the Lakers’ formula for success now hinges on Dončić to a degree rarely seen in NBA history. The NBA record for usage rate — a possession that ends in either a field goal attempt, a free throw attempt or a turnover by a certain player — is 41.6%, set by Russell Westbrook in 2017. Dončić is currently at 40.44%, by one measure, which if sustained would rank third all time.

Dončić touches the ball nearly 84 times per game, nearly 14 more than Reaves, the next closest teammate, according to league tracking data. The strategy has paid off; of the 43 high-usage players who touch the ball more than 60 times per game, Dončić’s points-per-touch average ranks third best.

“We live on a spaceship, and we’re going at the speed of light at all times when he’s on the court,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said.

A team hasn’t empowered Dončić to this degree since he led Dallas to the 2024 NBA Finals, said an NBA scout not authorized to speak publicly about player evaluations.

“I think the Lakers bought into the heliocentric style of play that the Mavericks tried to avoid at times” over concerns about his stamina, the scout said. “Credit to Luka for being in good enough shape to play that way the entire game.”

But, the scout added, “the test will be if he can withstand this level of play for 65-plus games.”

Luka Dončić of the Los Angeles Lakers prepares to shoot a free throw during a game against the Charlotte Hornets on Tuesday. Adam Pantozzi / NBAE via Getty

The Lakers have acknowledged the heavy burden. After Dončić scored 29 points on 28 field goal attempts during a loss to lowly Utah in November, Redick said that “the shot creation that is required from him takes its toll.” Perhaps as a result, his habits as a scorer have changed. Compared with his previous eight NBA seasons, Dončić is more reliant on 3-pointers, with 52% of his field goal attempts coming there and only 6% of his shots coming from within 3 feet of the rim, compared to his career rate of 15%.

Franko believes the biggest difference that has sparked this scoring run and the Lakers’ 15-3 record is “him being healthy and continuing with his commitment to off court, diet, training plan that started in the summer of 2025,” he said. “That, along with the motivation to lead this team, to prove this new team is capable of being better than people expect it to be, I think resulted in the biggest on-court change, which is his commitment to defensive end, and to play faster.”

“I think defensively he was very good for [a] majority of the games, and his buy-in there has been crucial for Lakers success so far,” Franko added.

The Lakers’ commitment to Dončić as their leader was evident last summer, when teammates flew to Ljubljana, Slovenia, to spend several days training and hanging out with Dončić at his invitation. A Slovenian media outlet reported he had paid for his teammates’ chartered flight. The gesture was also symbolic: No other Laker is more responsible this season for whether the team can continue to fly high.

“It just feels like almost anything he shoots, whether it’s a circus shot, or whether it’s a regular stepback 3, or it’s a tough look, it seems like everything he shoots is going to go in,” Lakers teammate Quentin Grimes said in early November, after Dončić had scored at least 37 points in five consecutive games. “It’s kind of surreal. I don’t think I’ve ever been on the court when everything somebody shoots, you think it’s going in.”

Frequently asked questions What is Black Friday? Black Friday is one of the biggest shopping events of the year when retailers slash prices on products across categories. It happens the day after Thanksgiving, and while it used to be dedicated to in-store shopping, more shopping now happens online. What should I buy on Black Friday? The best products to buy on Black Friday include tech, toys, small home and kitchen appliances, clothes and shoes, subscriptions and experiences and gift cards and sets. Retailers tend to focus on products that people usually want to gift loved ones (or themselves) ahead of the December holidays. What’s the difference between Black Friday and Cyber Monday? There’s not much of a difference between Black Friday and Cyber Monday anymore. Black Friday, the day after Thanksgiving, was once dedicated to in-store shopping, while Cyber Monday, which happens the Monday after Thanksgiving, was dedicated to online shopping. But in recent years, the line between the two holidays has blurred. Retailers start their sales earlier, host them for longer and discount items in stores and online throughout November, so there’s little distinction. When do Black Friday sales end? Black Friday sales technically end tonight, November 27. However, Cyber Monday is coming up, so most deals are still available over the weekend. That said, you shouldn’t wait to shop — the longer you do, the more likely items on your wish list will sell out. Can you return Black Friday purchases? Yes, you can usually return Black Friday purchases, which often carry the same return policy as items you buy any other time of year. However, there are exceptions, so read the fine print or ask a customer service representative if you’re unclear.

Black Friday is historically one of the biggest shopping holidays of the year online and in stores, and retailers offer some of the lowest prices across categories. Are 20% off or more

Are highly rated with at least a 4.0-star average rating from hundreds of customers

I wrote about every deal in this article and worked with NBC Selected editors to finalize the live list, which I’m updating live every 10 to 15 minutes throughout Black Friday to reflect the most up-to-date offers and prices. For more information on our editorial team and how we choose products, check out this page.

World.title: Power being slowly restored as heavy Thanksgiving storm eases
World.content:
Heavy rain over flooded East Coast communities began easing Friday, and power was slowly restored to hundreds of thousands of customers as some places stayed on guard for high-tide flooding following a round of holiday storms.

The storms snarled travel and downed trees and power lines. The heavy weather led to water rescues from New York to Virginia. In New York City, preparations were underway to hold Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade on Saturday after an unprecedented postponement because of rain and high winds.

Elsewhere, wet snow fell as far south as the Tennessee Valley and freezing rain moved across northern New England. Cold rain was reported in parts of the Midwest, including the Ohio Valley and the lower Great Lakes.

Another storm system in the Northwest brought rain along coastal Oregon. More snow was forecast in the Cascade Range and in mountain passes in Montana and Wyoming.

There were just under 3,700 flights in the U.S. delayed as of Friday night, with another 162 canceled, according to the flight tracking service FlightAware.

The number of power outages, which peaked Thursday at more than 900,000 customers, fell to just under 300,000 by Friday night, according to utility tracker PowerOutage.us.

Bad weather in the East is taking its time to go

Conditions were expected to improve Friday across the entire eastern U.S., "but this huge system will take some time to weaken," the National Weather Service said on its website. Coastal flood warnings were posted from New Jersey to Virginia.

"A lot of standing water, tree branches, siding ripped off of houses and buildings," homeowner Chris Rizzo told CBS New York.

Waves crash against Virginia Beach Fishing Pier on Thanksgiving Day in Virginia Beach, Virginia, on Nov. 26, 2026. L. Todd Spencer/AP Photo

In Hampton, Virginia, the storm toppled a beloved landmark at Grandview Beach: a weathered, leafless tree known as the "Grieving Tree" or the "Shell Tree." Visitors regularly decorated its branches with seashells, and it became a popular subject for photographers.

After surviving many storms, the tree "may have finally met its match," local meteorologist Ricky Matthews wrote on Facebook, sharing a photograph.

Roofs in Ocean City and Rockville collapsed. In Norfolk, Virginia, crews rescued 39 people and two dogs, City Councilman Tommy Smigiel posted.

In Baltimore, the storm brought a record 3.04 inches of rain to BWI Thurgood Marshall Airport on Thursday, while high tide in Annapolis reached 4.48 feet that night, a level officials said was among the 10 highest on record.

Part of a fishing pier collapsed in Virginia Beach, Virginia, closing a 3-mile section of beach, including the boardwalk, "due to dangerous conditions," the city said.

Downtown merchants in Avalon, New Jersey, scrambled to pump out saltwater Friday after Thanksgiving brought some of the most significant tides in the seaside community's history. More than 1,100 people participated in a charity run, and Santa Claus was scheduled to arrive on a fire truck by evening to light the Christmas tree.

Conditions were a "million times better than they were 24 hours ago," borough business administrator Scott Wahl said.

Cheryl McKenna of Ocean City, New Jersey, said water flooded her garage and surrounded her property, keeping her family inside for six hours on the holiday. She said flooding has become more frequent since Superstorm Sandy in 2012.

A damaged traffic light pole lies across a flooded street in Ocean City, New Jersey, on Nov. 27, 2026, after heavy rain on Thursday. Allie Ippolito/AP Photo

"Our family has been here for 36 years," McKenna said. "But honestly, we're thinking, is this the right place for us to be? We're now retired, and we want to stay down here, but how often can we continue to do this."

Another round of rain and strong winds are expected to hit the East Coast by Sunday evening, potentially disrupting the Monday morning commute. Up to 2 inches of rain and wind gusts of 65 mph are possible in some areas, according to CBS News meteorologist Nikki Nolan.

Parts of South and Midwest see snow, while California contends with coastal flooding

Part of Tennessee was under a winter storm warning for up to an inch of snow Friday, after rain turned into light snow on Thanksgiving. Conditions were calmer for the Midwest, compared with Thanksgiving, when as much as 15 inches of snow fell in eastern Missouri.

The ice arena in Wentzville, Missouri, was empty when the roof caved in early Thursday.

Snow is expected to begin falling Saturday from Montana to Colorado, with accumulations of up to 10 to 18 inches in some areas, according to Nolan. The storm will then move into the Midwest and Gulf Coast on Sunday, bringing rain to cities including Chicago, St. Louis, Nashville and New Orleans.

A pedestrian is hit with water as a wave crashes into a seawall during inclement weather in Pacifica, California, on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026. Jason Henry/Bloomberg via Getty Images

Waves driven by high tides caused flooding along the Pacific Coast and continued to affect train service Friday. Buses were pressed into service as Amtrak's Pacific Surfliner canceled or shortened more than a dozen trains between San Diego and Los Angeles.

Record tides along the California coast forced evacuations from Humboldt County in the far north to Ventura County near Los Angeles.

Heavy snow was expected in parts of Montana and Wyoming. A renewed surge of moisture associated with an atmospheric river across the Pacific Northwest moved toward the northern Rockies, the weather service said.

World.title: U.S. Air Force cloud platform breached by hackers, report says
World.content:
The U.S. Air Force's cloud computing platform was breached in a cyberattack, multiple sources told Reuters on Friday.

The hackers breached Cloud One, the Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, according to Reuters, potentially exposing sensitive military and personnel information.

The breach was discovered at some point in the last month during system upgrades, sources told the outlet.

In a statement provided to CBS News, an Air Force spokesperson did not confirm or deny the breach, saying that it "does not comment on the security posture, vulnerabilities, or operational status of specific networks and systems."

"Ensuring the security, resilience and availability of our most critical war fighting assets remains a top priority," the Air Force spokesperson said.

In a follow-up statement, the Defense Department said that its systems "are safe, secure, and managed 24-7 by the best experts and teams in the world," adding that it "will continue to maintain all mission-critical operations and applications."

When reached by CBS News, Leidos, the tech company which has served as the main contractor operating Cloud One since May, declined to comment specifically on the hack, deferring to the Air Force. A Leidos spokesperson noted that earlier this year, it announced a $454.9 million contract to modernize and secure the Air Force's cloud operations.

The alleged incident follows a series of breaches and outages that have been reported at federal agencies this month, including at the National Security Agency, the CIA, the FBI, the U.S. Department of Agriculture, and the Federal Aviation Administration, the latter of which prompted a nationwide ground stop that triggered chaos for tens of thousands of travelers at U.S. airports.

In the FBI breach reported last week, hackers accessed a large database used by law enforcement agencies nationwide to access criminal records.

The NSA's network outage was linked to an urgent patching of vulnerabilities in PHP, the programming language that powers the majority of all websites, multiple sources told CBS News. The NSA's internal network, which is used to store and share classified information, went offline during the ordeal, the sources said.

The CIA and Office of the Director of National Intelligence, meanwhile, suffered an intrusion of an internal network that gathers intelligence from publicly available information, such as social media.

An ODNI official told CBS News in a statement Tuesday that there were "no disruptions to critical capabilities or classified systems" from that breach.

All this comes as White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired from his position last week. Sources told CBS News that White House chief of staff Stephen Miller had long wanted Cairncross out of the job, and that he had told people he didn't think Cairncross had the expertise needed to be national cyber director.

World.title: 2 American Airlines jets clip wings on tarmac of Reagan Airport
World.content:
There were no injuries when the wingtips of two American Airlines jets made contact Friday evening on the tarmac of Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport outside Washington, D.C., officials said.

American Airlines Flight 638 clipped the wing of American Airlines Flight 2152 a little after 5 p.m. local time while both aircraft were taxiing for departure, according to the Federal Aviation Administration.

In a separate statement provided to CBS News, American Airlines said that both planes returned to their gates and were "removed from service for inspection by our maintenance team."

Both the FAA and American Airlines said no injuries were reported.

The wingtip of an American Airlines jet was damaged after it made contact with another American Airlines jet on the tarmac of Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport outside Washington, D.C., Nov. 27, 2026. la_leere/X

The Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority said in a statement that its fire and rescue personnel responded to both planes. The airports authority said there were no disruptions to any other flights.

Flight 638 was bound for Dallas, while Flight 2152 was headed to Chicago. The airline said passengers would be placed on new planes and depart for their destinations later Friday night.

Earlier this month, two passengers suffered minor injuries when the wingtip of a Copa Airlines jet struck the nose of a UPS cargo plane on the tarmac of Miami International Airport.

And in early October, the left wingtip of a Delta Air Lines plane clipped the tail of an Air Canada aircraft on the tarmac of Los Angeles International Airport. There were no injuries.

Reagan Airport has three runways, one of which is considered the busiest in the nation, and it operates with a tightly restricted airspace due to its location near the White House and Capitol Hill.

In January 2025, an Army Black Hawk helicopter collided in midair with an American Airlines plane that was approaching to land at Reagan Airport. All 64 people aboard the American Airlines flight were killed, along with the three soldiers aboard the chopper.
