World.title: Poland releases international expert findings that Smolensk air disaster was an accident
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Polish prosecutors have published findings by international experts that the 2010 Smolensk air disaster in Russia that killed President Lech Kaczyński and 95 others was an accident caused by a series of human errors. The findings contradict claims by the opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party, which is led by Lech’s identical twin brother Jarosław Kaczyński, that the crash was caused deliberately by Russia. PiS figures have claimed that today’s announcement was a “manipulation” that omits key facts. Według Międzynarodowego Zespołu Biegłych katastrofa samolotu Tu-154M z 10 kwietnia 2010 r. była następstwem ciągu zdarzeń podczas końcowego podejścia do lądowania na lotnisku Smoleńsk Północny, w tym niestabilnego podejścia do lądowania, błędnej oceny rzeczywistej wysokości… — Prokuratura (@PK_GOV_PL) November 27, 2026 The international team of experts was, in fact, first appointed in 2019 under the then-PiS government, which ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023. During that time, it launched various new investigations into the Smolensk tragedy. PiS has always rejected the findings of official Polish and Russian investigations into the crash, which found it to have been an accident. It has also accused the Polish government that was in power in 2010 – then, as now, led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk – of helping to cover up the true causes. In its announcement today, the National Prosecutor’s Office said that the team of 22 experts – which included individuals from the US, UK, Hungary, Denmark and Ireland, as well as Poland itself, none of whom were named – analysed a wide range of information relating to the crash. That included photographs, audio recordings, laboratory test results and written documentation. The experts did not, however, have access to the wreckage of the plane – which Russia has refused to hand over – or the crash site itself. The experts found that the aircraft had descended too quickly and too far in its approach to Smolensk amid very difficult weather conditions, including heavy fog. Around 15 seconds before the crash, the plane’s commander decided to abort the landing, but the aircraft’s left wing then struck a birch tree, causing the plane to roll sharply. It then “collided with further terrain obstacles” before hitting the ground short of the runway. “According to the experts, the course of the disaster was consistent with a Controlled Flight Into Terrain (CFIT) event,” wrote the prosecutors. “This is a type of aviation accident in which a technically sound aircraft, under the control of the crew, inadvertently collides with terrain or an obstacle.” Among the contributory factors identified by the experts were the crew initiating the landing descent too late, incorrectly assessing the plane’s altitude during the approach, and failing to abort the landing early enough. The experts also identified failings from Russian air-traffic controllers, who wrongly told the crew that the aircraft was maintaining a correct heading and descent path when, in fact, it was to the left of the correct approach and its descent was unstable. A court in Poland has ordered the arrest of a Russian air traffic controller accused of intentional actions that caused the crash at Smolensk in 2010 which killed President Lech Kaczyński and 95 others. Russia has so far refused to cooperate in the case https://t.co/dYxyiRHk3B — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 20, 2022 The experts also found that there had been failings on the Polish side, including the selection of Smolensk North Airport for the landing and various irregularities and a lack of relevant experience in the air force unit assigned to oversee the flight. They also noted that cockpit recordings indicated the voices of individuals other than the crew in the cockpit, which could have distracted the pilots. However, they said that they could not confirm if any of these individuals was President Kaczyński himself. Significantly, prosecutors say that the experts found “no evidence of an explosion” on board the aircraft before it crashed. PiS has regularly suggested that explosives were used to bring down the plane.” A court has ordered Antoni Macierewicz, deputy leader of opposition party PiS, to apologise to @donaldtusk and two of his ministers, @sikorskiradek and @TomaszSiemoniak, for accusing them of “hiding the perpetrators” of the 2010 Smolensk plane crash https://t.co/6p0VmlhV0o — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 2, 2024 Commenting on the findings, Tusk said that they confirmed the earlier official investigations. Those were “questioned for purely political reasons” by Jarosław Kaczyński and PiS deputy leader Antoni Macierewicz, who has been the chief proponent of conspiracy theories around the Smolensk crash, he added. “They destroyed public life with these accusations of an attack [on the plane] in which I was allegedly involved,” declared Tusk, saying that PiS had turned “the nightmare in Smolensk” into a “political charade”. “I am convinced that the PiS leadership, especially Macierewicz but also Kaczyński, who tries to fan the flames of hatred, should pay a very high price for this, also for the sake of the memory of those who died,” concluded the prime minister, quoted by Polsat News. In 2022, for example, Jarosław Kaczyński said that the decision to bring down the plane carrying his brother was made “at the highest level of the Kremlin” and that Tusk’s government “covered up” the incident as part of a “macabre reconciliation with Russia”. Smolensk was an “attack decided at the highest level of the Kremlin”, says Jarosław Kaczyński ahead of the 12th anniversary of the crash. Donald Tusk's government then “covered up” the incident as part of a “macabre reconciliation with Russia”, he adds https://t.co/5ae0gHJj3B — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 4, 2022 At the time of writing, Kaczyński had not commented on today’s announcement by prosecutors. However, it was strongly criticised by other leading PiS figures. Małgorzata Wassermann, a PiS MP whose father, Zbigniew, also a PiS MP, died in the Smolensk crash, accused prosecutors of “clumsily presenting a version of events” that was based on “significant manipulation”. She said that, without an inspection of the crash site being carried out, the findings were unreliable. Meanwhile, Macierewicz himself attended the prosecutors’ announcement of the expert findings today, where he accused them of omitting key findings that did not fit their narrative. When PiS was in power, Macierewicz led the main investigatory commission that was tasked with re-examining the causes of the crash. However, despite spending almost eight years and millions of zloty, it failed to produce any conclusive evidence to support Macierewicz’s claims that the plane was deliberately brought down Macierewicz o ekspertach: Żaden z nich nie był w Smoleńsku! Dziennikarz: A pan był? Macierewicz: Nie, ja akurat nie byłem w Smoleńsku. Kurtyna. pic.twitter.com/QzbtKOKy6f — Aneta ObserwatorXY ® (@ObserwatorXY) November 27, 2026 After Tusk’s government came to power in December 2023, one of its first actions was to abolish Macierewicz’s commission. The following year, it published findings indicating major irregularities in how the PiS government had investigated Smolensk. In August this year, prosecutors announced that they had ended a decade-long investigation into whether Tusk’s earlier government had been guilty of the crime of “diplomatic treason” in its response to the Smolensk crash. World.title: Disputed Polish constitutional court announces 12-month suspension of chief justice
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The government-backed judges who have taken control of Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) have issued a decision suspending chief justice Bogdan Święczkowski, who was appointed to the tribunal under the former government, for 12 months. The news was welcomed by justice minister Waldemar Żurek. However, Święczkowski has rejected the validity of the decision, saying that the “robed usurpers” currently claiming control over the TK are acting unlawfully. Szanujemy decyzje niezależnych instytucji, bo dokładnie na tym polega przywracanie praworządności. Sąd dyscyplinarny TK zawiesił Bogdana Święczkowskiego na 12 miesięcy za bezprawne blokowanie sędziów wybranych przez Sejm. Skończył się czas prywatnego folwarku, który chronił… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) November 26, 2026 The move marks the latest twist in a long-running battle for control over the TK, which dates back a decade to the unlawful appointment to the court of three judges under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. As a result, Tusk’s centrist government, which took power from PiS in 2023, had effectively ignored the court and its rulings until this year, when it began appointing new judges to fill a growing number of vacancies on the TK’s 15-person bench. However, opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in five of the eight judges chosen by Tusk’s coalition in parliament, citing concerns over their qualifications or method of appointment. Events came to a head on 30 October, when those eight judges seized control of the court and announced that Święczkowski had been provisionally suspended for a month. Święczkowski, backed by Nawrocki and PiS, rejected their actions as an illegal “coup d’état” and maintains he is the rightful head of the court. On 3 November, the eight government-backed judges held their first general assembly. It was boycotted by the TK’s seven other judges, including Święczkowski, who were all appointed to the tribunal when PiS was in power. The general assembly approved moving forward with disciplinary proceedings against Święczkowski for alleged violations of his duties in leading the court, including refusing to accept the five judges chosen by parliament but whom Nawrocki has refused to swear in. On Thursday this week, the TK’s disciplinary court, made up of three government-backed judges, issued a decision to suspend Święczkowski for 12 months, saying that it would provide time for the disciplinary proceedings against Święczkowski to be fully resolved. A lawyer representing Święczkowski told the hearing that the disciplinary court was improperly convened, noting that two of the three judges had not sworn their oath before the president. He also said that the entire takeover of the TK and subsequent decisions made by it were unlawful, reports Gazeta Wyborcza. The International Commission of Jurists has criticised the takeover of Poland’s constitutional court, saying it “contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary” But it also criticised the president for refusing to swear in judges https://t.co/2kBv3GT20d — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 4, 2026 Święczkowski, who did not attend the hearing, afterwards condemned the entire process, calling the judges involved “usurpers dressed in robes” and saying that “the decisions of this body are illegal and have no legal effect”. He also argued that they had violated the basic judicial principle of judges not being permitted to rule on their own cases, given that the disciplinary proceedings against him concerned his refusal to accept judges not sworn in by Nawrocki, two of whom were on the disciplinary panel. The TK’s decision was, however, welcomed by Żurek, the justice minister, who said that it was another step in “the tribunal returning to serving the public” rather than being Święczkowski’s “private fiefdom”. Prezes @TK_GOV_PL Bogdan Święczkowski: Nemo iudex in causa sua – nikt nie może być sędzią we własnej sprawie. Tego uczą na pierwszym roku prawa. Przebrani w togi uzurpatorzy nie odrobili nawet tej lekcji. Nie wyłączyli się od orzekania w sprawie, która dotyczy ich samych. A… — Weronika Ścibor (@WeronikaScibor) November 26, 2026 Separately, the judges currently controlling the TK last week also approved requests from Żurek, in his role as prosecutor general, to lift Święczkowski’s immunity so that he can face charges over alleged crimes committed while heading the TK and previously serving as a senior prosecutor under the PiS government. However, Święczkowski’s position was effectively endorsed last week by the Supreme Court – a separate body from the TK – which issued a resolution stating that TK judges are only legitimate if sworn in by the president. The government has rejected the legitimacy of that resolution itself given that it was issued by Supreme Court judges who were themselves appointed unlawfully. Meanwhile, earlier this week the government moved to restore funding to the TK after its accounts were frozen at the central bank, whose governor, Adam Glapiński, was appointed under PiS and is a close associate of the party’s leader, Jarosław Kaczyński. World.title: Court overturns Warsaw mayor’s ban on protest outside Constitutional Tribunal
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A court has overturned the mayor of Warsaw’s decision to ban the ongoing demonstration taking place outside the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) in protest against the takeover of the TK by a group of government-backed judges. While the mayor, who is a deputy leader of Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party, argued that the gathering threatened public safety, Warsaw’s district court found that banning it completely was too “radical” a step. Sąd uchylił decyzję stołecznego ratusza odmawiającą przedłużenia zgody na zgromadzenie pod TK#PAPinformacje pic.twitter.com/kBLm9kT9vc — Polska Agencja Prasowa/Polish Press Agency (PAP) (@PAPinformacje) November 26, 2026 Protesters have been present in front of the TK since mid-September, fearing that the government would make a move to take control of the tribunal from its chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, who was appointed to the court under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. On 30 October, a group of eight judges appointed to the TK this year by Tusk’s parliamentary majority – but five of whom opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in – did indeed seize control of the tribunal and announced that Święczkowski had been suspended. They avoided the demonstrators who were blocking the tribunal’s main gate by entering through a side entrance that leads in from the prime minister’s chancellery. On Wednesday this week, city hall announced that mayor Rafał Trzaskowski had refused a request from the organiser of the protest for the public gathering in front of the TK to be allowed to continue from the end of November through to early January. The municipal authorities said that the demonstration had blocked the busy road outside the tribunal, thereby hindering access for emergency vehicles. They also pointed to a number of “dangerous incidents”, including aggression towards the police by participants in the protest. Such developments “have caused the gathering to lose its peaceful character”, wrote city hall. There are also “grounds to assume that the intention is, in effect, a long-term blockade of the entrance to the Constitutional Tribunal and the street itself”. The mayor’s decision was condemned by the opposition, with PiS party leader Jarosław Kaczyński calling it “authoritarianism in its purest form” and a “trampling of citizens’ constitutional rights” to freedom of assembly and speech. Warsaw's mayor, who is deputy leader of Poland's main ruling party, has refused permission for opposition protests outside the constitutional court to continue, saying they threaten public safety. The opposition has condemned the "authoritarian" decision https://t.co/b6fIsqXzDH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 25, 2026 The organisers of the gathering had the right to appeal the decision within 24 hours, which they exercised. And late on Thursday, Warsaw’s district court announced that it had overturned Trzaskowski’s prohibition of the gathering. The information provided by city hall “does not provide grounds to assume that the assembly violates the rules for organising assemblies and may pose a threat to people’s life or health or to property to a significant extent”, found judge Anna Bonkowska-Kubek. “The court holds the view that the most radical measures in the form of a ban on demonstrations can only be applied in very exceptional cases, and the authorities must always first consider actions and decisions that would enable the peaceful holding of the planned assembly,” she added. A prohibition of a gathering “can only be applied in absolute exceptional circumstances, and the authorities must always first consider actions and decisions that would enable the peaceful holding of the planned assembly”, said the judge. Bezprawna decyzja prezydenta Warszawy Rafała Trzaskowskiego zakazująca zgromadzenia przed Trybunałem Konstytucyjnym uchylona przez sąd! Kolejni sędziowie nie chcą ochraniać nielegalnych decyzji polityków Koalicji Obywatelskiej, a tym samym żyrować ich swoim nazwiskiem. To… — Jarosław Kaczyński (@OficjalnyJK) November 26, 2026 The court’s ruling was welcomed by Kaczyński, who said that it showed how “judges are refusing to protect the illegal decisions of Civic Coalition politicians”. He called on supporters to join him for a further protest outside the TK at 3 p.m. on Sunday. However, Bonkowska-Kubek’s decision was questioned by Tusk’s justice minister, Waldemar Żurek. “I’m always a supporter of freedom of speech and the right to protest,” he told broadcaster RMF on Friday morning. “However, I would very much like the court to approach this rationally.” Żurek said that, due to the effective blockade of the TK by the demonstrators, it is not possible for people to exercise their right to file cases to the tribunal in person. Later on Friday morning, Trzaskowski announced that, while he “respects the court’s decision”, the city would exercise its right to issue a further appeal against Bonkowska-Kubek’s ruling. Szanuję decyzję sądu, ale skorzystamy z prawa do zażalenia. Chodzi o mieszkańców i o służby ratunkowe, które muszą przejechać przez Aleję Szucha. Wolność zgromadzeń – tak. Blokowanie ulicy przez ponad miesiąc – nie. — Rafał Trzaskowski (@trzaskowski_) November 27, 2026 The legal situation at the TK itself remains under dispute. The group of eight government-backed judges have begun holding meetings and processing cases, including stripping Święczkowski of legal immunity to face criminal charges. However, Święczkowski and Nawrocki continue to insist that the actions of those judges are unlawful and that their decisions have no legal effect. World.title: Polish PM orders alternative financing channel for constitutional court after central bank freezes accounts
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Prime Minister Donald Tusk has issued an order for the National Development Bank (BGK) to provide financing for the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) after Poland’s central bank froze the TK’s accounts following a disputed takeover of the court by government-backed judges. The relevant funds for the TK to function will be allocated by the finance ministry, announced government spokesman Adam Szłapka on Thursday morning, a day after the cabinet approved a resolution authorising the move. However, the ousted chief justice of the court has condemned the government’s actions as “completely unlawful” and said that they make the court’s current leadership “directly subordinate” to the prime minister. Premier @DonaldTusk wydał dyspozycję, by Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego zapewniał finansowanie Trybunału Konstytucyjnego, a środki na ten cel zabezpieczy minister finansów. Państwo musi działać. — Adam Szłapka (@adamSzlapka) November 26, 2026 The move marks the latest twist in a long-running battle for control over the TK, which dates back around a decade to the unlawful appointment to the court of three judges under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government. As a result, Tusk’s centrist government, which took power from PiS in 2023, had effectively ignored the court and its rulings until this year, when it began appointing new judges to fill a growing number of vacancies on the TK’s 15-person bench. Events came to a head on 30 October, when the eight judges appointed by Tusk’s majority in parliament – five of whom opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in – seized control of the court. They announced that the chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, who was appointed under PiS, had been suspended. Święczkowski, backed by Nawrocki and PiS, rejected their actions as an illegal “coup d’état” and maintains he is the rightful head of the court. The disputed status of the TK’s leadership led the National Bank of Poland (NBP) to announce earlier this month that it had frozen all outgoing transfers from TK accounts. The central bank cited conflicting claims over who had the authority to manage the institution, saying it “has no authority to decide who is legally entitled to control the Constitutional Tribunal”. The NBP is led by Adam Glapiński, who was appointed under PiS and is a longtime associate of party leader Jarosław Kaczyński. Tusk’s government condemned the bank’s decision as politically motivated and pledged to find alternative ways of securing the tribunal’s finances. Meanwhile, both Święczkowski and Anna Korwin-Piątkowska, the government-backed judge who has assumed leadership of the court, each appealed to Glapiński to unblock the Constitutional Tribunal’s accounts and recognise their respective authority to manage the court’s funds. Poland’s central bank has frozen outgoing transfers from the bank accounts of the Constitutional Tribunal, citing conflicting claims over who has the authority to manage the court following a takeover by a group of judges backed by the government https://t.co/ZYkzoneojO — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 17, 2026 On Wednesday, the government adopted a resolution “on taking measures necessary to prevent a crisis situation related to the functioning of the Constitutional Tribunal” due to the NBP’s decision to freeze its accounts. “At a time when, after many years, an opportunity has arisen to overcome the constitutional crisis, restricting the Constitutional Tribunal’s ability to exercise its constitutional powers will negatively affect the level of legal certainty for individuals, including citizens,” the resolution reads. It requires the prime minister and finance minister to take “appropriate measures to protect the interests of the State Treasury and to ensure the state’s internal security and public order.” Szłapka subsequently announced that Tusk had instructed BGK, a state-owned development bank, to provide financing to the tribunal. The dispute around Poland's constitutional court risks entrenching a system of legal dualism in which judicial authority depends on political allegiance rather than broad constitutional consent, writes @AleksSzczerbiak https://t.co/mtgutqSTQh — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 10, 2026 Jan Grabiec, head of the prime minister’s chancellery, on Thursday morning told broadcaster TVN24 that the tribunal had an “auxiliary account” at BGK. This would allow its day-to-day operations to be financed despite the NBP’s decision to block payment orders, he added. “It is not just a matter of ordinary tribunal staff potentially not receiving their salaries,” said Grabiec. “The State Treasury also bears responsibility for contracts entered into by the tribunal’s previous leadership that include specific payment deadlines.” “This creates a liability for damages, potentially amounting to losses of many millions of zloty,” he added. “We cannot allow the State Treasury to be exposed to losses resulting from such politically motivated decisions of the National Bank of Poland.” The International Commission of Jurists has criticised the takeover of Poland’s constitutional court, saying it “contravenes international standards on the independence of the judiciary” But it also criticised the president for refusing to swear in judges https://t.co/2kBv3GT20d — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 4, 2026 On Thursday, Święczkowski condemned the government’s decision to channel money to the TK through BGK, calling it “completely unlawful”, reports the Dziennik Gazeta Prawna daily. “If this usurper Anna Korwin-Piotrowska accepts money from Tusk’s government, it will mean she is directly subordinate to Tusk,” he added. At the time of writing, the NBP had not publicly commented on the government’s decision to channel funding to the tribunal through BGK. BGK, meanwhile, told PAP that it could not comment on the details of its arrangements with other parties, citing banking secrecy. The Warsaw hospital at the heart of a recent scandal over allegations that politically connected patients were given preferential treatment has been fined 2.3 million zloty (€520,000) after an investigation found that it admitted patients out of turn and doctors were absent during scheduled shifts. The doctor at the centre of the scandal, who was a local councillor for Poland’s main ruling party, was charged with fraud in October and is now also facing disciplinary proceedings over alleged breaches of medical ethics and professional standards. Niestety – Dawid K. jednak nie posiadł daru bilokacji, cudu nie było. Z ustaleń kontrolerów Narodowego Funduszu Zdrowia wynika, że po prostu oszukiwał. Ale to nie jest tylko sprawa jednego młodego medyka z legitymacją Koalicji Obywatelskiej w torbie. Cały ten przypadek wiele… pic.twitter.com/DfC35LLUpo — OficjalneZero (@OficjalneZero) November 26, 2026 The audit was conducted by the National Health Fund (NFZ), which finances public healthcare in Poland. It was carried out following a series of revelations in June by media outlets about alleged irregularities at the hospital. Many of the claims centred around a young doctor, who can be identified only as Dawid K. under Polish privacy law due to the criminal proceedings against him. He served as coordinator of emergency services at the Southern Hospital. News outlet Zero.pl was the first to report that the doctor, who also served as a local politician for the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party that leads Poland’s ruling coalition, worked a seemingly impossible number of hours at four different hospitals and earned 1.6 million zloty last year alone. The website alleged that the doctor had declared shifts when he was actually not present and cited instances in which he reportedly appeared in local media during hours when he was officially listed as being on duty at the hospital. ❗️ Błyskawiczne przyjęcia, wykonywanie pakietów kilkunastu, a nawet kilkudziesięciu badań w bardzo krótkim czasie, możliwość przebywania w innym pomieszczeniu niż ogół pacjentów. W Warszawskim Szpitalu Południowym stworzono nieoficjalnie szybszą i bardziej komfortową ścieżkę… pic.twitter.com/3aanpRVeBu — Patryk Słowik (@PatrykSlowik) June 17, 2026 Over the following weeks, Zero.pl and two other news websites, Wirtualna Polska and Onet, revealed further alleged cases of huge salaries for some doctors and impropriety at the Southern Hospital, including preferential treatment for patients with political connections. This included claims that there was a “VIP lounge” in which patients with connections to KO were given more comfortable facilities than others and that such patients were often allowed to skip the queue and receive treatment more quickly. In its audit of the Southern Hospital, the NFZ found that certain patients had been admitted out of turn. Inspectors also identified cases in which patients in stable condition were admitted to the emergency department ahead of others whose health condition warranted more urgent attention. The NFZ also found that doctors were absent during scheduled shifts and and that medical services were sometimes provided by staff without the required qualifications. The audit raised further concerns about the appointment of an inexperienced doctor as the coordinator of the emergency department. In a statement published on Wednesday, the hospital acknowledged the NFZ’s fine but noted that it was a preliminary decision and that the hospital could submit objections. It said that its board was reviewing the details before deciding on its next steps. Poland’s health minister has unveiled a set of reforms intended to “rebuild trust” in public hospitals following a series of reports about exorbitant pay for some doctors and that politically connected patients could skip queues and use a "VIP lounge" https://t.co/pidAHxohc4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 8, 2026 After announcing the end of its audit, the NFZ noted that it would forward the findings to prosecutors who have been investigating reports of irregularities at Southern Hospital. Prosecutors last month charged Dawid K. with fraud, alleging that he submitted fraudulent or unreliable invoices to the hospital worth more than 583,000 zloty. He has pleaded not guilty. Prosecutors are also investigating other cases of alleged wrongdoing at the hospital. However, a spokesman last month said that the findings so far do not confirm reports of a “VIP lounge” at the hospital. Meanwhile, on Thursday, the spokesman for the National Chamber of Physicians (NIL), Poland’s medical professional body, announced that they had decided to bring disciplinary proceedings against Dawid K. The claims against him concern alleged improper performance of medical duties, breaches of professional ethics, and conduct that undermined public trust in the medical profession. Zgodnie z obietnicą przekazuję do wiadomości publicznej: Rzecznik Odpowiedzialności Zawodowej podjął decyzję o przedstawieniu zarzutów Dawidowi K. Dotyczą one rzetelności wykonywania zawodu, naruszenia etyki i podważenia zaufania do zawodu lekarza. Będziemy informować o… — Piotr Pisula (@PanPisula) November 26, 2026 In the wake of the allegations against him, Dawid K. resigned from his seat on the local council, left KO, and stopped working at the Southern Hospital. His former party also distanced itself from him. Jan Grabiec, the prime minister’s chief of staff and head of the KO in the Mazovia province, which includes Warsaw, told reporters in June that the scandal “has no connection to KO, but since he was a KO councillor, we will be all the more stringent in holding those responsible to account”. In July, the health minister, Jolanta Sobierańska-Grenda, unveiled a series of reforms intended to “rebuild trust” in the healthcare system. They include caps on doctors’ salaries, a requirement for them to work at least half their statutory working time at a designated hospital, and a new electronic waiting list system. Meanwhile, the mayor of Warsaw, Rafał Trzaskowski, who is also a deputy leader of KO, ordered a separate municipal audit of the hospital, which revealed a number of irregularities, including in relation to Dawid K.’s activities. It concluded with 44 recommendations that Trzaskowski said were being implemented. World.title: Poland plans no-fly zone on eastern border to aid downing of Russian missiles
World.content: Keep our news free from paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s defence ministry has announced plans to establish a no-fly zone along the country’s eastern border with the aim of making it easier to shoot down Russian missiles and drones that violate Polish airspace. Meanwhile, foreign minister Radosław Sikorski has again suggested that Poland should be allowed to shoot down Russian missiles that are over Ukraine but heading towards the Polish border. However, the defence ministry acknowledged today that NATO is so far opposed to the idea. Wiceminister obrony Cezary Tomczyk zapowiedział wprowadzenie strefy zakazu lotów przy wschodniej granicy Polski. Jak poinformował minister Tomczyk, rozporządzenie trafiło do rządowego zespołu, strefa ma obejmować od kilkunastu do 50 kilometrów przy granicy wschodniej Polski i ma… pic.twitter.com/3xF68uNNRU — Dariusz Wiewiorka (@darekwiewiorka) November 25, 2026 Speaking on Wednesday at the opening of a new military satellite imaging centre, deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk announced that his department “will request the government to establish a no-fly zone on the country’s eastern border, to ensure Poland’s security”. Tomczyk acknowledged that, after three Russian missiles struck southeastearn Poland last Friday, NATO had offered support, including the deployment of an Airborne Warning and Control System (AWACS) to Poland. “But at the same time, the Polish military must do everything possible to protect our interests here and now,” he added. The defence ministry recently took one such step by allowing easier identification of objects that can be shot down, said Tomczyk. “The no-fly zone at the state border will be an additional factor supporting the operations of the Polish Air Force.” At a subsequent press briefing, Tomczyk provided more details of the plan. The proposed no-fly zone would stretch for a distance of between “a dozen or a few dozen kilometres from the border”, he said. “When a Polish fighter pilot knows that an aircraft is entering Polish airspace from Ukraine, is flying at a certain altitude and speed, is entering the no-fly zone and is detected on radar, this constitutes grounds for shooting down such an object…We will also urge NATO as a whole to establish such a rule on the eastern flank.” The deputy minister said that a relevant regulation had already been submitted and “will be processed in the coming weeks”. He expressed hope that the measures could be in place by the end of December or in early January. As well as last Friday’s missile strikes, on Monday this week a Russian drone entered Poland from Ukraine and spent a few minutes in Polish airspace. The Polish military had been authorised to fire upon it, but eventually did not do so after it turned back towards the border. Poland is changing the procedures under which its military can fire upon foreign aircraft, citing the "growing threat from Russia". Visual identification of targets will no longer be required, with other forms of data to be used instead https://t.co/foCWsBDazH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 29, 2026 The government’s plans for a no-fly zone were, however, questioned by Mariusz Błaszczak, a former defence minister and now head of the parliamentary caucus of Law and Justice (PiS), the main opposition party. Błaszczak noted that current regulations already allow the introduction of a temporary no-fly zone. He suggested that what the government had announced was simply a “cosmetic measure” and asked what “real operational capabilities” it would provide to the military. Earlier on Wednesday, Bloomberg reported, based on unnamed sources, that Poland had, at a NATO meeting called on Monday to discuss last week’s Russian missile strikes in Poland, asked about the possibility of shooting down Russian missiles that are over Ukraine but heading towards NATO states. Asked about the issue, Tomczyk said that he could not confirm Bloomberg’s reporting, but noted that discussion of shooting down Russian missiles over Ukraine had been going on for months. “NATO is not in favour of this in any way,” said Tomczyk, quoted by broadcaster TVN. “If we want to make any decisions that concern the space over Ukraine, it must always be a decision of the entire NATO…Many months ago NATO decided that such a procedure was out of the question. And that’s where we stand now.” NATO has approved the deployment of an Airborne Warning and Control System to Poland in response to three Russian missiles striking Polish territory last week. Hours after the decision was announced, Poland’s airspace was again violated by a Russian drone https://t.co/gudQJsPlQ5 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 24, 2026 On Wednesday morning, before Bloomberg’s report had been published, Sikorski, the foreign minister, was asked during an interview with Polskie Radio about the idea of shooting down missiles over Ukraine before they reached Poland. “A missile or drone approaching our airspace already poses a direct threat to us, so I believe that shooting [it] down over Ukraine at Ukraine’s request would fall within the definition of self-defence,” said Sikorski. However, he acknowledged that any such policy would need to be agreed by NATO. As far back as 2024, Poland proposed the idea of shooting down Russian missiles over Ukrainian territory. But it was rejected by NATO, whose then-secretary general, Jens Stoltenberg, said that it would risk NATO “becoming part of the conflict”.
