World.title: Peeter Raudsik: Fear of data centers reached Estonia before data centers
World.content:
The debate surrounding data centers has become so distorted that untangling it now requires a real effort. Just a few years ago, it is unlikely that the authors of the "Industrial Policy 2035" strategy envisioned that there would be calls to regulate a sector that currently consists of only one major company.

"Among other things, ensuring minimal regulatory operating costs is necessary for industry to function and develop," states the now largely forgotten framework document. Yet because fears have been imported from elsewhere, the data center discussion has reached a schizophrenic state.

At the center of the confusion are 2,900 megawatts of connection applications currently on Elering's desk. Commentators fixated on this figure have expressed serious concern about both the grid's capacity and electricity prices.

A closer look, however, shows that the number tells us very little about the actual potential impact of data centers. Just as applying for a driver's license does not grant the right to drive, submitting a grid connection application to Elering does not mean electricity will actually be consumed. A data center developer's test consists of meetings with local governments, investors, planners, environmental experts, engineers and technology providers. Only after all those discussions can an application become something more than paperwork.

"Many data center developers themselves do not know in the early stages how much electricity their facilities will ultimately consume."

Confusion surrounding capacity figures is compounded by the fact that many modern large-scale data centers use multiple connection points to ensure reliable power supply. Current grid statistics do not distinguish whether one project has connections at several locations through different transmission lines. Instead, the capacities are simply added together. Two separate connections for a 100-megawatt data center at different voltage levels can quickly become 200 megawatts in public debate.

And as if that were not enough, many data center developers themselves do not know in the early stages how much electricity their facilities will ultimately consume. Technology is evolving too rapidly. Three years ago, processor rack power density was around 8.5 kilowatts; today it is closer to 25 kilowatts. The same amount of space can now accommodate three times more computing power.

Projects are also built in phases rather than all at once. That is likely why most detailed plans launched in Estonia do not specify the exact capacity of a future data center.

Therefore, away from superficial commentary and in the real world, the grid question is not nearly as critical as it is often portrayed. Estonia's electricity consumption has actually declined over the past decade rather than increased. At the same time, the country's transmission network has become significantly stronger thanks to investments made ahead of disconnecting from Russia's power grid, largely financed with European funding.

In other words, Estonia is well prepared to connect new consumers. "The story with these data centers is that if they arrive in Estonia gradually and at a reasonable pace, they will not have a major impact on either security of supply or electricity prices because the system can adapt," Elering CEO Kalle Kilk said in a recent interview. He is right.

Concerns about electricity prices are, of course, understandable, but it should not be forgotten that data center operators have those same concerns. There may have been a brief moment a year and a half ago when money was no object in this field and securing a grid connection was the overriding priority, but that has changed.

BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, has pointed out that rising interest rates have made debt-servicing capacity one of the key issues for artificial intelligence companies. Electricity accounts for 68 percent of data center operating costs, directly affecting operators' cash flow. Just as households have an interest in keeping electricity costs under control, so do data centers.

In light of all this, does Estonia have reason to follow Ireland and Spain by requiring data centers to build their own power generation facilities? Finland, among others, is also reportedly considering such a requirement.

"In light of all this, does Estonia have reason to follow Ireland and Spain by requiring data centers to build their own power generation facilities?"

However, there is one significant difference between Finland and Estonia, which makes importing Finnish concerns across the Gulf unjustified. Unlike Estonia, where only one data center is currently under construction, Finland is actively building them: 23 projects are under construction, 18 have construction permits, and five are awaiting permits. More than 60 additional projects are at various planning stages. Finland built this impressive pipeline in part by offering tax incentives on electricity consumed by data centers.

Against the backdrop of domestic calls for data centers to "bring their own power plants," one question remains unanswered: if the state itself has been unable to fully convince local governments to support wind farm development, how are data center operators supposed to do so?

Fortunately, there are finally signs of progress here as well. The government's newly announced wind energy support premium is encouraging investment in new generating capacity. Together with the latest auction, it marks the first meaningful step in years that is likely to bring new electricity production online and reduce Estonia's dependence on imported power.

In turn, available grid capacity, access to local energy and a predictable, reasonably priced electricity supply form the cornerstone of the value proposition for new industry, whether that industry is a data center or something else.

World.title: Lithuania's mail carrier enters top bid for acquiring Eesti Post/Omniva
World.content:
Lithuanian postal operator AB Lietuvos paštas submitted the highest bid in a public written auction for shares in Eesti Post, offering just over €115 million to acquire the company, which operates under the Omniva brand.

Minister of Regional Affairs and Agriculture Hendrik Johannes Terras announced the results of the auction for Eesti Post on Friday. AB Lietuvos paštas, which submitted the highest bid, is prepared to pay €115 million for Eesti Post, while runner-up Posti Group Corporation offered €96.2 million.

Sigrid Soomlais, deputy secretary general at the Ministry of Regional Affairs and Agriculture, said at a press conference that identifying the highest bidder does not yet mean a change in ownership. The evaluation committee will next review the bid in greater detail, after which the minister will propose either approving or rejecting the auction result.

Terras has 20 working days to make a decision, after which the process can move toward signing a sales agreement.

"Ownership will change once all the conditions necessary to complete the transaction have been met," Soomlais emphasized, adding that this is expected to take place next year.

Soomlais added that announcing the auction results will not affect the day-to-day provision of postal services, nor will a change in ownership terminate the company's existing contracts or statutory obligations, as postal service quality and conditions are governed by the Postal Act.

The auction opened on September 4 and ran through November 27.

The Ministry of Regional Affairs and Agriculture on Friday opened the bids submitted in the public written auction for shares in Eesti Post (Omniva). Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR

World.title: Estonia cuts port waterway fees up to 25 percent for cleaner ships
World.content:
The Riigikogu has passed amendments to Estonia's Maritime Safety Act cutting waterway fees by up to 25 percent for lower-emission vessels starting in 2027.

The overhaul ties port fees to environmental performance, ends an exemption for offshore fossil fuel bunkering and raises rates for cruise ships beginning in 2028.

Under the amended law, which enters into force at the start of 2027, vessels with above-average environmental ratings will pay up to 25 percent less than standard waterway rates when calling at Estonian ports or anchorages.

The legislation also ends a longstanding exemption for fossil fuel bunkering — the transfer of marine fuel or engine lubricants — at offshore anchorages due to marine pollution risks. Operators refueling vessels with fossil fuels at anchorages will pay 50 percent of the standard waterway fee in 2027 and the full rate from 2028. Vessels bunkering with non-fossil fuels will remain exempt.

Cruise ships face higher charges beginning in 2028. Cruise operators currently pay a unit rate roughly 2.5 to three times lower than other commercial vessels, according to the Ministry of Climate. Both the existing unit rate and the per-visit fee cap for cruise ships will remain unchanged through 2027.

Waterway fees are levied whenever a ship enters an Estonian port or anchorage to fund navigation infrastructure, icebreaking and maritime safety services.

Minister of Infrastructure Kuldar Leis (Reform) said the revised fee structure is intended to offset compliance costs for cleaner operators as shipping enters the EU's Emissions Trading System (ETS) while keeping Estonian ports competitive.

"The new system of waterway charges favors less polluting ships, helping to reduce the environmental impact of maritime transport. Lower charges give owners of greener ships another reason to choose Estonian ports, strengthening the position of both our ports and Estonian businesses in the highly competitive Baltic Sea region. The discount also helps cushion the impact on shipowners of bringing the maritime sector into the European Union's Emissions Trading System," Leis said via a ministry press release.

Estonia had temporarily discounted waterway fees — including a 15 percent reduction — to cushion maritime operators after the loss of Russian transit cargo. The Port of Tallinn competes closely with lower-fee terminals in neighboring Latvia and Lithuania.

World.title: Israeli strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff in Gaza
World.content:
Jerusalem: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said Saturday an Israeli strike killed two staff members at a clinic in Gaza, with the Israeli army labelling the pair as Hamas “terrorists.”

The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) identified the men, who worked as security guards at the clinic, as Hamas artillery cell commander Moaz Yousef Alitsbach and Ahmed Sufyan Muhammad Ali Abu.

MSF said it was “devastated” by the killings and denounced “a direct hit” on the organization.

“Our premises were clearly marked with MSF logos, and their location had been communicated to and was known by the Israeli military,” it wrote on X.

World Health Organization chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus slammed the attack.

“Attacks on health facilities, health workers and humanitarian personnel in #Gaza are outrageous and unacceptable,” he posted on X.

The IDF denied targeting a hospital or damaging medical infrastructure.

“This is another example of the Hamas terrorist organization embedding itself within international organizations,” it posted on Telegram.

World.title: US military says cyber systems secure after reports of Air Force hack
World.content:
Washington: The US military denied Friday any issues with its computer security following media reports that the Air Force’s cloud based system was hacked, in what would be the latest high profile breach of US digital infrastructure in recent weeks.

Asked whether the Air Force’s Cloud One platform had been hacked, the Pentagon did not specifically deny that the system had been breached.

Instead, a Defense Department official told AFP late Friday that “The Department of War’s systems are safe, secure, and managed 24-7 by the best experts and teams in the world. We will continue to maintain all mission-critical operations and applications.”

“As a matter of policy and operations security, the Department of War does not comment on the status of our networks,” a Defense Department official said earlier on Friday.

NBC News, a major US broadcaster, reported Friday citing an unnamed US official, that the cloud platform had been breached and that an attack “could have exposed sensitive military information.”

The breach was first reported by Reuters earlier Friday.

Federal News Network, which specializes in covering US federal agencies, also confirmed the breach, citing a “person familiar with the incident.”

The contractors discovered the hack earlier in the year while doing maintenance on the system, Federal News said.

The reported attack is the latest in a string of major outages in US government and private-sector digital infrastructure.

In recent weeks the CIA and FBI were also reportedly subject to hacks.

Suppliers for major American financial institutions including JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard were also hit.

In other instances, such as a major Microsoft Outlook outage, a separate US air traffic control issue and a reported issue with a top-secret National Security Agency (NSA) network earlier this month, officials were at pains to blame the outages on maintenance or defects — not intrusions.

The attacks and outages are not limited to the United States.

The European Commission last week said it came under an AI-assisted cyberattack in October.

AFP was hit by a cyberattack on Thursday, forcing a major client-facing system to be taken offline.

World.title: Von Dellingshausen in charge at Australian PGA Championship as Noren lurks
World.content:
Sydney: Germany’s Nicolai von Dellingshausen stayed on track for a second DP World Tour title Saturday at the Australian PGA Championship, but he has 12-time winner Alex Noren in hot pursuit.

Von Dellingshausen maintained the three-shot advantage he took into the third round by firing a 69 at The Lakes in Sydney, mixing six birdies and three bogeys to be 16-under for the tournament.

Sweden’s Noren, the highest-ranked player in the field at 25, kept the pressure on at the opening event of the European Tour season with a blemish-free 65 to be outright second.

Northern Ireland’s Tom McKibbin (70) and Thailand’s Kiradech Aphibarnrat are a shot further back.

With all the golfers out early to ensure the round was finished before a forecast severe storm, Von Dellingshausen picked up where he left off with three birdies in the first five holes.

But he dropped a shot at the eighth as the wind kicked in and again on the 10th and 16th.

“To be honest, I’m trying not to think too much about it,” said the German about winning.

His only other victory was at the Austrian Alpine Open in 2025.

“I did a good job today just playing golf and really embracing the moment. Of course I was nervous. I am going to be very nervous tomorrow.

“There’s a reason to be nervous and I did a good job today to really embrace it and to manage it.”

Noren is far more experienced at the pointy end of tournaments, but he is coming off a lengthy break and just happy to be in contention.

“I hadn’t played for a while. I’ve been practicing, but not knowing where my game stands. I’m extremely happy,” he said.

“I took care of the par-5s today and then you can kind of play some of the other holes a little bit more defensively maybe. It’s a really fun course to play.”

Along with Noren and Kiradech, the day’s other big mover was veteran Australian Adam Scott, who also stroked 65 to be seven off the pace.

He is striving to end a global tournament drought spanning over six years, but is not confident of challenging on Sunday.

“I mean, I feel like I’m a long way behind still, so we start just wanting to play for a good place, I think,” he said.

“I think it’d be miraculous if I was in the mix tomorrow, but we’ll see.”

World.title: Warriors’ Curry ‘making good progress’ after oblique injury
World.content:
San Francisco: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry is “making good progress” in his recovery from an oblique abdominal tear but will remain sidelined for at least three more games, the NBA team said Friday.

The Warriors said in a statement that a re-evaluation of Curry’s injury on Friday showed progress.

“He has started to do individual on-court workouts and will be re-evaluated again next Wednesday,” the team said.

Curry suffered the torn muscle in the first quarter of a November 11 loss to the Rockets in Houston, and the Warriors said the following day that he would miss at least two weeks.

The 38-year-old had been playing at an elite level this season, averaging 27.8 points per game with 3.7 rebounds and 3.9 assists while shooting a career-high 45.7 percent from three-point range.

The Warriors went into the game in Houston on an eight-game winning streak but lost five straight without Curry before putting together two wins this week.

Curry, a four-time NBA champion and two-time Most Valuable Player, missed 39 games last season, 27 of them with a nagging knee injury.

World.title: Messi’s defending champions Miami knocked out of MLS Cup playoffs
World.content:
Miami: Columbus Crew, with an injury-time goal from Santiago Rodriguez, beat Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami 1-0 to knock the defending champions out of the first round of the MLS Cup playoffs on Friday.

Rodriguez’s goal in the second minute of stoppage time gave Columbus a 2-0 triumph in the best-of-three first-round series, after their stunning 3-0 victory in game one in Florida.

The defeat was a season-ending disappointment for the star-studded Miami side that features Messi, Luis Suarez, Casemiro and Rodrigo De Paul, which also came up short in the CONCACAF Champions Cup and the Leagues Cup.

For Argentine superstar Messi, MLS’s top scorer in the regular season and the favorite to win an unprecedented third straight Most Valuable Player award, it was a second first-round exit in the three MLS Cup playoffs he has contested.

Miami, facing a must-win game after dropping the opener at home to seventh-seeded Columbus, had chances to score on a cold, rainy night in Ohio.

German Berterame had a golden opportunity six minutes from full time, but his header from point-blank range went over the crossbar.

The match appeared headed for a penalty shootout with injury time ticking away. But Inter’s defense allowed Rodriguez to bring down a cross in the box from Moroccan Anass Zaroury and blast it past Canadian goalkeeper Dayne St. Clair.

Miami’s early exit extends the champion’s curse in MLS. No team has retained the title since the Los Angeles Galaxy in 2012.

World.title: Saudi military industries chief wraps up UK visit focused on defense tech transfer, investment
World.content:
RIYADH: Bandar Alkhorayef, acting governor of Saudi Arabia’s General Authority for Military Industries (GAMI), has concluded an official visit to the UK aimed at expanding defense-industrial ties and attracting strategic investment into the Kingdom’s military manufacturing sector.

During his stay in London, Alkhorayef held bilateral talks with UK Minister for Defense Readiness and Industry Luke Pollard and co-chaired a meeting of the Saudi–UK Industrial Committee, the Saudi Press Agency reported on Friday.

Discussions focused on deeper industrial integration, technology transfer, and joint partnerships to strengthen national defense capabilities.

The London talks directly support GAMI’s core mandate under Saudi Vision 2030 to localize more than 50 percent of the Kingdom’s military spending by 2030.

Established in August 2017 to regulate, license, and develop the domestic defense ecosystem, the Riyadh-based authority drives international knowledge-transfer agreements to shift Saudi Arabia from heavy reliance on defense imports toward self-sustaining local manufacturing.

World.title: Syrian governors mark second anniversary of uprising that toppled Assad regime
World.content:
DAMASCUS: Syrian governors on Friday marked the second anniversary of the launch of the Deterrence of Aggression Battle, paying tribute to those who took part in the military campaign that culminated in the ouster of Bashar Assad's regime.

The governors of Damascus Countryside, Tartous and Hama stressed the importance of preserving the gains of liberation, pursuing reforms and reconstruction, and creating conditions for displaced Syrians to return to their homes.

In a post on X, Damascus Countryside Governor Amer Al-Sheikh said the anniversary recalled the sacrifices of those who helped bring about a historic turning point in Syria's history.

An image grab taken from a video uploaded on YouTube shows smoke billowing from a Syrian army tank hit by rebels in the Sakhur district of Syria’s second largest city Aleppo on July 23, 2012, after the opposition’s Free Syrian Army announced the start of the battle to “liberate” Aleppo, Syria’s commercial hub and a traditional bastion of President Bashar al-Assad’s regime. (AFP)

4

He said honoring those sacrifices meant safeguarding the country's unity, preserving the gains of liberation, promoting reform and continuing efforts to build a state that fulfills the aspirations of its people.

Al-Sheikh described the anniversary as a defining moment after years of patience, preparation and collective efforts that paved the way for Syria's liberation and restored hope to its people.

Tartous Governor Ahmad Al-Shami also recalled the night the military campaign began, describing it as a turning point that changed the course of Syria's history and ended years of oppression.

Call for reconstruction, return of displaced

Hama Governor Abdul Rahman Al-Suhyan said the launch of the battle opened a new chapter of hope for Syrians, noting that the people of Hama had made significant sacrifices in the struggle for freedom and dignity.

He said the sacrifices of those killed, along with the suffering of wounded people, detainees and displaced families, would remain part of the nation's collective memory.

Al-Suhyan stressed the need to repair the damage caused by years of conflict, rebuild affected communities and provide the conditions necessary for displaced people to return safely to their cities and villages.

End of more than five decades of Assad family rule

The Assad family ruled Syria for more than five decades, beginning with Hafez Al-Assad's seizure of power in a 1970 military coup. His son Bashar succeeded him in 2000, continuing a system characterized by centralized authority, extensive security controls and the suppression of political opposition.

This picture taken in Damascus on October 06, 2010, shows Syrian President Bashar Al-Assad greeting children as he visits the Martyr's Monument on Qassyoun Mountain marking the 37th anniversary of October Liberation War led by his father, the late President Hafez Al-Assad. (SANA handout photo/via AFP)

Hafez's rule was marked by a powerful security apparatus and the concentration of political and economic power among loyalists. One of its bloodiest episodes was the 1982 military crackdown in Hama, which killed thousands of people.

Bashar initially raised hopes of political and economic reform after taking office, but his government soon suppressed calls for greater freedoms and maintained tight control over political life.

The uprising against his rule began in March 2011, when peaceful protests inspired by the Arab Spring spread across Syria. A government crackdown escalated the demonstrations into an armed conflict that drew in regional and international powers, including Iran, Russia, Turkiye and the United States.

The nearly 14-year war killed an estimated 500,000 people and displaced approximately 13 million Syrians, both inside the country and abroad. It devastated cities, destroyed infrastructure and left millions dependent on humanitarian assistance.

The conflict ended with a dramatic opposition offensive — the Deterrence of Aggression Battle — launched on Nov. 27, 2024, in Qabtan Al-Jabal in western Aleppo countryside. Forces led by Hayat Tahrir Al-Sham advanced rapidly from northwestern Syria, capturing Aleppo, Hama and Homs before entering Damascus on Dec. 8. Assad fled the country, bringing an end to more than 50 years of rule by his family.

World.title: Jermaine Haley, known as WWE wrestler Bronson Reed, dies at 38
World.content:
STAMFORD, Connecticut: Jermaine Haley, known as the WWE wrestler Bronson Reed, has died due to medical complications. He was 38.

World Wrestling Entertainment announced Haley’s death on Friday, but did not provide details.

“WWE is devastated to announce that Jermaine Haley, also known as Bronson Reed, passed away earlier today at the age of 38 due to medical complications,” the company said. “Jermaine was a larger-than-life figure in WWE, but more importantly, he was a phenomenal person, a devoted family man, and a beloved colleague. Our thoughts and deepest condolences are with Jermaine’s entire family, including his pregnant wife, Paige, their daughter, as well as his friends, co-workers and fans.”

Haley last appeared at the Nov. 6 WWE Crown Jewel in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in a match against Oba Femi.

Born in Adelaide, Australia, Haley had two stints in WWE after joining the promotion in 2019.

World.title: Nasiriyah International Airport airside reaches 100% completion ahead of navigation system checks
World.content:
Nasiriyah (IraqiNews.com) – Nasiriyah International Airport Director Ali Al-Gharabi announced on Friday, November 27, 2026, that construction on the airport’s airside infrastructure has reached 100% completion, while infrastructure works and the dedicated airport access highway have achieved advanced completion rates amid ongoing federal and provincial efforts to accelerate the facility’s opening.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Al-Gharabi noted that the project is progressing steadily under direct follow-up from the Prime Minister, the Minister of Transport, and the Secretary-General of the Council of Ministers to overcome operational hurdles.

He confirmed that the fully completed airside section encompasses the main runway, taxiways, and aircraft parking apron, adding that a specialized technical committee is scheduled to depart soon to conduct factory acceptance testing for the airport’s air navigation systems.

Alongside terminal and utility construction, Al-Gharabi reported substantial progress on the parallel Nasiriyah International Airport Road project, which stretches from the city center to the international highway to connect Dhi Qar’s urban landmarks directly with the airport.

Once operational, the airport will feature an annual capacity of 750,000 passengers alongside a dedicated air cargo terminal—providing a major transit and economic hub for Dhi Qar Governorate and its archaeological heritage sites.

World.title: Zaidi orders flat 5% import tariff and doubles traveler dollar quotas to 12 trips annually
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi issued sweeping economic directives on Friday, November 27, 2026, establishing a unified 5% customs tariff across all imported goods and doubling the annual foreign currency cash allowance for Iraqi travelers through the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI).

According to a statement from the Prime Minister’s Media Office received by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the measures form part of a broader government drive to bolster macroeconomic stability and streamline trade and monetary policy:

Unified 5% Customs Tariff: Effective December 1, 2026, customs duties on all imported goods will be standardized at a flat rate of 5%, replacing tiered tariff schedules to curb customs evasion and simplify border clearance.

Doubled Traveler Dollar Quotas: Under parallel monetary adjustments executed by the Central Bank of Iraq, citizens traveling abroad are now entitled to receive 12 foreign currency cash allocations per year—up from the previous cap of six—at $3,000 per trip (raising the maximum annual traveler allowance from $18,000 to $36,000).

The dual fiscal and monetary package aims to expand citizens’ access to foreign currency at the official exchange rate of 1,520 IQD per dollar while easing upward pressure on parallel cash markets ahead of the new year.

World.title: Iraq seizes smuggled oil bound for Sulaymaniyah as Baghdad tightens control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi security forces intercepted a truck carrying smuggled oil at the Chimen checkpoint in Kirkuk on Friday as Baghdad steps up efforts to fight oil smuggling and reinforce federal authority across the nation.

According to Iraq’s Security Media Cell, which reports to the Prime Minister’s Office, forces from the Kirkuk Operations Command seized a vehicle traveling from Basra to Sulaymaniyah, which was carrying a container labeled as plumbing materials and protected with customs seals.

Security staff got suspicious of the package and ran a scan, which revealed hidden oil.

The driver was apprehended, and the truck was confiscated for further investigation and legal action.

The seizure comes as Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi pushes for more federal supervision of border crossings in Iraq’s Kurdistan Region and oilfields in disputed territory as part of larger measures to curb smuggling and defend Iraq’s national resources.

On Friday, US President Donald Trump voiced support for Al-Zaidi’s efforts to establish state authority across Iraq, curb oil smuggling, battle corruption, and place all weaponry under government control.

The operation comes as Baghdad steps up its attempts to improve government management of transportation routes, border crossings, and the country’s oil resources.

World.title: Trump backs Baghdad’s push to assert federal authority across Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – US President Donald Trump pledged support for Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s attempts to establish federal authority throughout the country on Friday, as Baghdad prepares to place border crossings in the Kurdistan Region and numerous oilfields in disputed territory under federal control.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump praised Al-Zaidi’s efforts to fight oil smuggling, battle corruption, and place all weaponry under state control.

“We support Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s efforts to build a united, prosperous, and strong Iraq that makes its own political decisions,” Trump said.

Washington’s backing is a diplomatic setback for the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG), which has sought international support against Baghdad’s aspirations to strengthen federal authority over border crossings and oil resources.

Iraqi Kurdish officials have aggressively criticized Al-Zaidi’s decree, claiming it breaches the region’s constitutional rights and weakens Iraq’s federal structure.

Iraqi Kurdish Prime Minister Masrour Barzani urged the international community to protect the region’s constitutional rights. In contrast, Trump’s speech expressly supported Baghdad’s attempts to impose state authority throughout the country.

The support also indicates the improved ties between Washington and Baghdad under Al-Zaidi’s leadership.

A national conversation is set for December 1 to resolve remaining conflicts between Baghdad and Erbil in line with the Iraqi constitution.

The advances occur as Baghdad works to consolidate state power, establish national sovereignty, and create a unified Iraq that serves all residents, regardless of race, religion, or sectarian affiliation.

World.title: Under-attack Palestinians find unlikely ally in Israeli retired general
World.content:
As Sawiyah – The four Israeli soldiers stepped out of their car in the occupied West Bank, their faces masked, their uniforms unmarked and automatic weapons strapped across their shoulders.

They had entered a Palestinian olive grove but, little did they expect, the person there planning to tell them to leave could have once been issuing them orders.

A retired Israeli general, Eyal Ben Reuven, had come that day to the Palestinian town of As Sawiyah, on a mission to prevent some of the rampant violence against Palestinians by extremist Israeli settlers.

For the 72-year-old, joined by fellow battle-hardened veterans of the Israeli military, the violence is a stain on the institution in which they once served.

“I’ve fought in a number of wars. And unfortunately, I have reached the point where I have seen an evolution,” said the former military man with piercing eyes, who spent much of his career driving tanks.

The army is failing to act, he said, even when the violence has reached a level “I never could have imagined”.

Unrest has soared in the West Bank since the unprecedented October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas on Israel, which responded with a massive military campaign in the Gaza Strip.

More than 1,100 Palestinians have been killed by the army or settlers in the West Bank since then. More than 50 Israelis have died in the same time in the territory, which Israel captured in 1967.

The olive harvest has become a flashpoint, with settlers attacking or stealing from Palestinian farmers on a nearly daily basis.

With the other former soldiers, Ben Reuven has set up a protective presence, a tactic more common among leftist activists who put themselves in the way in a bid to stop attacks against Palestinians.

– Army intervenes in harvest –

Clad in comfortable hiking attire and carrying walking sticks, it is difficult to imagine that some of the greying volunteers fought in intense combat.

Like good soldiers, they review instructions upon going out — they are there to assist the olive harvest, not to confront the settlers, and they will obey the army’s instructions.

A Palestinian human rights activist, Arafat Abu Ras, led the military men to a small olive grove. An old Palestinian woman was waiting to guide them and the soldiers, more accustomed to the battlefield than to farming, used sticks and small rakes to start knocking the olives off the trees, volunteering to do the work on the Palestinians’ behalf.

Almost immediately a military vehicle arrived. Under the humming of a drone, one of the serving soldiers shoved aside an AFP team to prevent filming, while another checked Abu Ras’s identity papers and ordered everyone to leave.

Abu Ras said that the olive farmers had coordinated with the army, which insists that Palestinians receive approval for their harvests in the occupied West Bank, arguing that it is for safety reasons.

“They say, ‘yes, yes’, and then the next day they come and force us to leave,” Abu Ras said.

After the serving soldiers arrived, a second vehicle came, this time with Israeli settlers. An official from a neighbouring settlement also ordered the olive pickers out, with troops saying it was a “closed military zone”.

The Israeli veterans, in line with their guidance, complied. They instead moved elsewhere with the farmers, hoping to prevent attacks on them.

“Our army is a joke,” fumed Yoel Feldschuh, a 77-year-old former air force brigadier general.

“Is it its role to shut an olive grove? What does the military have to do with that?”

Feldschuh made headlines when he was handcuffed and taken away by police in a similar action a month earlier.

Changing the behaviour of the military, he said, “will take a generation”.

– Rampant violence –

COGAT, the Israeli body responsible for civil affairs in the Palestinian territories, maintains that “security forces are deployed to ensure a safe olive harvest”.

But since September, the harvest has been marked by nearly 500 attacks, some of them fatal, according to the Israeli human rights organisation Yesh Din.

Amram Mitzna, an 81-year-old retired general, attributes the army’s inaction to the young ages of the soldiers, who have grown up under now-caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving leader.

“They consider every Arab an enemy who must be treated as such,” said Mitzna, who has also served as mayor of Haifa, Israel’s third largest city.

Netanyahu has allied himself with the far-right and championed a rapid growth of West Bank settlements, which are considered illegal under international law.

Netanyahu is fighting for political survival after losing ground in elections. Gadi Eisenkot, a former general seeking to succeed him, supports many of Netanyahu’s security policies but accuses him of yielding to “Jewish terrorism” in the West Bank and vowed to crack down on extremist settlers.

In As Sawiyah, the former soldiers eventually finished harvesting the olives in a nearby area alongside a school, putting them in bags to be taken by Palestinian villagers.

While no one was injured, Ben Reuven remained deeply disturbed by how the young soldier acted during the altercation.

“When I saw him arrive, masked, shouting, kicking sacks of olives, I was ashamed.”

World.title: BP eyes deeper energy ties with Iraq as CEO visits Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – British energy giant BP has reaffirmed its commitment to expanding operations in Iraq following CEO Meg O’Neill’s first visit to the country and meeting with Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi in Baghdad.

According to the Prime Minister’s office, talks centered on developing oilfields and boosting exploration efforts, notably at Rumaila in Basra, Eridu in Dhi Qar, and Kirkuk, as Iraq aims to produce 10 million barrels of oil per day by 2032.

To reach output objectives, Al-Zaidi advocated for faster development, intensified field activities, and longer working hours.

Iraq’s Prime Minister also emphasized the need for collecting related gas and decreasing waste to improve domestic energy supply.

O’Neill reaffirmed BP’s commitment to expanding its activities in Iraq, utilizing sophisticated technology and technical experience to boost production and develop the country’s oilfields.

Following the meeting, O’Neill lauded Iraq’s objectives, workforce, and energy potential on LinkedIn, stressing prospects to enhance the company’s collaboration with Baghdad.

Along with its partners and the Iraqi operator, BP plays a critical role in Rumaila, Iraq’s biggest producing oilfield, providing technical knowledge to boost production and maximize resource recovery.

In Kirkuk, BP is engaging in a large rebuilding program involving oil, gas, electricity, and water infrastructure, with the first phase covering resources amounting to more than three billion barrels of oil.

The company’s growing presence is especially important as Iraq pursues foreign investment, modernizes its energy infrastructure, reduces gas flaring, and expands its oil production capacity.

O’Neill emphasized that combining Iraq’s immense natural resources and indigenous knowledge with BP’s technology and worldwide experience may provide significant benefits for both parties.

The visit highlights Iraq’s strategic significance to BP, as well as the company’s long-term engagement in growing the country’s oil industry.

World.title: Iraq and Bahrain to strengthen economic and diplomatic ties
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih Al-Zaidi met with Bahraini Ambassador Khaled Ahmed al-Mansour on Thursday, as the two countries work to repair and enhance their bilateral ties.

The envoy delivered congratulations from Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and underlined his government’s commitment to developing economic cooperation with Iraq, promoting mutual growth, and resolving common difficulties.

Both parties addressed ways to further collaboration across sectors, as well as regional and international trends, emphasizing the necessity of coordinating views and ensuring regional stability.

The meeting comes after Bahrain’s decision on November 7 to reinstate its ambassador to Baghdad, after Al-Zaidi’s historic visit to Manama on November 4, the first by an Iraqi prime minister since 2003.

Al-Mansour departed Baghdad in April due to increased diplomatic tensions over drone strikes on Bahrain by Iran-backed Iraqi forces.

The reinstatement of full diplomatic representation represents a major step forward in Iraqi-Bahraini relations, creating new potential for commerce, investment, and economic cooperation while improving Iraq’s links with its Gulf neighbors.

World.title: Baghdad cracks down on Kurdistan oil smuggling to Iran
World.content:
Baghdad – The Iraqi government’s crackdown on oil smuggling through the Kurdistan region targets routes used to move crude into Iran to help it evade sanctions, according to document cited by state media and a security official.

On Tuesday, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi moved to put Kurdistan’s border crossings and several oil fields under federal control in an effort to curb oil smuggling.

Following Zaidi’s announcement, the state news agency INA cited what it described as an intelligence document revealing that crude oil was being smuggled in tanker trucks from fields in Kirkuk and Sulaymaniyah provinces into Iran.

There, according to the document, it was being blended with Iranian crude and then exported to Afghanistan for domestic consumption.

The document, which AFP has seen but could not independently authenticate, says Iranian and Iraqi crude are mixed in an effort to help Iran “evade sanctions.”

The United States, with which Zaidi has enjoyed close ties since taking office earlier this year, accuses Iran of using Iraq’s economy to evade sanctions, and has previously sanctioned Iraqi individuals and companies for blending Iraqi and Iranian oil.

A security source in Baghdad told AFP that the government’s position is that “any smuggling to Iran or elsewhere is prohibited, and the entire international border must be secured.”

The source added that Zaidi’s crackdown on oil smuggling, whether in the Kurdistan Region or elsewhere in Iraq, is backed by the United States, which has sought to choke Iran’s economy.

The intelligence document also indicated that another smuggling route runs through border crossings to Turkiye, but it was not clear if Turkiye was the final destination.

A former oil ministry official told AFP on condition of anonymity that the Kurdistan region has long exported oil to Turkiye not only via a pipeline, but also in huge quantities in tanker trucks.

He added that “illicit crossings in the Kurdistan region are used to smuggle crude oil, including from other parts of Iraq, to neighboring countries,” including to Iran and onwards to Afghanistan.

For months, Zaidi has been cracking down on the illicit oil trade, arresting officials and challenging an Iran-backed armed group after smuggling was uncovered in its stronghold near Baghdad.

But the move to bring Kurdistan’s border crossings and several oil fields under federal control could sour relations with Kurdish authorities, who have denounced Zaidi’s decision while keeping the door open for talks.

World.title: 131st vs 132nd Amendment Bills: What has changed in the Centre's fresh delimitation proposal
World.content:
Key changes in Centreâs fresh delimitation proposal

Here are the key differences between the two proposals:

Uniform 50 per cent increase in seats for all states and UTs

Use of 2011 Census figures for delimitation

Revised seat allocations and boundaries to remain until 2051

New Delimitation Commission to oversee the exercise

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Earlier Bill defeated in Lok Sabha in April

NEW DELHI: Centre is set to introduce the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026, in the Lok Sabha on Monday, seeking to implement one-third reservation for women in Parliament and state and Union territory legislative assemblies through a fresh delimitation exercise.The proposed legislation differs from the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, defeated in the Lok Sabha in April, mainly in its approach to delimitation, the allocation of seats among states and the census data to be used for redrawing constituencies.The most significant change in the 132nd Amendment Bill is the provision for a uniform 50 per cent increase in the number of seats in the Lok Sabha and the legislative assemblies of every state and Union territory.The fresh Bill proposes to increase the Lok Sabha's maximum strength to 850, comprising up to 815 members from states and 35 from Union territories. It also seeks to raise the ceiling on the strength of state assemblies from 500 to 650.The earlier 131st Amendment Bill did not provide for a uniform percentage increase in seats across states. Under the fresh proposal, applying the same 50 per cent increase to each state's existing strength would broadly preserve its share of seats in the Lok Sabha.The two proposals also differ in the census data they allow for delimitation.The 2023 women's reservation law linked the implementation of the quota to delimitation after the publication of figures from the first census conducted after the law came into force.The fresh Bill, however, allows constituency boundaries to be redrawn using the "latest published census figures available on the date of the commencement" of the proposed amendment. This effectively means the 2011 Census figures.The 132nd Amendment Bill proposes that the revised allocation of seats and the division of constituencies following delimitation remain in force until 2051.The fresh proposal also provides for one-third reservation for women, including those belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, for 15 years from the commencement of the 2023 amendment. Parliament would have the power to extend the reservation period by law.It would also determine the authority and manner in which seats reserved for women are rotated.The accompanying Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026, provides for a three-member commission headed by a serving or former Supreme Court judge appointed by the Centre.The commission would determine the allocation of seats, redraw constituencies and identify seats to be reserved for women.Under the Bill, reserved seats would be allotted by rotation "as the Commission may deem fit". Seats reserved for women from the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes would be rotated within constituencies reserved for their respective categories.The earlier Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha on April 17, falling short of the required two-thirds majority. A total of 298 MPs voted in favour of the Bill, while 230 voted against it.The government subsequently did not proceed with the accompanying Bills.

World.title: 'Both are Congress seats': Imran Masood on SP announcing Saharanpur candidates for UP polls
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Congress leader Imran Masood on Saturday objected to the

announcing candidates for Saharanpur and Behat ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, saying both seats belong to his party.

His remarks came amid ongoing seat-sharing negotiations between the Congress and the Akhilesh Yadav-led party, with uncertainty persisting over the alliance arrangement.

âBoth those seats belong to the Congress. The Congress won them in 2017. In 2022, the Samajwadi Party won one of them because I had joined the Samajwadi Party. If you look at the electoral equations in those constituencies whenever the Samajwadi Party contested without me, the party had no presence thereâ¦Akhilesh ji is a very senior leader.



He is a very senior leader and wants to become the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh.

He will have to show generosity and give us some room,â he said.

Congress on Friday said negotiations with the Samajwadi Party were not restricted to the 26 seats initially proposed by the latter. The party said discussions were under way over a list of constituencies it had submitted to the SP earlier this week.

The assertion came after a meeting of senior Congress leaders at party president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence to discuss matters concerning Uttar Pradesh.





The Samajwadi Party's decision to announce five candidates while seat-sharing negotiations were underway has added to the uncertainty over the alliance.

The SP has played down the announcement, maintaining that it had declared candidates only for seats where its claims were indisputable. The Congress, however, has indicated that such announcements should have been avoided while negotiations were still in progress.

World.title: 'SC must review its order': TN Congress as top court directs deepam lighting at Deepathoon
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu Congress committee (TNCC) president Manickam Tagore on Saturday urged the

to review its order directing the lighting of the

lamp at the Deepathoon stone pillar atop Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai.

He raised concerns over federal principles, religious harmony and the respective roles of the judiciary, state government and temple administration.

"Concern over federal principles and religious harmony - the Supreme Court must review its order! The Tamil Nadu Congress Committee expresses its deep concern over the Supreme Courtâs order in the matter of lighting the lamp at Thiruparankundram in Madurai. Respecting and upholding religious beliefs and worship rights, as well as safeguarding harmony among various communities and the peaceful social environment prevailing in Tamil Nadu, is everyoneâs foremost responsibility," he said in a post on X.



Tagore questioned the court's actions concerning temple administration, its appointment of a committee comprising retired judges and the involvement of central paramilitary forces in security arrangements.

"In this context, the courtâs actions concerning temple administration, its appointment of a committee comprising retired judges, and the involvement of central paramilitary forces in security arrangements raise important questions about the jurisdictions of the judiciary, the state administration, and temple administration.





In such sensitive matters, not only must the rule of law be upheld, but the administrative responsibilities of the democratically elected state government and the federal framework established by the Indian Constitution must also be duly taken into account," he said.

He also stressed that the responsibilities of the elected state government and the federal structure under the Constitution must be considered in sensitive matters.

"Furthermore, the courtâs order must be framed in a way that fosters trust and peace among all parties without hurting the religious sentiments of any party. The Tamil Nadu Congress Committeeâs firm position is that the rule of law must be upheld in the country, while Tamil Naduâs peace, religious harmony, and constitutional values must be protected without any harm. Therefore, on behalf of the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee, we urge the Supreme Court to review its order in this matter," he said.

SC directs deepam lighting at Deepathoon

World.title: Support to Bill may not automatically lead DMK to NDA, but will open alignment path
World.content:
NEW DELHI: If Congress and DMK could join hands in 2004 after their bitter split where the Sonia Gandhi-led outfit accused the M Karunanidhi government of complicity in the assassination of former PM Rajiv Gandhi and brought down the United Front government in 1998, then anything can happen in politics.

Thus said a multi-term DMK MP over the prospect of his partyâs widely-expected support to BJP in securing passage of the delimitation bill in Parliament after it was in the vanguard of opposition to the governing party since 2014.

While DMKâs support to the bill is unlikely to automatically lead the party to BJP-led NDA but it does open a path for their alignment and offer the national party a fresh opening in Tamil Nadu, which has remained a tough nut for it to crack despite repeated attempts.



It certainly weakens the anti-South charge DMK, Congress and others have levelled against BJP.

Besides making explicit provision in the bill that the share of every state in Lok Sabha will remain the same and the maximum strength of LS will be frozen till 2051, both concessions aimed at winning over DMK, BJP has of late made subtle moves to dial down its push for legislative measures which had drawn sharp opposition from the Tamil party.





This includes a sudden slowdown in the working of two parliamentary committees overseeing Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, which has proposed an apex regulator in place of several for higher education, and a Constitution Amendment Bill, which proposes automatic removal of PM, CMs and ministers detained on criminal charges for 30 continuous days, when they were on the verge of adopting their reports.

DMK, which has long championed state autonomy and decried central governmentâs alleged encroachment on its turf, has been sharply critical of both bills.

Both parties have a history of working together. BJP and DMK were allies in the 1999 Lok Sabha elections and the regional party was a member of the Atal Bihari Vajpayee-led government before their split in 2003. Their âsecularâ opposition to BJP, which then moved closer to DMKâs rival AIADMK, helped them explain away their alliance. DMKâs current challenge is the sudden emergence of Vijay-led TVK as Congress dumped it overnight to help the star actor become chief minister.

World.title: Attacks on shipping, seafarers unacceptable: EAM
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Attacks on maritime shipping and seafarers are simply unacceptable and call for a global response, EAM S Jaishankar said Friday. Addressing the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA), an inter-governmental body comprising 23 member-states, he said international law, particularly United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, must be respected.

The 25th meeting of the IORA council of ministers here was followed by a joint communique that expressed concern over the undermining of maritime safety and security of vessels and seafarers and called for ensuring their safety and security.

PM Narendra Modi met the foreign ministers and heads of delegation of the 23 IORA member-states participating in the meeting. âIndian Ocean has connected our people for a millennia.



As chair of IORA, India looks forward to working closely with all partners to advance its vision of Mahasagar (Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions) and to strengthen peace, security, stability and prosperity in the Indian Ocean Region,â he posted on X.

According to the Delhi communique, IORA reaffirmed its commitment to maintaining the Indian Ocean as a region of peace, stability and prosperity, and to upholding applicable international law to ensure âfreedom of navigation and overflight, unimpeded commerce, peaceful settlement of disputes and other lawful uses of the seaâ.





It also reaffirmed its commitment to sovereign equality, territorial integrity, political independence, non-interference in internal affairs, peaceful co-existence and mutual benefit.

India announced a grant of $500,000 for the associationâs institutional and financial capacity-building. âWhether it is to counter terrorism, narcotics trade or illegal, unreported, unregulated fishing, or indeed response to climate events and disaster situations, we have to become more self-reliant as well as more enthusiastic about cooperating with partners,â said Jaishankar.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

âWe are focused on the volatile aspects of a transforming global order, especially conflicts, frictions and disruptions. It is equally imperative to appreciate the promising aspects: deep interdependence, strong globalisation and the benefits of international cooperation,â he said.

The Indian Ocean is central to global trade, energy security, connectivity and economic prosperity. It is also a region of immense diversity, opportunity and of shared challenges, he stressed. âOur collective responsibility is to ensure that it remains peaceful, stable, secure and conducive to development,â Jaishankar added.

World.title: E-certificates for new citizens, hard copy on request
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Individuals who acquire Indian citizenship by registration or naturalisation will henceforth only be issued a digital certificate of registration as a citizen, with a hard copy being provided only upon the applicantâs request.

As per amendments notified to Citizenship Rules, 2009, every person who is registered as a citizen of India under clauses a, c, d, e or f of Section 5(1) of Citizenship Act â by virtue of marriage to an Indian national, being born to Indian parents, or persons of Indian origin, etc â will be issued a digital certificate of registration in Form X, digitally signed or signed by an officer not under the rank of under-secretary to government of India or one who is authorised by the central government.

The Supreme Court appointed joint receivers, Justices S. Vaidyanathan and V. Parthiban, on Saturday (November 28, 2026) left for Madurai to take charge of the administration of the Thirupparankundram temple from the Board of Trustees, which was suspended by the top court.

Justice S. Vaidyanathan, former chief justice, High Court of Meghalaya, and Justice V. Parthiban, former judge, High Court of Madras, left by a morning flight to Madurai.

The Supreme Court declared that Executive authorities had wilfully disobeyed the orders of the court over the failure to light the ceremonial Karthigai Deepam at the disputed stone pillar on Thirupparankundram hill. Hearing the contempt petitions on Friday (November 27, 2026), the court accused the authorities and the Board of Trustees of having acted “according to their political bosses”.

The Supreme Court directed the temple receivers to light the Karthigai Deepam at the stone pillar -- ‘deepathoon’ -- on Saturday (November 28, 2026) after consultations with the priests.

Also read: Indefensible defiance: On Tamil Nadu and Court’s Thirupparankundram order

This year’s festival might be over, but the long-standing issue is far from resolved. Disagreements over the use of the hill by the Muslim and Hindu communities, its ownership and traditional practices have existed since 1915. Now, with the apex Court’s order being a temporary arrangement, legal closure is yet to come.

World.title: NCP-SP announces support to delimitation, Congress calls it ‘unfortunate’
World.content:
The Nationalist Congress Party–Sharadchandra Pawar (NCP-SP) on Friday (November 27, 2026) announced its support for the delimitation Bills.

The NCP-SP, led by Sharad Pawar and his daughter Supriya Sule, is a part of the Opposition bloc, the Indian National Developmental, Inclusive Alliance (INDIA). Most of the INDIA parties oppose the Centre’s delimitation plan, and the Congress has termed the decision of its ally, the NCP-SP, to support the Bills as "unfortunate". Earlier in the day, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut had referred to parties supporting the Bills as "traitors”.

NCP-SP leader Jitendra Awhad on Friday (November 27, 2026) said in Mumbai, “We will support the delimitation Bill. We will attend the INDIA Bloc meeting.” He was referring to a meeting of INDIA bloc floor leaders called for Saturday morning to discuss the Opposition’s joint response to the Bills.

Meanwhile, Ms. Sule will be in Mumbai over the weekend, as Mr. Pawar continues to remain hospitalised in the city. She will go to Delhi only on Monday (November 30) to attend the parliamentary session, she announced on her WhatsApp status. Mr. Pawar is likely to be discharged over the weekend, Mr. Awhad said.

“Supriya Sule, along with the eight party MPs, has decided to support the delimitation Bill. The party will do so accordingly. That is the final decision,” Mr. Awhad said minutes after meeting Mr. Pawar at hospital. The party has already issued a whip to all its leaders to remain present in Delhi.

When asked about his discussion with Mr. Pawar, he said that they did not discuss the party’s official stance per se. “The general point being discussed was that delimitation is a constitutional process. It will have to be done at some point,” he said.

The Union Cabinet on Friday approved the Constitution Amendment Bill, providing a proportionate increase of 50% seats across all States. This ratio will continue for 25 years till it changes in accordance with the population in the Census after 2051. The Women’s Reservation law will come into effect along with the increase in seats.

‘Deeply unfortunate’

Reacting to NCP SP’s announcement, Congress leader Sachin Sawant called the decision “deeply unfortunate”.

“It helps the [Narendra] Modi government’s authoritarian mindset. This Bill has been introduced to tighten the noose of authoritarianism that has been tightening for the past 12 years. The government’s intentions behind this Bill are not honest,” he said in a post on X.

However, Maharashtra Congress sources told The Hindu that the party had anticipated that the NCP-SP would take this stance.

The INDIA bloc has been rallying against the delimitation Bills. Criticising the Union government, Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut called the move a ploy. “Realising they are set to lose in 2029, they have devised a new ploy. They intend to bring in 860 MPs and carry out a delimitation exercise. This Bill is anti-national and anti-democratic; it must be opposed. Those who vote in favour of this Bill will be traitors to the nation. Their names will be recorded in history as traitors,” he said.

He added that the parties of the INDIA bloc cannot take an independent decision. “Whatever decision is to be taken will be taken within the INDIA bloc,” he said

World.title: Saudi Arabia, Houthis trade attacks on rival capitals
World.content:
Saudi Arabia said on Saturday (November 28, 2026) it shot down a cruise missile targeting the capital Riyadh, after Houthi media reported Saudi strikes on Yemen.

A Saudi-led coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government has been regularly bombing areas controlled by the Iran-backed group since Yemen's civil war reignited over the summer.

In response, Houthi fighters have been targeting the oil-rich kingdom almost daily, hitting energy facilities, airports and Riyadh's financial district.

"Air defences intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the Houthi terrorist militia towards the Riyadh region," Saudi coalition spokesperson Turki Al-Malki wrote on X.

It came as Houthi news agency Saba reported a Saudi attack on Yemen's capital Sanaa, which the fighters control.

"Eight homes and three shops were damaged after Saudi enemy forces targeted the residential neighborhood of Bir Abu Shamlah in Al-Tahrir district, Sanaa," Saba posted on Telegram.

The attack wounded 13 people, according to Houthi news outlet Almasirah.
