World.title: Bombay High Court gives go-ahead for Tata Sons board meeting on November 30
World.content:
The Bombay High Court on Friday (November 27, 2026) refused urgent relief to two Tata Trusts challenging the casting voting rights of reappointed executive chairman N. Chandrasekaran, ruling that Tata Sons' November 30 board meeting can proceed as scheduled, subject to the High Court's final orders.

A Bench of Justice Abhay Ahuja said it was not granting any immediate relief and that the meeting can go on as scheduled, but the same would be subject to the final orders of the court.

The Tata Trusts had sought for the meeting to be deferred or stayed or for an order that Mr. Chandrasekaran would not be allowed to exercise his vote as executive chairman.

During the hearing, the court asked what was the need to defer the meeting or not permit Mr. Chandrasekaran to cast his vote as executive chairman when he is already holding the post in his second term.

"We are not granting any relief today. Let the meeting (on November 30) go on as per schedule. Any outcome of the meeting would be subject to our final orders," the court said.

The Bench ordered Tata Sons and the other respondents in the case, which include the board members, to submit their reply affidavits to two suits filed on Thursday (November 26) and posted the matter for further hearing on January 18, 2027.

The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the RD Tata Trust (RDTT) had filed the suits in the High Court against Tata Sons and six of its directors, challenging the reappointment of Mr. Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for a third five-year term.

The SDTT has sought ₹50 crore, while the RDTT has demanded ₹15 crore in damages, with 18% annual interest, from Tata Sons.

As per the suits, the September 17 Tata Sons board resolution reappointing Chandrasekaran was invalid because it did not receive the affirmative vote required under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association (AoA).

The immediate relief sought was to prevent the chairman of Tata Sons from exercising his casting vote during the November 30 board sitting in the event of a split in opinion among nominee directors.

On Friday (November 27, 2026), the Trusts' counsels also sought for the meeting to be deferred, which was opposed by Tata Sons.

"His (Chandrasekaran) third term is not coming into effect on Monday (November 30), right? He is already the chairman executive now. What are the plaintiffs (trusts) anticipating to happen during the November 30 meeting?" Justice Ahuja asked, seeking to know what was the need to defer the meeting or not permit Chandrasekaran to cast his vote.

There may be some other items on the agenda for the November 30 meeting other than confirmation of the reappointment of Mr. Chandrasekaran as executive chairman, the court said, adding those matters can be heard and decided.

Senior counsel Harish Salve, appearing for Tata Sons, said the board meeting needs to be held as it has got direction from the Reserve Bank of India giving a deadline of December 12 to inform the RBI of its (Tata Sons) decision (to comply with the mandated listing).

Any resolution passed would be subject to the orders of the High Court, Mr. Salve said.

Senior counsel Abhishek Manu Singhvi, appearing for the SDTT, said the RBI directive is just a ploy used by Tata Sons to show fake urgency to hold the meeting.

Mr. Singhvi sought a deferment of the board sitting on November 30, claiming that it has been called to confirm the minutes of the September 17 meeting during which it was decided to reappoint Mr. Chandrasekaran.

He pointed out Article 121 of the Articles of Association, which says such a decision cannot be taken unless there is an affirmative vote of the majority of the trustees.

When Noel Tata, who chairs Tata Trusts, had not given an affirmative voting in the September 17 meeting, then there was no majority and hence the next step of taking the vote of the other four board members could not have been initiated, Mr. Singhvi argued.

"Majority between two votes cannot be one vote. It has to be more than one. Noel Tata made it clear on September 17 that there was no affirmative majority vote. When Noel Tata disagreed there was lack of majority vote," Mr. Singhvi said.

The senior counsel added that Mr. Chandrasekaran's third term would be effective from February 27, 2027.

Mr. Singhvi submitted to the court the agenda of the November 30 meeting after which Justice Ahuja noted that one of the items was to confirm Chandrasekaran's reappointment.

Senior counsel Aspi Chinoy, appearing for RDTT, argued that the casting vote confirming the reappointment could not have been cast when there was no affirmative majority vote.

"The (reappointment) decision is perverse. They have destroyed the structure of the Articles that has governed the company for generations," he submitted.

Mr. Salve, appearing for Tata Sons, said there can never be a majority vote when there are two nominees for the trust and hence the resolution had to go for a casting vote.

"The decision (to reappoint Chandrasekaran) was taken after a unanimous vote. One of the directors (Noel Tata) holds the company hostage by saying he won't vote until things are done his way. It cannot be that if Noel Tata says no, it is a no. There could not have been a majority when there are only two directors," Mr. Salve contended.

Noel Tata says either it is his way or the highway, Mr. Salve argued and questioned as to why the suits were filed in November when the meeting and decision of reappointment were taken two months ago in September.

Mr. Salve added that the trusts, in their interim application, have not asked for deferment of the November 30 meeting. No prejudice would be caused if the meeting is held as scheduled. "The two trustees (SDTT and RDTT) cannot paralyse the company," he stated.

The suits said Article 121 of Tata Sons' AoA does not permit the chairman of a board meeting to exercise a casting vote in cases where the articles require the affirmative vote of a majority of the trustees.

The dispute follows Mr. Chandrasekaran's reappointment as Tata Sons executive chairman for five more years on September 17. The suits have claimed the Tata Sons board decision was "ultra vires the Articles of Association and is invalid, illegal, null and void".

Tata Trusts holds around 66% of Tata Sons and has sought a permanent order and injunction restraining the latter, its directors, officers and other agents from acting upon in any manner or giving effect to the resolution reappointing Mr. Chandrasekaran.

World.title: Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh arrested on charges of harassing IAS officer
World.content:
Kallakurichi MLA C. Arul Vignesh of the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) was arrested on Friday evening (November 27, 2026) by a police team on charges of harassing a woman IAS officer. The officer had accused him of making inappropriate advances and comments.

A case was registered after the Madras High Court recently directed the State Public Prosecutor to get in touch with the officer regarding the allegations after she filed a formal police complaint.

Police sources said a team led by Shristi Singh, the Investigating Officer appointed by the Madras High Court, arrested the legislator at his residence in Kallakurichi on Friday evening and took him in a police vehicle. He was subsequently brought to the Circuit House in Kallakurichi on the Salem-Ulundurpet highway for questioning, where a large posse of police personnel has been deployed.

The Kallakurichi All Women Police, which had registered a sexual harassment case against the MLA, served summons on Mr. Vignesh on Wednesday directing him to appear for questioning in connection with the case. Speculation over his arrest grew after Inspector Bhuvaneshwari, attached to the All Women Police station, visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi on Wednesday (November 25) and handed the summons to him in person.

On 23.11.2026, a senior lady officer in Kallakurichi District preferred complaint against Thiru C. Arul Vignesh, MLA, Kallakurichi Constituency regarding alleged harassment and inappropriate conduct. On the same day, a case in Kallakurichi AWPS Cr No. 91/2026 was registered under appropriate sections of law. Initial investigation was done by the local police and on the directions of the Hon'ble High Court of Madras in WP (Crl) No. 3183/2026 dated 24.11.2026, Tmt. Shristi Singh, IPS, Superintendent of Police, Tiruppur District took investigation of this case under the supervision of Tmt. N. Kamini, IPS, Inspector General of Police, Administration, Chennai. During the investigation, the petitioner and other witnesses have been enquired by the Investigation Officer. Consequent to the enquiry, the alleged accused Thiru C. Arul Vignesh, MLA, Kallakurichi Constituency has been arrested and the investigation is under progress. Relating to this incident, 201 social media posts were pulled down by the local police and the Cyber Crime Department of Tamil Nadu Police. However, since the Hon'ble High Court has also ordered against publishing, communicating or making known to the public any of the matters covered under sections PoSH Act, it is requested to avoid posting any post in contravention to the above directions.. — Tamil Nadu Police (@tnpoliceoffl) November 27, 2026

The police have booked a case against the MLA invoking provisions of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Ms. Singh began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) after receiving the inquiry report from Kallakurichi Superintendent of Police I. Shahnaz at the All Women Police Station.

Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini also visited Kallakurichi on Thursday (November 26) and supervised the investigation.

The opposition DMK, AIADMK, PMK and BJP had demanded his arrest after the incident came to light. The BJP Mahila Morcha also held Statewide protests on Friday (November 27), accusing the government of shielding the MLA.

The local police and the Cyber Crime Department had taken down 201 social media posts related to the incident, according to the police. The High Court has barred publishing, communicating or making public any matter covered under the PoSH Act, it said, urging the public not to post anything that violates these directions.

VIDEO | Kallakurichi: TVK MLA Arul Vignesh taken to court under heavy police security after the completion of interrogation. Arul Vignesh was arrested from his residence on Friday evening in connection with a sexual harassment complaint allegedly filed by a woman district collector. (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd) — Press Trust of India (@PTI_News) November 27, 2026

TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh arrested in connection with alleged sexual harassment complaint filed by a woman IAS officer.

World.title: Congress reaches out to DMK, other Opposition parties to stall passage of delimitation Bill
World.content:
Accusing Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah of seeking to change the Constitution under the garb of implementing women’s reservation after carrying out the delimitation exercise, the Congress on Friday (November 27, 2026) made a last-minute attempt to reach out to all Opposition parties, including the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and the Sharad Pawar-led Nationalist Congress Party (NCP), to stall the proposed legislation.

The party is also considering urging the Chief Ministers of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka and Telangana to address press conferences explaining their opposition to the delimitation Bill in its current form.

The Congress is planning a nationwide campaign against the delimitation exercise, arguing that it is divisive and against national unity and integrity.

Meeting held

Some of these options were discussed at a meeting of the party’s parliamentary strategy group on Friday (November 27, 2026) evening at the official residence of Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) chairperson Sonia Gandhi. The meeting discussed possible strategies to stall the passage of the Bills – the Constitution (132nd Amendment) Bill, 2026 and the Delimitation (Second) Bill, 2026 – in the Lok Sabha.

“They [the BJP] wanted 400 seats to change the Constitution and now, through delimitation, by increasing the strength, they are attempting it again. The Congress will fight this along with other parties. It is in talks with other parties and will continue to do so,” deputy leader of the Congress in the Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi told reporters after the meeting.

Party president Mallikarjun Kharge, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, general secretary (organisation) K.C. Venugopal, general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Chief Whip in the Lok Sabha Kodikunnil Suresh and Chief Whip in the Rajya Sabha Jairam Ramesh attended the meeting, apart from Mr. Gogoi.

Sources said Mr. Ramesh made a detailed presentation on the likely strength of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) and the Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance (INDIA) bloc in Parliament, based on the developments since April, when the government failed to secure a two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha, resulting in the defeat of the Bills.

He is learnt to have argued that the government would again fall short of the required two-thirds majority if the DMK voted against the Bills.

While the Sharad Pawar-led NCP, a key constituent of the INDIA bloc, has officially announced its support for the Bills, the DMK is yet to make a categorical statement on its position. The DMK had left the bloc after the Congress extended support to the TVK government in Tamil Nadu last year.

Mr. Kharge or Mr. Gandhi could make a last-minute attempt to persuade Opposition leaders to vote against the legislation.

Several leaders, including former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee and Left leaders in Tamil Nadu, are also trying to persuade DMK president M.K. Stalin to oppose the Bills, sources said. The INDIA bloc may also make a public appeal to the DMK.

Big trap, says Venugopal

Earlier in the day, Mr. Venugopal accused the Prime Minister and the Home Minister of seeking to set up a “big trap” for the people of India. “We are approaching everybody. The DMK always stands with the Constitution of India. I think whoever loves the Constitution of India cannot support these types of divisive agendas. So, we will approach all the Opposition parties,” Mr. Venugopal said.

In a post on X, Mr. Ramesh termed the move an assault on the Constitution and reiterated the Congress’s three demands: retaining the existing strength of the Lok Sabha and the State-wise distribution of seats for another 25 years, and implementing one-third reservation for women, including sub-quotas for women from the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, from the 2029 Lok Sabha election.

In a post on X, former Union Minister P. Chidambaram said the Centre’s proposed 25-year “freeze” on the States’ share of seats in the Lok Sabha will address two of their concerns but absolute numbers also matter.

He said the gap between Southern States and the other States will increase from 413 to 620. “Besides, the increased strength of the Lok Sabha will entail delimitation of the constituencies within each State. That will give a free licence to the government to gerrymander the constituencies within the State – as the government did in Assam and J&K. Gerrymandering is the greater evil and the greater danger,” Mr. Chidambaram added.

World.title: Centre proposes freeze on Lok Sabha seat proportions for States until 2051
World.content:
A new Constitutional Amendment Bill approved by the Union Cabinet on Friday (November 27, 2026) proposes an extension of the existing freeze on the inter-State distribution of Lok Sabha seats for another 25 years, until 2051, addressing the core concern of States that feared a loss of their proportionate strength due to the decline in their share of the national population.

Also read | Lok Sabha seat freeze is no longer linked to population stabilisation

The 132nd Constitutional Amendment Bill marks a significant turn from the 131st Amendment Bill moved by the Centre in April 2026 that sought to redistribute Lok Sabha seats among States according to the 2011 Census population.

The proposed amendment removes the linkage of the existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats to the 1971 Census and links it with provisions related to women’s reservation in Article 334A of the Constitution. The guarantee for a 50% increase in the number of Lok Sabha seats for each State is being written into this, providing that, for the purposes of giving immediate effect to such reservation for women, “the delimitation so undertaken shall provide for an increase of fifty per cent in the number of seats allocated to each State and Union territory in the House of the People.” The total number of seats in the Legislative Assembly of each State and Union territory will also increase similarly, “over and above the number of seats existing immediately before such delimitation”.

The new Bill, accompanied by a fresh Delimitation Bill, proposes to increase the number of Lok Sabha seats in each State by 50%, while the maximum strength of the lower House will rise from the current 550 to 850. If these Bills are passed by Parliament in its special sittings from November 30 to December 3, the path to immediate delimitation will open, which will also bring into force the 33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha.

Amendments to Articles 81 and 82, which mandate the size and distribution of Lok Sabha seats among the States, propose to extend a sunset clause for the existing proportion until 2051.

The existing provision in Article 82 that says that “until the relevant figures for the first census taken after the year 2026 have been published, it shall not be necessary to readjust” the distribution of seats is being amended in the Bill and will be changed to read “until the year 2051”.

Article 82 currently has two definitions for population: for the purposes of distribution among States, the 1971 population; and for the purposes of delimitation of individual constituencies within the States, the 2001 Census. The proposed amendment will extend the sunset clause to “until the year 2051”, but the reference to the 1971 Census has been dropped.

The Bill proposes that the distribution among States will be determined “in accordance with Article 334A”, while the boundaries of individual constituencies will be determined by the “latest published census figures available on the date of the commencement of the Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-second Amendment) Act, 2026”.

World.title: Death toll in Baloch Colony building collapse rises to 11 as rescuers recover three more bodies
World.content:
KARACHI: Rescue workers recovered three more bodies from the rubble of a six-storey building that collapsed near Karachi’s Baloch Colony area on Saturday, taking the death toll to 11.

On Wednesday, three people were killed and 14 others injured when the under-construction building — reportedly being constructed illegally on a residential plot — collapsed. Another body was recovered on Thursday, taking the death toll to four. On Friday, four more bodies were recovered, taking the toll to eight.

Videos shared by Rescue 1122 from the site showed members of the Urban Search and Rescue team using heavy-duty bolt cutters to cut through rebar and recover bodies, while clearing rubble with various tools.

At least eight more people are still missing according to reports submitted by their relatives at the information desk set up at the site of the collapsed building.

Commissioner’s office submits report to CM

The Karachi Commissioner’s Office has submitted a report to the chief minister on action taken against illegal and unauthorised buildings in the city, stating that 516 buildings have been sealed so far as part of an ongoing crackdown, as of November 27.

According to the report, action was taken against 262 buildings under construction in various districts. Of these, 158 were sealed, while notices were issued to 12 buildings. Construction work was found to have been halted at one site during an inspection.

In Korangi district, 41 of the 48 buildings were sealed, while notices were issued to seven. In Keamari, 12 of the 19 buildings were sealed and notices were issued to five, while construction work was found to have stopped at one site. The report also recorded 12 buildings in West, 21 in Malir, 64 in Central, 61 in South and 37 in East. Of these, eight buildings in Malir, five in Central, 55 in South and all 37 in East were sealed.

Karachi Commissioner Syed Hassan Naqvi has directed deputy commissioners to continue action against illegal and unauthorised constructions and ensure that those violating building regulations are dealt with in accordance with the law.

Man rescued alive after 54 hours

A day earlier, emergency services rescued a man alive from beneath the rubble, two days after the building collapsed.

Rescue 1122 said that 28-year-old Muhammad Adil was rescued alive from the rubble. It said that the search operation for any other individuals feared trapped was underway.

Its spokesperson, Hassaanul Haseeb Khan, termed the rescue a “breakthrough”. He added that rescue operations were ongoing to search for other survivors from the debris.

He said the rescued man told them that two other persons who might be alive were in touch with him. However, Khan said the rescuers conducted a search in the identified area but could not locate them.

Khan added that heavy machinery was also being used to remove debris, but that whenever a human body was spotted in the debris, the team stopped the machine operations and initiated manual work with extra care to recover the body.

Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah expressed gratitude that the man trapped under the rubble survived for 54 hours, describing it as a “miracle”, according to a statement issued from his office.

According to the statement, the chief minister directed rescue agencies and the Karachi commissioner to accelerate the ongoing rescue operation and deploy all available resources.

Murad also praised rescue workers for their tireless efforts and directed officials to ensure the survivor receives the best possible medical treatment.

Sindh Local Government Secretary Waseem Shamshad, who also served as director general of the Sindh Building Control Authority (SBCA), was removed from both posts on Thursday on the directives of CM Murad following the incident.

The CM ordered sweeping action over the incident while chairing a high-level meeting, further issuing directives for the removal of East Deputy Commissioner Nasrullah Abbasi, as well as Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) East Zubair Sheikh over “negligence”, a statement issued by the CM Office said.

In addition to the removal of the three officials, CM Murad further issued directives for the suspension of 16 SBCA officials and the initiation of an inquiry against them.

He directed the police to “immediately” arrest the building’s owner, Salman Tahir, and the builder, Zeeshan.

Moreover, he instructed that the building’s architect and structural engineer be included in the incident’s investigation to determine whether the construction complied with approved plans, building regulations and safety standards.

14 ‘illegal’ buildings in KAEHS to be demolished

The KDA’s Additional Deputy DG Farhan Kaiser visited the site on Thursday and told the media that their first priority was to remove the debris. He said that under the directions of the Sindh CM and LG minister, “illegal buildings” were being sealed across the metropolis.

He said that so far, 14 buildings had been sealed in the KAEHS after the building collapse and would be demolished in a second phase of the operation.

Kaiser added that it was the responsibility of the residents to report illegal buildings in their respective areas, and vowed to take action against the builders and owners of these buildings.

Members of the Chief Minister Inspection Team (CMIT), Bilal Memon and Anwar Shar, visited the scene and collected samples of the material used in the construction of the building for investigation purposes.

Rehabilitation secretary Rafiq Mustafa Shaikh, SBCA DG Abid Saleem, Rescue 1122 DG Brig. (retd) Wajid Sibghatullah Mahar and Rescue 1122 COO Dr Abid Jalaluddin Shaikh also visited the site and supervised the rescue operation.

FIR registered

A first information report (FIR) of the incident was registered at the Tipu Sultan police station on Wednesday, on the complaint of an official of the Sindh Local Government Department.

The FIR, seen by Dawn, invoked Sections 302 (intentional murder), 119 (public servant concealing design to commit offence), 427 (mischief causing damage), 337-H(1) (hurt caused by rash or negligent act), 109 (abetment) and 34 (acts done by several persons in furtherance of common intention) of the Pakistan Penal Code.

The building’s four owners — including Salman Tahir whose arrest the Sindh CM has ordered — its builder, architect, structural engineer and its contractors have been nominated in the FIR.

According to the FIR, the complainant alleged that poor-quality material was being used in the construction of the building. He claimed that the suspects, in collusion with the officials of various government departments, had been involved in constructing additional structures and not complying with the building’s approved plan.

This was why the building collapsed around 1pm, the complainant alleged.

Police have arrested four of the suspects, including one of the owners, Saad Tahir, and three contractors, who were produced before the judicial magistrate (south) today.

The judge granted police a five-day physical remand of the suspects.

World.title: AJK PM extends olive branch to protesters in Rawalakot
World.content:
• Gillani says govt ready to discuss all demands within constitutional, legal framework

• Urges protesters to dissociate themselves from armed groups

• Speaker calls for elections to fill seven vacant assembly seats

MUZAFFARABAD: Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) Prime Minister Iftikhar Gillani on Friday offered to discuss the demands of protesters in Rawalakot within the constitutional and legal framework, but urged those involved in the unrest to dissociate themselves from armed groups.

Addressing a PML-N public meeting at Lal Chowk, the prime minister said the AJK government was prepared to take every possible measure, in the light of a recent resolution of the assembly, to restore peace and stability in the region.

“We are ready to discuss every demand that falls within the ambit of the Constitution and law. Disa­ssociate yourselves from armed groups; dialogue can only take place within the constitutional and legal framework,” he said.

Mr Gillani said some people publicly distanced themselves from armed groups but continued to provide them space, which was detrimental to efforts to restore peace.

Referring to some of the protesters’ demands, the prime minister said the government was planning to establish catheterisation laboratories (cath labs) and stroke centres in different parts of AJK. The government was also pursuing road improvement projects and the Kashmir Express electric bus service, besides planning employment and self-employment opportunities for young people, he said.

“Our aim is not to make a flurry of announcements but to translate plans into practical measures and deliver results,” he added.

100-day action plan

Referring to the 100-day action plan, Mr Gillani said his government had drawn up a strategy extending to five years, adding that decisions concerning the state’s future and prosperity required careful planning.

He said four governments had changed during the previous tenure, disrupting development activities and affecting

the resolution of public problems. His administration would focus on ending political uncertainty and improving governance, he added.

The prime minister said the plan covered healthcare, education, employment, tourism, transport, digital governance and urban development, with several initiatives to be implemented during the first 100 days and others continuing beyond that period.

He said recruitment in government departments would be carried out thr­ough third-party agencies on merit, while interest-free loans would be offered to young people to encourage entrepreneurship and self-employment. Schola­rships at leading universities would also be provided to deserving students.

Tourism promotion, public-private partnerships for government rest houses and facilities for local businesses would help generate investment and employment, he said. Digitalisation of government services through the AJK One Portal was intended to reduce bureaucratic hurdles and spare citizens repeated visits to public offices.

Mr Gillani said the government would also introduce housing loans for deserving people, improve sanitation in all 10 district headquarters and undertake beautification projects in Muzaffarabad.

He said the coming 100 days would provide an opportunity for people to assess the government’s performance following the Nov 18 visit to Muzaffarabad by PML-N supremo Nawaz Sharif, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar and Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz.

“Building roads and public infrastructure alone is not enough; the state also needs to address its underlying problems. Society must restore moral values and mutual respect. Differences of opinion do not justify humiliating one another,” he said.

Call for dialogue

Earlier, Legislative Assembly Speaker Chaudhry Tariq Farooq said the government had assumed office to serve the people and promote development and public welfare.

He said the Kashmir freedom movement remained the party’s fundamental objective and that it would defend Pakistan’s interests in AJK while preserving the distinct identity of Jammu and Kashmir.

Referring to a recently adopted Assembly resolution, he said it reflected the common position of the people of AJK, the PML-N and all political parties represented in the legislature.

Mr Farooq said the people of Poonch should regain their right to representation through elections on the seven Assembly seats that remained unfilled, thereby completing the strength of the legislature.

Energy and Water Resources Minister Saqib Majeed Raja said unrest and uncertainty in AJK since 2023 had affected the region’s administrative system, economy and everyday life.

He urged society to assess what it had gained and lost during the past three years, saying the support and solidarity extended to Kashmiris by the people of Pakistan were a valuable asset that should not be squandered amid political differences.

He said lasting solutions to public grievances lay in dialogue, democratic processes and effective performance by elected representatives rather than protests, confrontation and vandalism.

People should give their elected representatives an opportunity to resolve their problems, he said, adding that voters had the power to reject them in the next elections if they failed to meet public expectations.

Several other PML-N leaders also spoke on the occasion.

Published in Dawn, November 28th, 2026

World.title: PM calls for stronger Pak-Oman ties
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has called for further strengthening Pakistan’s bilateral cooperation with Oman, particularly in trade, investment, energy and defence.

During a meeting with the Omani ambassador at the Prime Minister’s House, the prime minister highlighted the longstanding brotherly relations between Pakistan and Oman, rooted in shared history, faith and culture.

According to a Prime Minister’s Office news release, PM Shehbaz stressed the importance of translating the positive momentum in bilateral relations into tangible results through increased economic engagement and institutional cooperation.

The two sides also discussed recent regional and global developments. The prime minister emphasised the importance of maintaining peace and stability through dialogue and diplomacy.

The Omani ambassador than­ked the prime minister for receiving him, conveyed the greetings of the Omani leadership and reaffirmed his country’s commitment to further strengthening its close relations with Pakistan.

PCSIR role in exports

Separately, PM Shehbaz on Fri­day directed the Pakistan Council of Scientific and Indus­trial Research to enhance its research capabilities and contribute more effectively to industrial development, export growth and the promotion of small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

Chairing a meeting on matters related to the PCSIR, the prime minister said the institution could play a significant role in helping Pakistani products compete in international markets.

He directed all PCSIR laboratories to obtain accreditation in accordance with international standards to facilitate internationally-recognised certification and validation of Pakistani export products.

The prime minister also called for stronger cooperation between the PCSIR and the National Vocational and Technical Train­ing Commission (NAVTTC) to improve industrial and technical training opportunities for young people. He sought the report of the third-party validation conducted on the institution.

The prime minister constituted a committee to review the PCSIR’s mandate, performance and future role. The committee will examine the institution’s original objectives, legal responsibilities, achievements and untapped potential, and recommend measures to improve its contribution to the national economy, industrial development and exports.

The meeting was informed that the PCSIR operates 10 research laboratories and units across the country, along with seven technical training institutes, while 12 additional laboratories are nearing completion.

The institution provides industries with modern technologies, research facilities and affordable technical solutions aimed at improving productivity and product quality.

Officials informed the meeting that the PCSIR had provided technical training to more than 12,000 young people. Its research and development activities cover a wide range of sectors, including food, agriculture, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, textiles, leather, minerals, engineering and energy.

The briefing further highlighted that PCSIR laboratories provide domestic industries and exporters with facilities for product testing, quality verification and calibration of technical instruments.

Published in Dawn, November 28th, 2026

World.title: Courts yet to settle if men can be prosecuted over ‘marital rape’: report
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan removed the marital rape exception from its criminal law two decades ago, but the courts have yet to settle whether a husband can be prosecuted for raping his wife, according to a new report by the South Asian Movement for Accessing Justice (SAMAJ), a coalition of 26 organisations convened by Equality Now.

The report, Challenging the Marital Rape Exception in South Asia, led and authored by lawyer Sahar Bandial, reviewed the law in eight countries.

It noted that the Protection of Women (Criminal Law Amendment) Act, 2006 redefined rape under Section 375 of the Pakistan Penal Code without reference to marital status, so marital rape can in principle attract the same penalty as any other rape. Yet no reported superior court judgement has confirmed this.

Cases described in the media as marital rape convictions have mostly been brought under Section 377, which covers “unnatural offences”.

Sherry urges action against child marriages; says one in six women in Pakistan was married as a child

In August 2026, a special court in Lahore sentenced a man to ten years under Section 376 for raping his wife — a clear marital rape conviction, the report says, though only at trial level.

By contrast, a 2025 Lahore High Court ruling held that forced sex within an ongoing marriage was not rape, effectively reading the exception back into the law.

In November 2026, the same court dismissed a petition seeking directions for legislation on marital rape. Domestic violence laws offer only civil remedies.

Regionally, the Maldives is the only country to fully criminalise marital rape on par with other rape, following a 2021 amendment. Nepal and Bhutan criminalise it with far lighter penalties. India and Sri Lanka recognise it only where spouses are separated; Bangladesh exempts husbands whose wives are over 13, and Afghanistan has no applicable law.

The World Health Organisation estimates cited in the report put lifetime intimate partner violence in Pakistan at 24.8pc, below Afghanistan (50.9pc), Bangladesh (48.9pc) and India (29.9pc), though the figures do not isolate marital rape.

The report urges legislators to make consent within marriage explicit in law.

Child marriages

Meanwhile, in a statement on the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage, Senator Sherry Rehman called for stronger legal protections, effective enforcement and sustained efforts to address the social and economic factors driving child marriages.

The PPP leader stressed that the practice deprived girls of their childhood, education, dignity and fundamental human rights.

“One in six women in Pakistan was married as a child. Pakistan ranks sixth globally among countries with the highest number of child marriages, while more than 19 million women and girls in the country were married before the age of 18. Nearly 4.8m girls were married before the age of 15.

“Globally, around 650m women and girls have been married in childhood. These are not just statistics; they represent millions of lives shaped by lost opportunities, interrupted education and diminished choices,” she said in a statement issued here.

She noted that child marriages had become particularly prevalent in flood-affected areas, where families facing displacement, poverty, loss of livelihoods and insecurity increasingly viewed early marriage as a survival mechanism.

“When disasters push families deeper into poverty and insecurity, girls are often the first to bear the cost. Marriage cannot be a coping mechanism for economic hardship, displacement or climate-induced vulnerability.

“It further exposes girls to risks and deprives them of the opportunity to rebuild their lives through education and empowerment,” she said.

Senator Rehman said the legislation had strengthened the legal framework for accountability and protection, but laws alone could not deliver justice without effective implementation, institutional commitment and public awareness.

“Every girl has the right to learn, to make decisions about her own future, to grow up without fear and to live a safe and dignified life. We cannot protect our girls through legislation alone unless we confront the inequalities and economic pressures that make child marriage possible,” she said.

Published in Dawn, November 28th, 2026

World.title: JUI-F claims scores held amid protests
World.content:
PESHAWAR/LAHORE/QUETTA: The JUI-F held protests across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan and parts of Punjab on Friday against the alleged detention of its chief, Maulana Fazlur Rehman, even as police denied that the party leader had been taken into custody.

Meanwhile, police continued to round up dozens of party workers and registered cases against hundreds more across the country.

The party’s Malakand chapter claimed 38 of its workers had been detained, while JUI-F leaders in Shangla said their district emir and among several protesters were arrested on the Karakoram Highway at Bisham. The party has also alleged that several activists were arrested and booked across Punjab during Thursday’s protests.

In Balochistan, JUI-F provincial spokesperson Dilawar Khan Kakar said lawmakers, local office-bearers and workers had been arrested in Quetta, Chaman, Kalat, Surab, Dera Bugti, Hub and other districts. He said the party’s provincial emir, Senator Maulana Abdul Wasay, and Opposition Leader in the Balochistan Assembly Mir Younas Aziz Zehri had been placed under house arrest.

Those held include former party candidate Usman Pirakani in Quetta, and district chairman Haji Amanullah Achakzai, district emir Maulana Abdul Mannan and information secretary Abdul Waris in Chaman. Several workers were also arrested in Kalat, among them Syed Huzaifa Shah, brother of the party’s provincial general secretary.

In Peshawar, 12 of the 16 leaders named in an FIR for blocking the M-1 Motorway are said to be in custody. Protests or attempted demonstrations were also reported in Charsadda, Bajaur, Shangla, Lower Dir, Malakand and Chitral, and near the Chashma checkpost, where police booked 19 leaders and 200 workers for blocking a road despite a ban on gatherings. Also, 32 workers were arrested from Chakdara Bridge, while police detained the party emirs of Lower and Upper Chitral.

In Quetta, a rally led by JUI-F district emir Maulana Abdul Rehman Rafiq set off from the party’s district office and passed through Jinnah Road, Qandahari Bazaar, Shara-e-Iqbal and Meezan Chowk before ending in a public meeting at Manan Chowk. Speakers from the JUI-F and other parties condemned the arrests, accused the authorities of suppressing political dissent, and said the party would continue its peaceful, constitutional struggle.

In Sargodha, meanwhile, seven activists were arrested on Friday, days after more than two dozen local leaders were taken in. Police sealed the entry points to Sargodha and kept watch on party leaders and seminaries in Sahiwal and Pakpattan.

In a message to workers in Lahore, the Maulana said the protest would continue and that arrests would not block their way, adding that the party leadership would decide the next step. He claimed he had been arrested.

Lahore police chief Bilal Siddique Kamyana denied this. “We did not arrest the JUI-F chief,” he told Dawn, adding that Fazl had been stuck in traffic when reports of his arrest surfaced and had since been allowed to return to his Lahore residence.

The CCPO said the JUI-F chief’s movement had not been restricted, and that since he had withdrawn his protest call there was no reason to arrest him.

Published in Dawn, November 28th, 2026

World.title: PR man booked for transporting dogs in train’s power van in Lahore
World.content:
LAHORE: During checking at Raiwind Railway Station, the railway police’ special branch staff recovered on Friday two dogs being transported illegally, without booking, in the Allama Iqbal Express (9-Up) power van.

According to officials, the train’s power plant operator, Mohammad Khan, allegedly charged Rs5,000 for transporting the dogs from Karachi, without booking them under the prescribed railway procedure.

The animals were reportedly to be handed over to a person at Kot Lakhpat Railway Station.

The police initiated legal proceedings against the operator, registering a case against him for violating railway regulations.

The dogs were subsequently booked, and a fine of Rs7,690 was deposited into the railway’s account, officials said.
